北京香山论坛多国代表对军用人工智能的潜在风险深表担忧。在美中两国准备举行高层会晤之际，武器自主化正急剧压缩决策时间，大国在此类技术管控上的分歧再度引发广泛讨论。
在欧盟释放信号，表示愿意让加拿大以“准成员”身份成为其特殊伙伴后，美国总统特朗普对此发出嘲讽，并表示，这一设想属于“敌对行为”。
周一，中共为前总书记江泽民举行百岁冥诞纪念大会。周二，前总理朱镕基的遗体在八宝山公墓火化，天安门等地降半旗致哀。江泽民与朱镕基留给习近平怎样的遗产？习近平能否借助已经逝去的时代安抚当下的民心，进一步巩固自己的权力？
最新民调显示，针对近期年轻人发起抗议活动，大部分德国民众对其诉求表示理解。绝大多数受访者认为，德国政界并未充分重视年轻一代的关切。
10月30日，刚刚与欧盟领导人进行会谈的加拿大总理卡尼接受了德国之声专访。他表示，加拿大对美国的依赖度过高，现在亟需深化与志同道合国家的多样化伙伴关系。
德国总理默茨在首尔与韩国总统李在明共同举行了联合新闻发布会，默茨表示，两国关系将提升至“深层战略伙伴关系”的水平。他说，在全球动荡时期，“我们现在加深伙伴关系是理所应当”。

title: 加國領袖及佩洛西促放黃之鋒 40團體譴責判刑
summary: 香港知名民主活動人士黃之鋒於2019年9月11日在德國柏林出席記者會。(Carsten Koall /Getty Images) 【大紀元2026年11月06日訊】（大紀元記者王蘭報導）加拿大參議院反對黨領袖及保守黨參議員胡薩科斯（Leo Housakos）和美國眾議院前議長佩洛西（Nancy Pelosi）發表聲明，敦促中共釋放被重判10年監禁的前香港眾志祕書長黃之鋒。與此同時，已經有40個國際人權及民主組織發表聯合聲明，譴責中共將黃之鋒判監10年。 加拿大參議院反對黨領袖
content:
香港知名民主活動人士黃之鋒於2019年9月11日在德國柏林出席記者會。(Carsten Koall /Getty Images)
【大紀元2026年11月06日訊】（大紀元記者王蘭報導）加拿大參議院反對黨領袖及保守黨參議員胡薩科斯（Leo Housakos）和美國眾議院前議長佩洛西（Nancy Pelosi）發表聲明，敦促中共釋放被重判10年監禁的前香港眾志祕書長黃之鋒。與此同時，已經有40個國際人權及民主組織發表聯合聲明，譴責中共將黃之鋒判監10年。
加拿大參議院反對黨領袖胡薩科斯11月5日在社交平台X上發文表示：「黃之鋒是因捍衛自由和人權而被監禁，這根本談不上公義。加拿大及其盟友必須一致地發聲，敦促（中共）立即釋放他。」
加拿大參議院反對黨領袖胡薩科斯資料照。（官方照片）
前香港眾志祕書長黃之鋒11月5日遭香港高等法院依《香港國安法》，以「串謀勾結外國或者境外勢力危害國家安全罪」重判10年監禁。
美國眾議院前議長佩洛西在官方國會網站發表聲明，形容香港法院另判黃之鋒監禁10年，是「令人震驚的濫用權力」。
美國眾議員南希‧佩洛西（加州民主黨）於2026年5月29日在加州舊金山舉行的「動員投票」集會上發表演說。(Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images)
佩洛西11月5日在聲明中說，黃之鋒已經被關押近6年，原本距離出獄回家只剩兩個月，如今卻面臨被監禁至2036年的命運。
「黃之鋒自十幾歲起，便一直與香港人民站在一起，支持他們爭取自由的抗爭。儘管法官表示，這項判刑旨在起到殺一儆百的作用，但顯而易見，黃之鋒所樹立的榜樣，其影響力將遠遠超過任何監禁刑期。
「美國及國際社會必須要求立即、無條件釋放黃之鋒。北京方面正寄望於黃之鋒及其他因捍衛香港自由而被囚禁的人士會相信沒有人在乎他們，沒有人願意為他們發聲。
「我們絕不會忘記黃之鋒、黎智英以及其他政治犯，並將繼續為他們發聲，直到他們重獲自由為止。」
英國人權活動家與記者貝內迪克特‧羅傑斯（Benedict Rogers）在X上發文說，「得知我的朋友黃之鋒再被判處10年監禁，我感到心碎，也深感憤慨。黃之鋒過去6年來，已經在獄中度過超過2,100天。他不應再多坐一天牢。」
英國人權活動家與記者貝內迪克特‧羅傑斯的帖文。(X)
40個國際人權及民主組織發表聯合聲明，強烈譴責香港高等法院於11月5日判處香港民主倡議人士黃之鋒監禁10年。
聲明中說，這是黃之鋒第二次因北京強加的《香港國安法》（NSL）被判刑。該法律已導致香港基本自由迅速倒退。
聲明表示，黃之鋒三週前在獄中度過30歲生日。他年少時便嶄露頭角，是學生組織「學民思潮」的共同創辦人，該組織反對在香港學校引入親北京的政治宣傳。
黃之鋒曾協助領導2014年具有歷史意義的「雨傘運動」，並於2016年創立民主派政黨「香港眾志」。2020年《香港國安法》獲通過後，該政黨被迫解散。
黃之鋒因推動民主運動獲得國際肯定，曾多次獲提名角逐諾貝爾和平獎。他多次遭到監禁，自2020年11月起一直被拘留。
聲明強調，這是中共一系列令人擔憂的行動之一，顯示中共不僅試圖限制和控制中國公民及香港居民可以與誰會面，還企圖干預外國政府官員可以接觸哪些人士，以及可以獲取什麼資訊。
聲明呼籲香港當局立即、無條件釋放黃之鋒，並要求各民主國家政府更強硬地要求香港當局釋放他。
具體而言，聲明要求白宮及美國國務院承諾，在11月於深圳舉行的亞太經濟合作組織（APEC）峰會，以及12月在佛羅里達州舉行的二十國集團（G20）峰會上，美國總統川普（特朗普）與中共黨魁習近平雙邊會談中，提出黃之鋒案件並要求釋放他。
聲明表示，川普政府在推動釋放世界各地政治犯方面，已作出值得肯定的努力。今年稍早，中共當局釋放了被拘押的政治犯、錫安教會牧師金明日（Ezra Jin Mingri），便證明美國總統直接介入，能夠帶來實質且攸關生命的重要改變。
有五個加拿大團體參與這份聯署，包括多倫多支聯會（Toronto Association for Democracy in China）、溫哥華支聯會（Vancouver Society in Support of Democratic Movement）、港加聯（Canada-Hong Kong Link）、蒙特利爾自由香港行動 （Action Free Hong Kong Montreal），以及華倫堡人權中心（Raoul Wallenberg Centre for Human Rights）。

summary: Skip to news navigation, settings and search Posted Thu 5 Nov 2026 at 4:22pmThu 5 Nov 2026 at 4:22pmThu 5 Nov 2026 at 4:22pm 许多因参与亲民主抗议活动而入狱的抗议者现已获释。 (ABC News: Brant Cumming) 2019年，Kris（化名）参加香港的大规模游行时从未想过这会让自己入狱，甚至断送职业生涯。 Kris是一大批因参与“暴动”而遭
content:
Skip to news navigation, settings and search
Posted Thu 5 Nov 2026 at 4:22pmThu 5 Nov 2026 at 4:22pmThu 5 Nov 2026 at 4:22pm
许多因参与亲民主抗议活动而入狱的抗议者现已获释。 (ABC News: Brant Cumming)
2019年，Kris（化名）参加香港的大规模游行时从未想过这会让自己入狱，甚至断送职业生涯。
Kris是一大批因参与“暴动”而遭起诉的人之一。当时的“反送中”修例草案，允许香港把刑事案嫌疑人移交至与香港没有现行引渡协议的地方，包括中国内地。
“我并不是罪犯，我没有犯罪。我因为我的良知参加反送中运动，一直是很和平，在现场帮助有需要的人。”Kris说。
Kris因担心人身安全，也要求ABC不要透露其性别和职业。
“在狱中，我一路憧憬着出来后要重新过新生活，加上其他朋友的鼓励，觉得自己过去澳洲也是一个可行的方法，”Kris说。
Kris在服刑近三年后获释，但重建生活之路并不顺利。
“出狱后，希望过回正常生活，自由到其他国家旅游，可以去外国读书，想法也很简单，”Kris说。
“我申请了[执业执照]的续牌，但至今仍未有结果。说实话，我已经做好最坏的打算。”
倡议团体候鸟（Waiting Bird ）的创办人Brandon Yau告诉澳大利亚广播公司（ABC），“反送中”运动结束后，香港通过了《国家安全法》，部分专业团体也对有刑事定罪纪录的从业者收紧了规定。
他说，这包括决定他们能否注册或继续获得执业执照，从事本职专业。
香港许多专业都要求从业者符合“适当适合人选”（fit and proper）标准，评核时可能会考虑个人品格和刑事犯罪纪录。
ABC就此联系了香港社会工作者注册局（Social Workers Registration Board）和香港律师会（Law Society of Hong Kong），征询评论。
香港护士管理局（Hong Kong Nursing Council）告诉ABC，对于有刑事定罪纪录的护士，该局有酌情权决定是否采取纪律行动，包括永久或暂时将其从注册名册中除名。
现年30多的Kris，希望在澳大利亚“重新开始”生活，并于2025年提交了学生签证申请。
“我在香港的刑事纪录，出国遇到困难，”Kris说。
"这样一路等待让我很难去计划将来……觉得是一个没有完结日期的惩罚。"
澳大利亚签证申请人必须通过品格审查，其中会考虑申请人的刑事案底等因素。
如果申请人有着“重大刑事记录”，包括被判处12个月或以上监禁，就可能无法通过审查。
香港警方表示，自2019年以来，已有超过一万人因与这些街头抗议活动有关而遭拘捕。 (Reuters: Tyrone Siu)
根据澳大利亚《1958年移民法》，像Kris这样的申请，很可能会被转交内政部下属的专门单位——签证申请人品格审议组（Visa Applicant Character Consideration Unit，简称VACCU）处理。
墨尔本移民律师詹姆斯·沃德洛（James Wardlaw）表示，申请人必须如实申报相关刑事纪录，这可能触发VACCU进一步评估。
他说，该单位积压案件数量庞大，有些案件要等上数年。
联邦内政部发言人告诉ABC，该部门注意到全球形势的发展，VACCU会根据个案具体情况进行评审，处理时间取决于每名申请人的具体情况。
沃德洛律师认为，大部分这类香港申请人不会对澳大利亚社会构成威胁。 (Supplied)
沃德洛先生目前代表多名向澳大利亚申请庇护的香港居民。
他说，在申请澳大利亚签证的亲民主活跃人士中，大部分人面对的指控都带有政治动机，申请人不会对澳大利亚社区构成威胁。
沃德洛先生补充说，他注意到，因示威相关罪名被定罪的香港申请人，包括申请旅游签证和学生签证的人，都遇到了长时间的延误。
香港当局表示，2019年示威期间共有逾一万人被捕，截至2026年6月30日，其中逾2400人已被裁定各项罪名成立。
澳大利亚外交与贸易部（DFAT）发言人表示，澳大利亚仍然密切关注香港权利与自由受到侵蚀，并已公开表达有关关切。
今年2月，澳大利亚国际人权事务特使马克·德赖弗斯（Mark Dreyfus）在联合国人权理事会上重申了这些关切。
2019年和2020年，香港爆发了多轮街头抗议活动；这些抗议最初源于对一项拟议引渡法案的反对。 (Reuters: Tyrone Siu)
香港特区政府在回应ABC的提问时，否定了这些批评，并称堪培拉“虚伪”。
香港特区政府表示：“香港是一个以法治为基础的社会，一直秉持‘有法必依、违法必究’的原则。”
“所有被告人都会依照适用于香港的法律（包括《香港国安法》）接受公平审判，并受《基本法》和《香港人权法案条例》保障。”
澳大利亚政府于2022年推出了“技术移民独立签证（189类别）”的香港专属途径，为符合资格的香港申请人提供获得永久居留权的渠道。
据内政部数据，2022年3月至2026年8月期间，该途径共批出1804张签证。
内政部数据还显示，截至2026年8月的六个月内，约有47宗香港居民的境内保护签证申请获批。

content:
图像加注文字，黄之锋自24岁被还押，刚在10月于狱中渡过30岁生日。
香港民主派活动人士黄之锋被控告中国《香港国安法》下的“串谋勾结外国势力危害国家安全”罪，星期四（11月5日）于香港高等法院被判囚10年。
上个月刚满30岁的黄之锋，自2020年底起因不同案件入狱，至今身在狱中超过六年。
他正就“民主派初选47人案”服刑，原有望于2027年1月获释。新增的10年刑期，其中2个月2日与“47人案”同期执行；预料他须服刑到2036年，出狱时或已年届40岁。
这是继壹传媒创办人黎智英后，第二宗在香港被起诉“勾结外国势力”罪的案件，也是黄之锋第二宗涉及《香港国安法》相关的案件。港府表示欢迎法庭的重判。
国际特赦组织批评，当局在黄之锋原定刑期获释前数月才新增定罪，“手法残酷”。有法律学者分析，案件反映国安法控罪或可被“反复动用”，令特定政治犯持续留在狱中。
英国外交部回覆BBC中文查询时称，最新判决说明《香港国安法》被用于针对行使政治表达权利的人。
图像加注文字，案情指，黄之锋在《国安法》生效前已展开“国际线”，多次参与国际游说要求外国制裁香港、中国。
此文包含Google YouTube提供的内容。由于这些内容会使用曲奇或小甜饼等科技，我们在加载任何内容前会寻求您的认可。 您可能在给与许可前愿意阅读Google YouTube小甜饼政策和隐私政策。 希望阅读上述内容，请点击“接受并继续”。
BBC中文记者现场所见，在正式宣判前，黄之锋到庭。
黄之锋身穿深蓝色长袖裇衫及卡其色长裤、戴黑框眼镜，较以往瘦削，面有须根，出庭时向旁听席点头，没有微笑，他不时细望旁听席的人士，然后微微点头打招呼。有旁听人士轮流进场换人，与黄之锋短暂打招呼后离去。
正庭公众席全满，旁听者包括：戴着黑色口罩的学民思潮前成员钱诗文、社运人士雷玉莲、前社民连成员黄浩铭、前民阵召集人陈皓桓、“47人案”获释者岑子杰，以及多国领事人员。
主审法官谭耀豪在判刑前，先交代判刑理由。在宣读判刑理由时，黄之锋戴着耳机不时手记笔记。最终判囚10年，黄之锋闻讯后平静低头。
有旁听人士向黄之锋挥手，并说“等你出来”，钱诗文与友人相拥哭泣；散庭后，有旁听人士一向走上前欲与黄之锋握手，被黄叫停。
香港民主党前创党成员、社运人士曾健成（阿牛）在判决后对BBC中文说，在《国安法》下看不到轻判，黄之锋如今要到40岁才得到自由，他感到相当难过、无奈，并反问“人生有多少个十年”。他隔空向黄之锋喊话：“辛苦你了之锋，顶住，希望你捱得过。”
图像加注文字，公众人士排队进入高等法院旁听黄之锋涉国安案件判刑，现场有多名警员戒备。
根据《香港国安法》，量刑分为两级，“勾结”罪可囚3年以上至10年以下，“罪行重大”者可判囚10年以上至无期徒刑。
法庭强调，国安法不具追溯力，被告被定罪基于法例实施后的行为；惟量刑时可将法例生效前的行为及活动作为其犯案背景的一部分来考虑，以评估罪行的严重性及程度。
早前一辩方资深大律师陈政龙在书面陈词中提出，本案不属“罪行重大”。辩方指，黄之锋并不回避本案属非常严重罪行的事实，但请法庭不要裁定本案为“罪行重大”。
辩方律师提出，黄之锋在国安法生效参与串谋的程度有限，角色属次要；与黎智英案比较本案情节较轻，涉及的外国政府、人物及平台内容也有实质分别。
另外，辩方也望法庭考虑黄之锋在最早期已认罪、连同其他案件已羁押近6年；他的个人背景品格、检控延近5年、整体刑期原则等。
辩方望法庭以低一级、接近 10 年监禁作为量刑起点来判决。
被告与其有联系的人士透过社交媒体帐户，经由西方主流新闻媒体或机构继续传播相关呼吁，涵盖本地及国际受众；
被告与罗冠聪等人在国安法实施后，刻意调整各自的角色，同样关键；被告知悉罗冠聪持续在海外呼吁的行为，并发布讯息和文章声援；
二人曾促成外国及外国实体实施制裁和不利措施，在当时地缘政治的氛围下，他们持续呼吁有可能令该等制裁及不利措施得以落实；
针对量刑起点，辩方曾提出参考吕世瑜、马俊文和黎智英案。
法官则认为黄之锋与罗冠聪在本案与黎智英相似，均站在最前线，是主谋，情节严重。综合本案所有情况，以13年监禁作为量刑起点，基于被告人的认罪答辩和求情，将量刑起点下调 3 年，判处监禁 10 年；即《国安法》第二十九条下属“罪行重大”所须判处的最低刑期。
黄之锋正就“民主派初选47人案”服刑，原有望于2027年1月获释。新增的10年刑期，其中2个月2日与“47人案”同期执行。
美国乔治城大学亚洲法律中心（Georgetown Center for Asian Law）高级研究员黎恩灏分析，从技术层面而言，若无新控罪，黄之锋原本望于明年初获释，故新增控罪客观上提供方式，“令黄之锋在更长时间无法重返公众视野”。
他表示，案件程序令人忧虑，一方面反映香港政府急于把刑事检控武器化，若政府认为有需要，国安法控罪便可以被“反复动用”，令特定政治犯持续留在狱中。
另一方面，控方就此案提出多项指控均涉及国安法生效前的行为，政府不惜牺牲正当程序原则，以追溯方式将政治犯的行为刑事化。
国际特赦组织亚太区副总监白舒然（Sarah Brooks）表示，最新的国安定罪，在黄之锋原定刑期获释前数月降临，形容“手法残酷，甚至可能是蓄意为之”，又指判刑提醒香港的《国安法》已沦为惩罚异见的工具，而非真正保障国家安全的手段。
她呼吁香港当局撤销黄之锋的定罪，并废除或修订所有违反香港国际人权义务的法例。
民间组织“香港监察”（Hong Kong Watch）亦表示，香港政府应立即无条件释放黄之锋。
英国外交部一位发言人对BBC中文称：“对黄之锋的判决清楚地表明，《国家安全法》正被用于针对因政治表达和参与而行使权利的个人。”
“我们呼吁立即停止所有针对根据《国家安全法》被起诉人士的不公正检控，并敦促中国及香港当局履行1984年《中英联合声明》所保障的香港民众应享有的权利与自由。”
图像加注文字，前学民思潮成员钱诗文及Louis旁听后离开。
香港警务处国安处总警司李桂华表示，欢迎法庭“重判黄之锋”，形容刑期合适，但会再与律政司商讨有否进一步行动。
李桂华表示，黄之锋未成年已经参与社运，18岁开始涉及不同罪行，包括触犯两项国安法、2019年6月包围警总及藐视法庭个案，形容他是“犯案纍纍”，“连法庭都不放在眼内”。他称，希望黄之锋反省对国家及香港做过的错事，培养守法精神及认识国家。
被问到案情背景为何涉及2016年事件、案发于2020年却延至2025年才起诉，李桂华引述法官指，2016年的资料对案件背景有作用，在2023年才根据报调查案件，两年后律政司指示送上法院，“时间合适，并没有任何拖延”。
有媒体引述黄之锋的求情信，指被捕时曾被执法人员称为“敌人”，李桂华回应称，他个人并没有将其视为“敌人”。
被问到Netflix仍上架黄之锋纪录片是否合法、能否在香港播放，李桂华表示，关注片中是否涉及煽动性内容，目前不能公开讨论。
行政长官李家超则形容，黄之锋、罗冠聪等人“是破坏香港繁荣稳定其中的祸首”，在《香港国安法》实施后“仍毫无悔改之意，肆无忌惮地继续充当外国和境外势力的代理人”，“祸港卖港、怙恶不悛”。
特区政府发言人表示，法庭对黄之锋予以重判，“彻底打破危害国家安全分子披着所谓‘国际线’或‘国际倡议’外衣便能逃避法律追责的幻想”；法庭判刑时详列理由，体现了黄之锋“是在公平公开的司法程序下被判刑”。
中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆表示，中国中央政府坚定支持香港，依法维护国安。“有关方面应切实尊重中国主权，尊重香港法制，停止就特区司法案件审理发表不负责任的言论，干预香港司法，干涉中国内政。”
前学民思潮成员Louis Lee在判刑前表示，希望黄之锋能尽快获释，早日与家人、朋友会面，“过一个他so called本来的生活”。他表示，上月底曾到监狱探望黄之锋，其“状态OK”，对世界有好奇，期待收到朋友的信件，但也担心刑期。
旁听人士、家庭主妇黄小姐对BBC中文说，她早于周二下午已到法院外排队。
她身穿写有“在颓垣中创造希望”字样的上衣，表示自己“看着黄之锋成长”，“十几岁已经振振有词，很有自己想法、有香港的大局观……他会为香港未来、人权、学运行一条很艰难的路，甚至有机会令自己身陷囹圄。”
她称，不敢预期结果，仅望可公平公开审讯。“无论什么结果都好，香港人愿意一起承担和承受，不应只是政治犯去承担罪名。”
宣判后，黄小姐表示“无罪就是一天冤狱都不应该坐”，又说希望大家除了流泪，还能保持希望和坚强。
图像加注文字，家庭主妇黄小姐手持旁听筹号，她早于周二下午已到法院外排队。
图像加注文字，社运人士雷玉莲等人亦有排队旁听，她举着“金心”以及“黄之锋”名字的纸张，表达支持。
本地媒体《法庭线》取得黄之锋的中英文版本求情信，两份信函内容有所差异。
在英文的求情信中，黄之锋表示，在原定出狱日期不足六个月之际面对判刑，“那种感觉几乎仿佛又回到了起点。”
他重申，其政治参与从来不是出于仇恨，对中国政府或香港政府并无怨恨；从未主张香港独立、鼓吹“中国崩溃”（collapse of China）或政权更替，亦从未接受任何外国资金资助，或花费金钱聘请外国政治顾问。
黄之锋提及选择认罪，也无意为其行为寻找藉口。他称，在国安法实施后，已意识直接倡议制裁属违法，故立即停止相关言论及行为；惟当时认为转载他人帖文，或呼吁外国企业基于其自身商业判断停止向香港警方供货，与直接倡议制裁有所不同，后来才明白判断错误。
Play video, "前學民思潮成員與黃之鋒的隔空對話", 节目全长 2,15
Play video, "黃之鋒給「前戰友」的信", 节目全长 2,55
根据《香港国安法》，“勾结”罪可囚3年以上至10年以下，“罪行重大”者可判囚10年以上至无期徒刑。
控罪指，黄之锋于2020年7月1日至2020年11月23日，在香港与罗冠聪及其他身分不详的人一同串谋，请求外国或境外机构、组织、人员，对香港或中国进行制裁、封锁或采取其他敌对行动。
控方案情指，黄之锋与“香港众志”创党主席罗冠聪早在2016年达成串谋，透过国际游说（international lobbying）达到“民主自决”主张。
案情指二人在《香港国安法》生效前已展开“国际线”，要求外国制裁香港、中国，包括多次参与国际游说，并出席欧洲议会人权小组委员会。二人在美国期间又会晤当地政要，如时任美国众议院少数党领袖佩洛西（Nancy Pelosi，裴洛西）、时任参议员卢比奥（Marco Rubio，鲁比奥／鲁比欧）等。二人被指推动《香港人权与民主法案》。
该法案于2019年11月27日生效，授权美国政府可制裁侵害香港人权的个人与组织，并要求美国国务院每年审查香港是否仍拥有足够自治、符合获得贸易特殊地位的资格。
除实体会面外，案情指黄之锋与罗冠聪曾推动多个国际联署，要求外国制裁港府并就国安法施压，包括要求美国等停止向香港警察供应装备。美国于2019年10月至11月通过法案，限制向香港供应催泪弹或人群管制相关技术的装备。
《香港国安法》于2020年6月30日深夜生效，“香港众志”同日解散及停止运作，罗冠聪离港。
案情指，二人在《香港国安法》生效后没改变共同目的（common intention），继续参与“国际线” 。其中黄之锋在 Facebook 发帖表示不会删除旧帖文、不会放弃其政治立场和意见、不会放弃打“国际线”，并会继续寻求国际社会支持。
2025年6月6日早上，黄之锋在赤柱监狱被捕。他于2026年9月2日认罪。
辩方陈政龙资深大律师求情时指，黄之锋自24岁开始还押，在狱中近六年间，已充分反思其行为和路向。辩方又指，黄于狱中并无浪费时间。他阅读超过100本书籍，又持正面的态度，期望有一天获释后可以照顾年迈家人。
香港“47人案”前议员胡志伟获准如常逗留英国 向BBC中文谈伦敦机场风波2026年7月28日
10月份刚满30岁的黄之锋，人生过半时间都在投身香港社运。
2011年，香港政府正打算在中小学推行“国民教育”政策，计划将“德育及国民教育科”设定为必修课。只有14岁的黄之锋与其他中学生自发成立香港首个中学生政团“学民思潮”。
2012年，他发起“反国教运动”，组织约12万人在香港政府总部外集会，最终成功迫使政府暂时搁置政策。
“反国教运动”成功之后，他并未沉寂下来。2014年，黄之锋与其他学运领袖在雨伞运动前夕，号召示威者冲入俗称“公民广场”的香港政府总部东翼前地，触发雨伞运动。当年，他登上美国《时代》杂志亚洲版的封面，标题为“抗争的面孔”，他亦被选为全球25位最具影响力的少年。
2016年，学民思潮停运。黄之锋20岁，与罗冠聪等人成立政党“香港众志”。黄担任该政党的秘书长。此举标志着他从学运领袖转型成为政治人物。
2019年区议会选举，黄之锋计划参选，但因其“鼓吹或推动民主自决”被指选举提名无效。2020年，反修例运动爆发后，黄之锋参与民主派初选，在九龙东以高票数“出线”，随后宣布参与当年的立法会选举，但参选资格及后被取消。
在2020年中国颁布《香港国安法》前夕，黄之锋及多名香港众志成员辞任职务，该政党亦宣告解散。
在北京当局眼中，黄之锋长期以来被视为是“反中乱港”分子。据报，国务院港澳办主任夏宝龙亦曾在2021年出席研讨会时，点名黎智英、戴耀廷、黄之锋为“反中乱港分子当中的极端恶劣者”。
被指涉案的罗冠聪于《国安法》生效前离开香港，目前获英国政治庇护。
2023年7月，罗冠聪被香港国安警察以涉嫌“煽动分裂国家罪”及“勾结外国或者境外势力危害国家安全罪”，悬红100万港元（12.76万美元；85.75万元人民币；403.68万元新台币）通缉。

content:
台湾将关闭巴布亚新几内亚办事处，归咎于中国压力 - 日经亚洲
台湾将关闭巴布亚新几内亚办事处，指责中国压力
自巴布亚新几内亚七月份宣布决定关闭以来，代表团一直保持开放状态
2018 年 11 月，巴布亚新几内亚莫尔兹比港一条中国修建的主干道前飘扬着中国国旗。© 路透社
2026 年 11 月 6 日 21:02 日本标准时间
台北（路透社）——台湾周五表示，已决定关闭在巴布亚新几内亚的代表处，并停止从该国购买液化天然气，并将其归咎于中国的压力。
台湾外交部表示，1999年与台湾短暂建立外交关系的巴布亚新几内亚重申了之前的要求，要求员工在规定的期限内离开莫尔兹比港的办公室，并敦促关闭该办公室。
外交部在一份声明中补充说，巴布亚新几内亚的行为“反映出中国持续利用政治压力和经济影响力干涉其他国家的外交决策，打压台湾的国际空间”。
今年7月，巴布亚新几内亚外长表示决定立即关闭台湾代表处，此举赢得了中国的赞扬和华盛顿的关注。不过，该办公室在此期间仍保持开放。
太平洋地区长期以来一直是中国和台湾之间的外交竞争地区，北京将台湾视为自己的领土，无权拥有国家的装饰。台湾政府拒绝接受这一立场。
巴布亚新几内亚和中国外交部均未立即回应置评请求。
台湾仅与三个太平洋岛国建立了正式外交关系：帕劳、图瓦卢和马绍尔群岛。它还在斐济设有代表处。只有12个国家与台湾保持正式外交关系。
台湾外交部还表示，已停止通过现货市场从巴布亚新几内亚购买液化天然气，原计划2026年上半年采购约50万吨。
台湾未来不会与台湾签署任何新的现货天然气采购合同。
台湾外交部表示，长期以来，台湾一直是巴布亚新几内亚天然气出口的重要市场，其采购量约占液化天然气出口总量的三分之一。
“因此采购政策的这一变化将对巴布亚新几内亚的天然气出口和外汇收入产生实质性影响，”它补充道。

Taiwan to close Papua New Guinea office, blames Chinese pressure - Nikkei Asia
Taiwan to close Papua New Guinea office, blames Chinese pressure
Mission had stayed open since PNG announced decision to shutter it in July
A Chinese flag flies in front of a Chinese-built main road in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, in November 2018. © Reuters
November 6, 2026 21:02 JST
TAIPEI (Reuters) -- Taiwan said on Friday it had decided to shut its representative office in Papua New Guinea and stop buying liquefied natural gas from the country, blaming Chinese pressure.
Taiwan's foreign ministry said Papua New Guinea, which briefly had diplomatic relations with Taiwan in 1999, had repeated previous demands that staff leave its office in Port Moresby within a set deadline and had pushed for its closure.
Papua New Guinea's actions "reflect China's continued use of political pressure and economic influence to interfere in other countries' diplomatic decisions and suppress Taiwan's international space," the foreign ministry added in a statement.
In July, Papua New Guinea's foreign minister said it had decided to close Taiwan's representative office immediately, winning praise from China and concern from Washington. The office had, however, remained open in the interim.
The Pacific has long been an area for diplomatic competition between China and Taiwan, which Beijing views as its own territory with no right to the trappings of a state. Taiwan's government rejects that position.
Neither the Papua New Guinea nor Chinese foreign ministries immediately responded to requests for comment.
Taiwan has formal diplomatic ties with only three Pacific Islands nations: Palau, Tuvalu and the Marshall Islands. It also has a representative office in Fiji. Just 12 countries maintain formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan.
Taiwan's foreign ministry also said it had stopped buying LNG from Papua New Guinea through the spot market, which in the first half of 2026 was planned for about 500,000 metric tons.
Taiwan will not sign any new spot natural gas purchase contracts with the country in the future, it added.
Taiwan has long been an important market for Papua New Guinea's natural gas exports, with purchases accounting for roughly a third of total LNG exports, its foreign ministry said.
"So this change in procurement policy will have a substantive impact on Papua New Guinea's natural gas exports and foreign exchange earnings," it added.

content:
特朗普-习近平-普京峰会可能意味着什么——以及它不会意味着什么 |政治新闻|半岛电视台
特朗普-习近平-普京峰会在社交媒体上可能意味着什么，以及它不会意味着什么
中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普参观中国北京的天坛 [文件：Brendan Smialowski/Pool/Getty]
本月在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会期间，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京可能会举行前所未有的三方会晤。
中国外交部发言人毛宁周三在北京对记者表示：“中方正在就三位国家元首会晤事宜与有关方面进行沟通。”
list 1 of 4特朗普在会见普京特使后表示俄罗斯与乌克兰的协议即将达成
list 2 of 4伊朗安全负责人会见普京，传达哈梅内伊的信息
list 3 of 4为什么伊朗免除印度、中国、卡塔尔、伊拉克的霍尔木兹限制？
4位美国法官中的4位禁止在华盛顿特区修建特朗普凯旋门
克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫周二表示，“协调此类会议的工作正在进行中”，并补充道：“我们希望会议能在未来几天内敲定。”
特朗普表示，他对围绕核武器问题进行的三方谈判持开放态度。 “如果习主席想要它，我就会拥有它，”他上个月告诉记者。
三位领导人曾分别会面，但从未一起举行过正式会谈。
那么，原定于 11 月 18 日至 19 日举行的会议是否真的会举行？这对世界其他地区意味着什么？这是我们所知道的：
俄罗斯将从与美国和中国的三方会谈中得到什么？
至少，有一个拍照的机会。
“这是一件大事，”莫斯科记者兼政治分析家亚历山大·布拉特斯基 (Alexander Bratersky) 告诉半岛电视台。
他提到了俄罗斯议会外交事务委员会主席彼得·托尔斯泰，他表示，托尔斯泰将这次会议描述为通向新雅尔塔的道路——1945年的会议上，苏联、美国和英国领导人塑造了欧洲的战后秩序。
布拉特斯基表示，这使得莫斯科能够“大言不惭”，同时将乌克兰置于一边。
他补充说，只要在谈判桌上，普京就可以成为“平等中的第一人”，这给了他一个拍照的机会，向世界展示他将成为乌克兰战争后决定欧洲安全架构未来的人之一。
他说，如果这次会议取得成果，这将体现中国对俄罗斯的影响力。
布拉特斯基说：“我们应该考虑到，我们面对的是选举后实力大大削弱的美国领导人。”
他解释说，特朗普仍然负责外交政策，但如果在本周中期选举中赢得国会两院控制权的民主党开始向基辅汇款，他的影响力将会减弱。
“会议本身就会取得成功，”他说。 “普京将能够在国内出售它”。
布拉特斯基表示，这次会议可能会在 12 月于迈阿密举行的 20 国集团 (G20) 峰会期间举行另一次会议，而这次会议可能会在一个月左右的时间内揭晓。
他补充道，如果圣诞节前没有任何成果，“那将只是拍照而已。”
伦敦大学圣乔治市国际政治学教授因德吉特·帕尔玛告诉半岛电视台，特朗普想要“一场个人的、戏剧性的会面”，让他声称自己正在按照自己的方式与另外两个大国“打交道”。

What a Trump-Xi-Putin summit could mean – and what it wouldn’t | Politics News | Al Jazeera
Share What a Trump-Xi-Putin summit could mean – and what it wouldn’t on social media
China's President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump visit the Temple of Heaven in Beijing, China [File: Brendan Smialowski/Pool/Getty]
On the sidelines of this month’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, an unprecedented three-way meeting between United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin could take place.
“China is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state,” Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told reporters in Beijing on Wednesday.

“Work is under way to coordinate such a meeting,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday, adding: “We hope that it will be finalised in the coming days.”
Trump has said he is open to three-way talks focused on nuclear weapons. “If President Xi wants to have it, I’d have it,” he told reporters last month.
The three leaders have met separately but have never held formal talks together.
So could the meeting, pencilled in for November 18-19, actually happen, and what would it mean for the rest of the world? Here’s what we know:
What would Russia get out of a three-way meeting with the US and China?
At the very least, a photo opportunity.
“It is a big event,” Alexander Bratersky, a Moscow-based journalist and political analyst, told Al Jazeera.
He pointed to Pyotr Tolstoy, chairman of the Russian parliament’s foreign affairs committee, who he said has described the meeting as a path towards a new Yalta – the 1945 conference where the leaders of the Soviet Union, the US and the United Kingdom shaped the post-war order in Europe.
That allows Moscow to “talk big”, Bratersky said, while putting Ukraine on the sidelines.
Simply being at the table would make Putin “first among equals”, he added, giving him a photo opportunity to show the world that he will be among those deciding the future of Europe’s security architecture after the war in Ukraine.
If the meeting produced results, he said, it would reflect China’s influence on Russia.
“We should take into account that we are dealing with a much weaker US leader after elections,” Bratersky said.
Trump remains in charge of foreign policy, he explained, but will have less leverage if Democrats, who won control of both chambers of Congress in this week’s midterm elections, start sending money to Kyiv.
“A meeting by itself will be a success,” he said. “Putin will be able to sell it at home”.
Whether anything comes of it should become clear within a month or so, Bratersky said, and the meeting could lead to another during the Group of 20 (G20) summit in Miami in December.
If nothing is produced before Christmas, he added, “it will be just a photo op.”
Trump wants “a personal, high-drama encounter” that lets him claim he is “dealing with” the other two great powers on his own terms, Inderjeet Parmar, a professor of international politics at City St George’s, University of London, told Al Jazeera.
A three-way meeting would allow Trump to present himself as “the indispensable deal-maker”, Parmar said, talking up potential deals on Ukraine, trade, energy or arms control.
“After the midterms the domestic political need for a foreign policy ‘win’ is real,” he said.
Any image of Trump sitting with Xi and Putin could be spun as evidence that American power still commands the table, he said, “even if the substance is limited or largely symbolic”.
“The domestic audience, and his eroding MAGA base, matters at least as much as the diplomatic one,” Parmar said.
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said he raised the idea of discussing Ukraine with Xi when they met in Beijing on October 30, and could see the “surprise” on his face, Germany’s DPA news agency reported.
Steinmeier told public broadcaster ARD that Xi said the three presidents would probably meet in Shenzhen, but not to discuss Ukraine.
He said Xi explicitly pointed out that the Russia-Ukraine war is a European conflict in which the “Europeans must sit at the table”.
Beijing is also likely to swat away Trump’s push for nuclear talks.
Last month, China’s Foreign Ministry said it would be “neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage”.
What would a meeting mean for the rest of the world?
Allies could be sidelined.
Parmar said a three-way meeting would mark “a clear break from the post-1945 pattern”, in which Washington coordinated closely with its European and Asian allies before engaging with Moscow or Beijing.
“A free-standing trilateral [meeting] risks treating those allies as secondary players whose interests can be managed after the fact,” he said, adding that those interests could even be traded.
That would be a shift towards “personalised great-power diplomacy”, he said. But the Trump administration still has hopes to drive a wedge between Russia and China, Parmar added.
Fears of a “G3” are “understandable but overstated in institutional terms”, he said, because the three capitals’ interests diverge sharply on Ukraine, Taiwan, technology and the rules of the international economy.
“The real risk is not a formal G3 secretariat, but the normalisation of great-power deals struck with little consultation of those most affected,” he said.
“History offers many examples of such moments. They rarely produce stable order and often leave the excluded feeling the costs,” Parmar said.

42 CFR Parts 413, 416, 419, 427, and 488
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
Final rule with comment period.
This final rule with comment period revises the Medicare Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and the Medicare Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) payment system for calendar year 2027 based on our continuing experience with these systems. We also describe the changes to the amounts and factors used to determine the payment rates for Medicare services paid under the OPPS and those paid under the ASC payment systems. In addition, this final rule with comment period updates and refines the requirements for the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and the Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Program. There are no changes to the Rural Emergency Hospital Quality Reporting Program. We finalized the expansion of the prior authorization requirement to include additional Botulinum Toxin Injection services. We also finalized implementation of certain provisions of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, for off-campus outpatient departments of a provider. In addition, this final rule with comment period announces notices of closure of teaching hospitals and opportunities to apply for available slots. Additionally, we finalized the policy that hospital accrediting organizations (AOs) with deeming authority may assess compliance with certain Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) administrative requirements under 42 CFR 489.20 during accreditation and reaccreditation surveys.

I. Summary and Background
A. Executive Summary of This Document
In this final rule with comment period, we are updating the payment policies and payment rates for services furnished to Medicare beneficiaries in hospital outpatient departments (HOPDs) and ambulatory surgical centers (ASCs), beginning January 1, 2027. Section 1833(t) of the Social Security Act (the Act) requires us to annually review and update the payment rates for services payable under the Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS). Specifically, section 1833(t)(9)(A) of the Act requires the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services (the Secretary) to review certain components of the OPPS not less often than annually, and to revise the groups, the relative payment weights, and the wage and other adjustments to take into account changes in medical practice, changes in technology, and the addition of new services, new cost data, and other relevant information and factors. In addition, under section 1833(i)(2)(D)(v) of the Act, we annually review and update the ASC payment rates. This final rule with comment period also includes additional policy changes made in accordance with our experience with the OPPS and the ASC payment system and recent changes in our statutory authority. We describe these and various other statutory authorities in the relevant sections of this final rule with comment period. In addition, this final rule with comment period announces the closure of a teaching hospital and the opportunity to apply for available slots. In addition, this final rule with comment period updates and refines requirements for the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and the Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Program. There are no changes to the Rural Emergency Hospital Quality Reporting Program. We finalized the expansion of the prior authorization requirement to include additional Botulinum Toxin Injection services. This final rule with comment period also includes changes to implement certain provisions of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, for off-campus outpatient departments of a provider. Additionally, we are finalizing a policy that hospital ( printed page 70286) accreditation organizations (AOs) with deeming authority may assess compliance with certain EMTALA administrative requirements under 42 CFR 489.20 during accreditation and reaccreditation surveys.
2. Summary of the Major Provisions
OPPS Update: For CY 2027, we are increasing the payment rates under the OPPS by an outpatient department (OPD) fee schedule increase factor of 2.3 percent. This increase factor is based on the inpatient hospital market basket percentage increase of 3.2 percent for inpatient services paid under the hospital inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS), reduced by the productivity adjustment of 0.9 percentage point. Based on this update, we estimate that total payments to OPPS providers (including beneficiary cost sharing and estimated changes in enrollment, utilization, and case mix) for calendar year (CY) 2027 will be approximately $114.4 billion, an increase of approximately $11 billion compared to estimated CY 2026 OPPS payments.
We are continuing to implement the statutory 2.0 percentage point reduction in payments for hospitals that fail to meet the hospital outpatient quality reporting requirements by applying a reporting factor of 0.9804 to the OPPS payments and copayments for all applicable services. Under the final 340B remedy offset, payments for services at hospitals subject to the 340B remedy offset will be reduced by 2.0 percentage points.
ASC Payment Update: For CYs 2019 through 2023, we adopted a policy to update the ASC payment system using the hospital market basket update. In light of the impact of the COVID-19 public health emergency (PHE) on healthcare utilization, we extended our policy to update the ASC payment system using the hospital market basket update an additional 2 years—through CYs 2024 and 2025. For CY 2026, we extended this interim period an additional year—through CY 2026. In this final rule, we are extending our utilization of the hospital market basket update as the update factor for the ASC payment system for one additional year (through CY 2027). Using the hospital market basket update, for CY 2027, we are increasing payment rates under the ASC payment system by 2.3 percent for ASCs that meet the quality reporting requirements under the ASCQR Program. This increase is based on a hospital market basket percentage increase of 3.2 percent reduced by a final productivity adjustment of 0.9 percentage point. Based on this update, we estimate that total payments to ASCs (including beneficiary cost sharing and estimated changes in enrollment, utilization, and case-mix) for CY 2027 will be approximately $9.9 billion, an increase of approximately $560 million compared to estimated CY 2026 Medicare payments.
Adjustment for Cost-of-Living in Alaska and Hawaii: For CY 2027, we are establishing a cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for outpatient hospital services provided in Alaska and Hawaii that applies the same COLA factors as finalized in the FY 2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule for FY 2027 for hospitals located in these States.
Device Pass-Through Payment Applications: For CY 2027, we received 19 complete applications for device pass-through payments. We sought public comment on 13 applications (six applicants withdrew) and are approving device pass-through payment status for nine applications. We are also denying device pass-through payment status for four applications in this final rule with comment period.
Changes to the List of ASC Covered Surgical Procedures and Ancillary Services Lists: For CY 2027, we are continuing to expand the ASC covered procedures list (CPL) by adding 618 codes to the ASC CPL that were recommended by interested parties or were finalized for removal from the IPO list for CY 2027.
Changes to the Inpatient Only (IPO) List: We are continuing to phase out the IPO list by removing 637 services from the auditory, digestive, endocrine, female genital, hemic and lymphatic systems, integumentary, male genital, maternity care and delivery, mediastinum and diaphragm, respiratory and urinary clinical families from the IPO list for CY 2027.
Cross-Program Updates for the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting and Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Programs: We are removing the Appropriate Follow-Up Interval for Normal Colonoscopy in Average Risk Patients measure from the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting and Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Programs.
Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program: In addition to finalizing the cross-program proposal to remove the Appropriate Follow-Up Interval for Normal Colonoscopy in Average Risk Patients measure, we are updating and refining validation and validation reconsideration procedures, including policies applicable to electronic clinical quality measures (eCQMs).
Rural Emergency Hospital Quality Reporting Program: We are not making any updates to the Rural Emergency Hospital Quality Reporting Program in this final rule with comment period.
Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Program: We are finalizing the cross-program measure proposal to remove the Appropriate Follow-Up Interval for Normal Colonoscopy in Average Risk Patients measure.
Expansion of Category for Hospital Outpatient Department Prior Authorization Process: We added Botulinum Toxin Injection codes to the existing category of services subject to the Hospital Outpatient Department prior authorization process for dates of service on or after July 1, 2027.
Partial Hospitalization and Intensive Outpatient Programs: We are updating the Partial Hospitalization Program (PHP) and Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) payment rates for CY 2027 using the methodology we finalized in CY 2026.
Payment Adjustment for 340B-Acquired Drugs Based on Results of the Medicare OPPS Drug Acquisition Cost Survey: Section 1833(t)(14)(D)(ii) of the Act requires the Secretary to periodically conduct surveys of hospital acquisition costs for each specified covered outpatient drug for use in setting the payment rates for such drugs. Additionally, on April 18, 2025, President Trump signed Executive Order (E.O.) 14273, “Lowering Drug Prices by Once Again Putting Americans First”. Section 5 of the E.O., “Appropriately Accounting for Acquisition Costs of Drugs in Medicare”, which directs the Secretary of HHS to publish in the Federal Register a plan to conduct a survey under section 1833(t)(14)(D)(ii) of the Act so he can determine the hospital acquisition cost for covered outpatient drugs at hospital outpatient departments. Accordingly, from January 1, 2026 through April 7, 2026, we conducted a survey of the acquisition costs for each separately payable drug acquired by all hospitals paid under the OPPS. Taking the survey results into account, for CY 2027 we are paying ASP minus 28 percent for 340B acquired drugs. Statute requires that this policy be implemented in a budget neutral manner, so this will increase OPPS payments for non-drug services by an equivalent amount, which is estimated to be a 7.50 percent increase to non-drug service payments for this final rule with comment period.
Prospective Adjustment to Payments for Non-Drug Items and Services to Offset the Increased Payments for Non-Drug Items and ( printed page 70287) Services Made in CY 2018 Through CY 2022 as a Result of the 340B Payment Policy: The Remedy for the 340B-Acquired Drug Payment Policy for Calendar Years 2018-2022 (88 FR 77150) codified an annual 0.5 percent reduction in the OPPS conversion factor applicable to non-drug items and services, excluding hospitals that enrolled in Medicare after January 1, 2018, until we estimated that the reduction had fully offset the additional $7.8 billion in non-drug services payments made as part of the prior 340B drug payment policy. This reduction was effective January 1, 2026. For CY 2027, we are increasing the annual percent reduction to the OPPS conversion factor used to determine the payment amounts for non-drug items and services for hospitals for whom this adjustment applies from 0.5 percent to 2 percent.
Method to Control Unnecessary Increases in the Volume of Outpatient Services Furnished in Excepted Off-Campus Provider-Based Departments (PBDs): For CY 2027, we are using our authority under section 1833(t)(2)(F) of the Act to apply the Physician Fee Schedule equivalent rate for any Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) codes assigned to the imaging without contrast APCs when provided at an off-campus PBD excepted from section 1833(t)(21) of the Act. We will exempt rural Sole Community Hospitals from this method to control the unnecessary volume of imaging without contrast services.
Payment for Software as a Medical Service (SaMS): Recently, there have been rapid developments in the use of software-based technologies to diagnose disease and support clinical decision-making in outpatient and physician office settings. For CY 2027, we are finalizing terminology for this group of services to be designated as Software as a Medical Service (SaMS) for Medicare payment purposes. As an interim policy as we continue to consider a longer-term payment methodology for this group of services, we are finalizing assignment of SaMS technologies to new technology APCs with payment rates that closely align with current CY 2026 payment rates. We are finalizing the creation of new status indicator (SI) “O1” (Software as a Medical Service, paid under OPPS; separate APC payment) and assigning the relevant HCPCS codes to this new (SI).
Similarly, for CY 2027, we are moving payment for stand-alone algorithmic analyses performed on data from prior laboratory tests, such as secondary genomic sequencing analyses, from the Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule (CLFS) as “diagnostic laboratory tests” to the OPPS as “other diagnostic tests” as provided in section 1861(s)(3) of the Act.
3. Summary of Costs and Benefits
In section XXVI. of this final rule with comment period, we provide a detailed analysis of the regulatory and Federalism impacts that the changes will have on affected entities and beneficiaries. Key estimated impacts are described below.
a. Impacts of all OPPS Changes
Table 112 in section XXVI.C. of this final rule with comment period displays the distributional impact of all the OPPS changes on various groups of hospitals and CMHCs for CY 2027 compared to all estimated OPPS payments in CY 2026. We estimate that the finalized policies in this final rule with comment period will result in a 1.7 percent increase in OPPS payments to providers for services. We estimate that total OPPS payments for CY 2027, including beneficiary cost-sharing, to the approximately 3,600 facilities paid under the OPPS (including general acute care hospitals, children's hospitals, cancer hospitals, and CMHCs) will increase by approximately $1.78 billion compared to CY 2026 payments due to the OPD update, excluding changes in enrollment, utilization, and case-mix. We estimated the isolated impact of our OPPS policies on CMHCs because CMHCs have historically only been paid for partial hospitalization services under the OPPS. Beginning CY 2024, they are also paid for IOP services under the OPPS. Based on our policy to calculate CMHC PHP and IOP costs based on 40 percent of the corresponding proposed hospital-based PHP and IOP costs, we estimate a 29.0 percent increase in CY 2027 payments to CMHCs relative to their CY 2026 payments.
b. Impacts of the Updated Wage Index
We estimate that our update of the wage indexes based on the fiscal year (FY) 2027 IPPS final rule wage indexes will result in no change for urban hospitals under the OPPS and a 0.3 percent increase for rural hospitals. These wage indexes include continued utilization of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) labor market area delineations based on 2020 Decennial Census data, with updates, as discussed in section II.C. of this final rule with comment period.
c. Impacts of the Rural Adjustment and the Cancer Hospital Payment Adjustment
For CY 2027, we will continue to provide additional payments to cancer hospitals so that a cancer hospital's payment-to-cost ratio (PCR) after the additional payments is equal to the weighted average PCR for the other OPPS hospitals using the most recently submitted or settled cost report data. Section 16002(b) of the 21st Century Cures Act requires that this weighted average PCR be reduced by 1.0 percentage point. For CY 2027, we are targeting PCR of 0.88 to determine the CY 2027 cancer hospital payment adjustment to be paid at cost report settlement. That is, the payment adjustments would be the additional payments needed to result in a PCR equal to 0.88 for each cancer hospital.
There are no significant impacts of our CY 2027 payment policies for hospitals that are eligible for the rural sole community hospital adjustment, as we are maintaining the current policy in the CY 2027 OPPS.
d. Impacts of the OPD Fee Schedule Increase Factor
For the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC, we are establishing an OPD fee schedule increase factor of 2.3 percent and applying that increase factor to the conversion factor for CY 2026. As a result of the OPD fee schedule increase factor and other budget neutrality adjustments, we estimate that urban hospitals will experience an increase in payments of 2.0 percent and that rural hospitals will experience an increase in payments of 5.6 percent. Classifying hospitals by teaching status, we estimate non-teaching hospitals will experience an increase in payments of 6.5 percent, minor teaching hospitals will experience an increase in payments of 3.5 percent, and major teaching hospitals will experience a decrease in payments of 2.0 percent. We also classified hospitals by the type of ownership. We estimate that hospitals with voluntary ownership will experience an increase of 2.1 percent in payments, while hospitals with government ownership will experience a decrease of 1.1 percent in payments. We estimate that hospitals with proprietary ownership will experience an increase of 10.5 percent in payments.
e. Impacts of the ASC Payment Update
For impact purposes, the surgical procedures on the ASC covered surgical procedure list are aggregated into surgical specialty groups using CPT and HCPCS code range definitions. The ( printed page 70288) percentage change in estimated total payments by specialty groups under the final CY 2027 payment rates, compared to estimated CY 2026 payment rates, ranges between an increase of 35 percent and a decrease of 5 percent.

Across 3,000 hospitals participating in the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program, we estimate that our finalized changes will reduce total information collection burden by 17,439 hours for a cost savings of $997,143 beginning with the CY 2029 reporting period/CY 2031 payment determination.

Across 5,149 ASCs participating in the Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Program, we estimate that our finalized changes will reduce total information collection burden by 16,753 hours for a cost savings of $957,937 beginning with the CY 2027 reporting period/CY 2029 payment determination.
B. Legislative and Regulatory Authority for the Hospital OPPS
When Title XVIII of the Act was enacted, Medicare payment for hospital outpatient services was based on hospital-specific costs. In an effort to ensure that Medicare and its beneficiaries pay appropriately for services and to encourage more efficient delivery of care, the Congress mandated replacement of the reasonable cost-based payment methodology with a prospective payment system (PPS). The Balanced Budget Act of 1997 (BBA) (Pub. L. 105-33) added section 1833(t) to the Act, authorizing implementation of a PPS for hospital outpatient services. The OPPS was first implemented for services furnished on or after August 1, 2000. Implementing regulations for the OPPS are located at 42 CFR parts 410 and 419.
The Medicare, Medicaid, and SCHIP Balanced Budget Refinement Act of 1999 (BBRA) (Pub. L. 106-113) made major changes in the hospital OPPS. Under the OPPS, we generally pay for hospital Part B services on a rate-per-service basis that varies according to the APC group to which the service is assigned. We use the Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) (which includes certain Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes) to identify and group the services within each APC. The OPPS includes payment for most hospital outpatient services, except those identified in section I.C. of this final rule with comment period. Section 1833(t)(1)(B) of the Act provides for payment under the OPPS for hospital outpatient services designated by the Secretary (which includes partial hospitalization services furnished by CMHCs), and certain inpatient hospital services that are paid under Medicare Part B.
The OPPS rate is an unadjusted national payment amount that includes the Medicare payment and the beneficiary copayment. This rate is divided into a labor-related amount and a nonlabor-related amount. The labor-related amount is adjusted for area wage differences using the hospital inpatient wage index value for the locality in which the hospital or CMHC is located.
All services and items within an APC group are comparable clinically and with respect to resource use, as required by section 1833(t)(2)(B) of the Act. In accordance with section 1833(t)(2)(B) of the Act, subject to certain exceptions, items and services within an APC group cannot be considered comparable with respect to the use of resources if the highest median cost (or mean cost, if elected by the Secretary) for an item or service in the APC group is more than 2 times greater than the lowest median cost (or mean cost, if elected by the Secretary) for an item or service within the same APC group (referred to as the “2 times rule”). In implementing this provision, we generally use the cost of the item or service assigned to an APC group.
For new technology items and services, special payments under the OPPS may be made in one of two ways. Section 1833(t)(6) of the Act provides for temporary additional payments, which we refer to as “transitional pass-through payments”, for at least 2 but not more than 3 years for certain drugs, biological agents, brachytherapy devices used for the treatment of cancer, and categories of other medical devices. For new technology services that are not eligible for transitional pass-through payments, and for which we lack sufficient clinical information and cost data to appropriately assign them to a clinical APC group, we have established special APC groups based on costs, which we refer to as New Technology APCs. These New Technology APCs are designated by cost bands which allow ( printed page 70289) us to provide appropriate and consistent payment for designated new procedures that are not yet reflected in our claims data. Similar to pass-through payments, an assignment to a New Technology APC is generally temporary; that is, we retain a service within a New Technology APC until we acquire sufficient data to assign it to a clinically appropriate APC group.
C. Excluded OPPS Services and Hospitals
Section 1833(t)(1)(B)(i) of the Act authorizes the Secretary to designate the hospital outpatient services that are paid under the OPPS. While most hospital outpatient services are payable under the OPPS, section 1833(t)(1)(B)(iv) of the Act excludes payment for ambulance, physical and occupational therapy, and speech-language pathology services, for which payment is made under a fee schedule. It also excludes screening mammography, diagnostic mammography, and effective January 1, 2011, an annual wellness visit providing personalized prevention plan services. The Secretary exercises the authority granted under the statute to also exclude from the OPPS certain services that are paid under fee schedules or other payment systems. Such excluded services include, for example, the professional services of physicians and nonphysician practitioners paid under the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS); certain laboratory services paid under the Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule (CLFS); services for beneficiaries with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) that are paid under the ESRD prospective payment system; and services and procedures that require an inpatient stay that are paid under the hospital IPPS. In addition, section 1833(t)(1)(B)(v) of the Act does not include applicable items and services (as defined in subparagraph (A) of paragraph (21)) that are furnished on or after January 1, 2017, by an off-campus outpatient department of a provider (as defined in subparagraph (B) of paragraph (21)). We set forth the services that are excluded from payment under the OPPS in regulations at 42 CFR 419.22.
Under § 419.20(b) of the regulations, we specify the types of hospitals that are excluded from payment under the OPPS. These excluded hospitals are:
Hospitals located in Maryland and paid under Maryland's All-Payer or Total Cost of Care Model;
Hospitals located outside of the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico;
Indian Health Service (IHS) hospitals; and
Rural emergency hospitals (REHs).
On April 7, 2000, we published in the Federal Register a final rule with comment period (65 FR 18434) to implement a prospective payment system for hospital outpatient services. The hospital OPPS was first implemented for services furnished on or after August 1, 2000. Section 1833(t)(9)(A) of the Act requires the Secretary to review certain components of the OPPS, not less often than annually, and to revise the groups, the relative payment weights, and the wage and other adjustments to take into account changes in medical practices, changes in technology, the addition of new services, new cost data, and other relevant information and factors.
Since initially implementing the OPPS, we have published final rules in the Federal Register annually to implement statutory requirements and changes arising from our continuing experience with this system. These rules can be viewed on the CMS website at https://www.cms.gov/​medicare/​payment/​prospective-payment-systems/​hospital-outpatient/​regulations-notices.
E. Advisory Panel on Hospital Outpatient Payment (the HOP Panel or the Panel)
1. Authority of the Panel
Section 1833(t)(9)(A) of the Act, as amended by section 201(h) of Public Law 106-113, and redesignated by section 202(a)(2) of Public Law 106-113, requires that we consult with an expert outside advisory panel composed of an appropriate selection of representatives of providers to annually review (and advise the Secretary concerning) the clinical integrity of the payment groups and their weights under the OPPS. In CY 2000, based on section 1833(t)(9)(A) of the Act, the Secretary established the Advisory Panel on Ambulatory Payment Classification Groups (APC Panel) to fulfill this requirement. In CY 2011, based on section 222 of the Public Health Service Act (the PHS Act), which gives discretionary authority to the Secretary to convene advisory councils and committees, the Secretary expanded the panel's scope to include the supervision of hospital outpatient therapeutic services in addition to the APC groups and weights. To reflect this new role of the panel, the Secretary changed the panel's name to the Advisory Panel on Hospital Outpatient Payment (the HOP Panel). The HOP Panel is not restricted to using data compiled by CMS, and in conducting its review, it may use data collected or developed by organizations outside the Department.
2. Establishment of the Panel
On November 21, 2000, the Secretary signed the initial charter establishing the Panel, and, at that time, named the APC Panel. This expert panel is composed of appropriate representatives of providers (currently employed full-time, not as consultants, in their respective areas of expertise) who review clinical data and advise CMS about the clinical integrity of the APC groups and their payment weights. Since CY 2012, the Panel also is charged with advising the Secretary on the appropriate level of supervision for individual hospital outpatient therapeutic services. The Panel is technical in nature, and it is governed by the provisions of the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA). The current charter specifies, among other requirements, that the Panel—
May advise on the clinical integrity of Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC) groups and their associated weights;
May advise on the appropriate supervision level for hospital outpatient services;
May advise on OPPS APC rates for ASC covered surgical procedures;
Is governed by the provisions of the FACA;
Has a Designated Federal Official (DFO); and
Is chaired by a Federal Official designated by the Secretary.
The Panel's charter was amended on November 15, 2011, renaming the Panel and expanding the Panel's authority to include supervision of hospital outpatient therapeutic services and to add critical access hospital (CAH) representation to its membership. The Panel's charter was also amended on November 6, 2014 (80 FR 23009), and the number of members was revised from up to 19 to up to 15 members. The Panel's current charter was approved on November 21, 2024, for a 2-year period.
The current Panel membership and other information pertaining to the Panel, including its charter, Federal Register notices, membership, meeting dates, agenda topics, and meeting reports, can be viewed on the CMS website at https://www.cms.gov/​Regulations-and-Guidance/​Guidance/​FACA/​AdvisoryPanelonAmbulatoryPaymentClassificationGroups.html. II. Updates Affecting OPPS Payments
A. Recalibration of APC Relative Payment Weights
a. Database Source and Methodology
Section 1833(t)(9)(A) of the Act requires that the Secretary review not less often than annually and revise the relative payment weights for Ambulatory Payment Classifications (APCs). In the April 7, 2000 OPPS final rule with comment period (65 FR 18482), we explained in detail how we calculated the relative payment weights for each APC group; this methodology was implemented on August 1, 2000.
For the CY 2027 OPPS, we proposed to recalibrate the APC relative payment weights for services furnished on or after January 1, 2027, and before January 1, 2028 (CY 2027), using CY 2025 claims data and the same basic methodology that we described in the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (90 FR 53455 through 53457). That is, we proposed to recalibrate the relative payment weights for each APC using a database constructed from claims and cost report data for hospital outpatient department (HOPD) services.
For the purpose of recalibrating the proposed APC relative payment weights for CY 2027, we began with approximately 147 million final action claims (claims for which all disputes and adjustments have been resolved and payment has been made) for HOPD services furnished on or after January 1, 2025 and before January 1, 2026, before applying our exclusionary criteria and other methodological adjustments. After the application of those data processing changes, we used approximately 74 million final action claims to develop the proposed CY 2027 OPPS payment weights (91 FR 41740). For exact numbers of claims used and additional details on the claims accounting process, we refer readers to the claims accounting narrative under “Downloads” for the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule on the CMS website at https://www.cms.gov/​medicare/​payment/​prospective-payment-systems/​hospital-outpatient/​regulations-notices.
Addendum N to the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule (which is available via the internet on the CMS website at https://www.cms.gov/​medicare/​payment/​prospective-payment-systems/​hospital-outpatient/​regulations-notices), includes the proposed list of bypass codes for CY 2027. Bypass codes allow the ratesetting process to use multiple-procedure claims to develop “pseudo” single claims, which are then used to develop OPPS payment rates. The proposed list of bypass codes contains codes that are reported on claims for services in CY 2025 and, therefore, includes codes that were in effect in CY 2025 and used for billing. We proposed to retain these deleted bypass codes on the proposed CY 2027 bypass list because these codes existed in CY 2025 and were covered HOPD services in that period, and CY 2025 claims data were used to calculate proposed CY 2027 payment rates (91 FR 41740). Keeping these deleted bypass codes on the bypass list potentially allows us to create more “pseudo” single procedure claims for ratesetting purposes. “Overlap bypass codes” that are members of the proposed multiple imaging composite APCs are identified by asterisks (*) in the third column of Addendum N to the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule. HCPCS codes that we proposed to add for CY 2027 are identified by asterisks (*) in the fourth column of Addendum N.
We did not receive any public comments on our general proposal to recalibrate the relative payment weights for each APC based on claims and cost report data for HOPD services or on our proposed bypass code process. We are finalizing as proposed the “pseudo” single claims process and the CY 2027 proposed list of bypass codes, finalized in Addendum N to this final rule with comment period (which is available via the internet on the CMS website). For this final rule with comment period, for the purpose of recalibrating the final APC relative payment weights for CY 2027, we used approximately 81 million final action claims (claims for which all disputes and adjustments have been resolved and payment has been made) for HOPD services furnished on or after January 1, 2025, and before January 1, 2026. For the exact numbers of claims used and additional details on the claims accounting process, we refer readers to the claims accounting narrative under supporting documentation for this final rule with comment period on the CMS website at https://www.cms.gov/​medicare/​payment/​prospective-payment-systems/​hospital-outpatient.
b. Calculation and Use of Cost-to-Charge Ratios (CCRs)
For CY 2027, we proposed to continue to use the hospital-specific overall ancillary and departmental cost-to-charge ratios (CCRs) to convert charges to estimated costs through application of a revenue code-to-cost center ( printed page 70291) crosswalk (91 FR 41740). To calculate the APC costs on which the proposed CY 2027 APC payment rates are based, we calculated hospital-specific departmental CCRs for each hospital for which we had CY 2025 claims data by comparing these claims data to the most recently available hospital cost reports, which, in most cases, are from CY 2024. For the proposed CY 2027 OPPS payment rates, we used the set of claims processed during CY 2025. We applied the hospital-specific CCR to the hospital's charges at the most detailed level possible, based on a revenue code-to-cost center crosswalk that contains a hierarchy of CCRs used to estimate costs from charges for each revenue code. To ensure the completeness of the revenue code-to-cost center crosswalk, we reviewed changes to the list of revenue codes for CY 2025 (the year of claims data we used to calculate the proposed CY 2027 OPPS payment rates) and updates to the National Uniform Billing Committee (NUBC) 2025 Data specifications Manual (91 FR 41740 through 41741). That crosswalk is available for review and continuous comment on the CMS website at https://www.cms.gov/​medicare/​payment/​prospective-payment-systems/​hospital-outpatient/​regulations-notices and included with every proposed and final OPPS rule.
In accordance with our longstanding policy, similar to our finalized policy for CY 2026 OPPS ratesetting, we proposed to calculate CCRs for the standard cost centers—cost centers with a predefined label—and nonstandard cost centers—cost centers defined by a hospital—accepted by the electronic cost report database. In general, the most detailed level at which we calculate CCRs is the hospital-specific departmental level.
While we generally view the use of additional cost data as improving our OPPS ratesetting process, we have historically not included cost report lines for certain nonstandard cost centers in the OPPS ratesetting database construction when hospitals have reported these nonstandard cost centers on cost report lines that do not correspond to the cost center number. We believe it is important to further investigate the accuracy of these cost report data before including such data in the ratesetting process. Further, we believe it is appropriate to gather additional information from the public as well before including the data in OPPS ratesetting. For CY 2027 and future years, we proposed not to include the nonstandard cost centers reported in this way in the OPPS ratesetting database construction (91 FR 41741).
We did not receive any public comments on the general CCR process, and therefore, we are finalizing our proposal for CY 2027 to continue to use the hospital-specific overall ancillary and departmental CCRs to convert charges to estimated costs through application of a revenue code-to-cost center crosswalk. We are also finalizing the proposed methodology regarding the treatment of nonstandard cost centers.

We note that under the OPPS, CY 2019 was the first year in which the claims data used for setting payment rates (CY 2017 data) contained lines with the modifier “PN,” which indicates nonexcepted items and services furnished and billed by off-campus provider-based departments (PBDs) of hospitals. a. Calculation of Single Procedure APC Criteria-Based Costs
Since the implementation of the OPPS in August 2000, we have made separate payments for blood and blood products through APCs rather than packaging payment for them into payments for the procedures with which they are administered. Hospital payments for the costs of blood and blood products, as well as for the costs of collecting, ( printed page 70292) processing, and storing blood and blood products, are made through the OPPS payments for specific blood product APCs.
We proposed to continue to establish payment rates for blood and blood products using our blood-specific CCR methodology (90 FR 53457), which utilizes actual or simulated CCRs from the most recently available hospital cost reports to convert hospital charges for blood and blood products to costs. This methodology has been our standard ratesetting methodology for blood and blood products since CY 2005. It was developed in response to data analysis indicating that there was a significant difference in CCRs for those hospitals with and without blood-specific cost centers and past public comments indicating that the former OPPS policy of defaulting to the overall hospital CCR for hospitals not reporting a blood-specific cost center often resulted in an underestimation of the true hospital costs for blood and blood products. To address the differences in CCRs and to better reflect hospitals' costs, our methodology simulates blood CCRs for each hospital that does not report a blood cost center by calculating the ratio of the blood-specific CCRs to hospitals' overall CCRs for those hospitals that do report costs and charges for blood cost centers and applies this mean ratio to the overall CCRs of hospitals not reporting costs and charges for blood cost centers on their cost reports. We proposed to calculate the costs upon which the proposed payment rates for blood and blood products are based using the actual blood-specific CCR for hospitals that reported costs and charges for a blood cost center and a hospital-specific, simulated, blood-specific CCR for hospitals that did not report costs and charges for a blood cost center.
We continue to believe that the hospital-specific, simulated, blood-specific CCR methodology takes into account the unique charging and cost accounting structure of each hospital, as it better responds to the absence of a blood-specific CCR for a hospital than alternative methodologies, such as defaulting to the overall hospital CCR or applying an average blood-specific CCR across hospitals. This methodology also yields more accurate estimated costs for these products and results in payment rates for blood and blood products that appropriately reflect the relative estimated costs of these products for hospitals without blood cost centers and for these blood products in general (91 FR 41742).
For a more detailed discussion of payments for blood and blood products through APCs, we refer readers to:
The CY 2005 OPPS proposed rule (69 FR 50524 and 50525) for a more comprehensive discussion of the blood-specific CCR methodology;
The CY 2008 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (72 FR 66807 through 66810) for a detailed history of the OPPS payment for blood and blood products; and
The CY 2015 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (79 FR 66795 and 66796) for additional discussion of our policy not to make separate payments for blood and blood products when they appear on the same claims as services assigned to a C-APC.
We received one public comment on these proposals. The following is a summary of the comment we received and our response.
Comment: A commenter supported CMS's proposal to continue to pay for blood and blood derived products in the HOPD rather than packaging the payment.
Response: We appreciate the commenter's support of our proposal.
After consideration of the public comment, we are finalizing our proposal to continue separate payment for blood and blood derived products in the HOPD for CY 2027.

Section 1833(t)(2)(H) of the Act mandates the creation of additional groups of covered OPD services that classify devices of brachytherapy—cancer treatment through solid source radioactive implants—consisting of a seed or seeds (or radioactive source) (“brachytherapy sources”) separately from other services or groups of services. The statute provides certain criteria for the additional groups. For the history of OPPS payment for brachytherapy sources, we refer readers to prior OPPS final rules, such as the CY 2013 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (77 FR 68240 and 68241). For purposes of setting payment rates, as we have stated in prior OPPS updates, we believe that adopting the general OPPS prospective payment methodology for brachytherapy sources is appropriate for several reasons (77 FR 68240). The general OPPS methodology uses costs based on claims data to set the relative payment weights for hospital outpatient services. This payment methodology results in more consistent, predictable, and equitable payment amounts per source across hospitals by averaging the extremely high and low values, in contrast to payment based on hospitals' charges adjusted to costs. We believe that the OPPS methodology, as opposed to payment based on hospitals' charges adjusted to cost, also would provide hospitals with incentives for efficiency in the provision of brachytherapy services to Medicare beneficiaries. Moreover, this approach is consistent with our payment methodology for most items and services paid under the OPPS. We refer readers to the CY 2016 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (80 FR 70323 through 70325) for further discussion of the history of OPPS payment for brachytherapy sources.
For CY 2027, except where otherwise indicated, we proposed to continue our policy and use the costs derived from CY 2025 claims data to set the proposed CY 2027 payment rates for brachytherapy sources because we proposed to use CY 2025 data to set the proposed payment rates for most other items and services that would be paid under the CY 2027 OPPS (91 FR 41742). With the exception of the proposed payment rates for brachytherapy sources A9527 (Iodine i-125, sodium iodide solution, therapeutic, per millicurie), C2636 (Brachytherapy linear source, non-stranded, palladium-103, per 1 mm), C2645 (Brachytherapy planar source, palladium-103, per square millimeter) and the proposed payment rates for low-volume brachytherapy APCs discussed in section III.D. of this final rule with comment period, we proposed to base the payment rates for brachytherapy sources on the geometric mean unit costs for each source, consistent with the methodology that we proposed for other items and services paid under the OPPS, as discussed in section II.A.2. of this final rule with comment period.
We also proposed for CY 2027 and subsequent years to continue the other payment policies for brachytherapy sources that we finalized and first implemented in the CY 2010 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (74 FR 60537). For CY 2027 and subsequent years, we proposed to pay for the stranded and nonstranded not otherwise specified (NOS) codes, HCPCS codes C2698 (Brachytherapy source, stranded, not otherwise specified, per source) and C2699 (Brachytherapy source, nonstranded, not otherwise specified, per source), at a rate equal to the lowest stranded or nonstranded prospective payment rate for such sources, ( printed page 70293) respectively, on a per-source basis (as opposed to, for example, per mCi), which is based on the policy we established in the CY 2008 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (72 FR 66785). For CY 2027 and subsequent years, we also proposed to continue the policy we implemented in the CY 2010 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (74 FR 60537) regarding payment for new brachytherapy sources for which we have no claims data, for the same reasons we discussed in the CY 2008 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (72 FR 66786, which was delayed until January 1, 2010, by section 142 of Pub. L. 110-275). Specifically, this policy is intended to enable us to assign new HCPCS codes for new brachytherapy sources to their own APCs, with prospective payment rates set based on our consideration of external data and other relevant information regarding the expected costs of the sources to hospitals. The proposed CY 2027 payment rates for brachytherapy sources are included in Addendum B to this proposed rule (which is available via the internet on the CMS website at https://www.cms.gov/​medicare/​payment/​prospective-payment-systems/​hospital-outpatient/​regulations-notices) and identified with status indicator “U (Brachytherapy Sources, Paid under OPPS; separate APC payment).”
For CY 2018, we assigned status indicator “U” to HCPCS code C2645 (Brachytherapy planar source, palladium-103, per square millimeter) in the absence of claims data and established a payment rate using external data (invoice price) at $4.69 per mm2 for the brachytherapy source's APC—APC 2648 (Brachytx planar, p-103) (82 FR 59233 through 59234). For CY 2019, in the absence of sufficient claims data, we continued to establish a payment rate for C2645 at $4.69 per mm2 for APC 2648 (Brachytx planar, p-103) (83 FR 58834 through 58836). Our CY 2018 claims data available for the CY 2020 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (84 FR 61142) included two claims with a geometric mean cost for HCPCS code C2645 of $1.02 per mm2 . In response to comments from interested parties, we agreed that, given the limited claims data available and a new outpatient indication for C2645, a payment rate for HCPCS code C2645 based on the geometric mean cost of $1.02 per mm2 may not adequately reflect the cost of HCPCS code C2645. In the CY 2020 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, we finalized our policy to use our equitable adjustment authority under section 1833(t)(2)(E) of the Act, which states that the Secretary shall establish, in a budget neutral manner, other adjustments as determined to be necessary to ensure equitable payments, to maintain the CY 2019 payment rate of $4.69 per mm2 for HCPCS code C2645 for CY 2020 (84 FR 61157 through 61158). Similarly, in the absence of sufficient claims data to establish an APC payment rate, in the CY 2021, CY 2022, CY 2023, CY 2024, CY 2025, and CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rules with comment period (85 FR 85879 through 85880, 86 FR 63469, 87 FR 71760 through 71761, 88 FR 81553, 89 FR 93925, and 90 FR 53458), we finalized our policy to use our equitable adjustment authority under section 1833(t)(2)(E) of the Act to maintain the CY 2019 payment rate of $4.69 per mm2 for HCPCS code C2645 for CYs 2021 through 2026.
There were no CY 2025 claims available that reported HCPCS code C2645 for the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule. Therefore, in the absence of claims data, we proposed to continue to use our equitable adjustment authority under section 1833(t)(2)(E) of the Act to maintain the CY 2026 payment rate of $4.69 per mm2 for HCPCS code C2645, which we proposed to be assigned to APC 2648 (Brachytx planar, p-103) for CY 2027 (91 FR 41743). Similarly, there were no CY 2025 claims available for the proposed rule that reported HCPCS A9527 (Iodine i-125, sodium iodide solution, therapeutic, per millicurie), which is assigned to APC 2632, or HCPCS code C2636 (Brachytherapy linear source, non-stranded, palladium-103, per 1 mm), which is assigned to APC 2636. While both APC 2632 and 2636 have historically been designated as Low Volume APCs, which uses up to 4 years of claims data, we are concerned that 4 years of historical claims data would only yield 2 claims for each APC, and that may not be reliable for ratesetting for these APCs for CY 2027. Therefore, we proposed to use our equitable adjustment authority under section 1833(t)(2)(E) of the Act, which states in part that the Secretary shall establish, in a budget neutral manner, other adjustments as determined to be necessary to ensure equitable payments, to maintain the CY 2026 payment rates for APC 2632 and APC 2636 for CY 2027. Specifically, for CY 2027, we proposed a payment rate of $396.32 per millicurie for APC 2632 and a payment rate of $89.40 per 1 mm for APC 2636 (91 FR 41743).
Additionally, for CY 2022 and subsequent calendar years, we adopted a Universal Low Volume APC policy for clinical and brachytherapy APCs. As discussed in further detail in section X.C. of the CY 2022 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (86 FR 63743 through 63747), we adopted this policy to mitigate wide variation in payment rates that occur from year to year for APCs with low utilization. Such volatility in payment rates from year to year can result in even lower utilization and potential barriers to access. Brachytherapy APCs that have fewer than 100 single claims used for ratesetting purposes are designated as Low Volume APCs unless an alternative payment rate is applied, such as the use of our equitable adjustment authority under section 1833(t)(2)(E) of the Act in the case of APCs 2632, 2636, and 2648 as detailed above.
For CY 2027, we proposed to designate five brachytherapy APCs as Low Volume APCs as these APCs met our criteria to be designated as Low Volume APCs (91 FR 41743).
We invited interested parties to submit recommendations for new codes to describe new brachytherapy sources. Such recommendations should be directed via email to outpatientpps@cms.hhs.gov.
