f. Supervised Visits for Esketamine Self- Administration (APCs 1513 and 1517)
On March 5, 2019, FDA approved SPRAVATO® (esketamine) nasal spray, used in conjunction with an oral antidepressant for treatment of depression in adults who have tried other antidepressant medicines but have not benefited from them (treatment-resistant depression (TRD)). This is the first FDA approval of esketamine for any use.
Esketamine is a noncompetitive N- methyl D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist. It is a nasal spray supplied as an aqueous solution of esketamine hydrochloride in a vial with a nasal spray device. Each device delivers two sprays containing a total of 28 mg of esketamine. Patients would require either two (2) devices (for a 56 mg dose) or three (3) devices (for an 84 mg dose) per treatment.
Because of the risk of serious adverse outcomes resulting from sedation and dissociation and respiratory depression caused by esketamine nasal spray administration, and the potential for abuse and misuse of the product, it is only available through a restricted distribution system under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). A REMS is a drug safety program that the FDA can require for certain medications with serious safety concerns to help ensure the benefits of the medication outweigh its risks. The SPRAVATO® REMS program requires, among other requirements, that the esketamine nasal spray be dispensed and administered to enrolled patients in health care settings that are certified in the REMS. See www.fda.gov for more information regarding the SPRAVATO® REMS program requirements.
A treatment session of esketamine consists of instructed nasal self- administration by the patient followed by a period of at least 2 hours post-administration observation of the patient under direct supervision of a health care professional in the certified health care setting. Refer to the CY 2020 PFS final rule and interim final rule for more information about supervised visits for esketamine nasal spray self- administration (84 FR 63102 through 63105); see also the SPRAVATO® REMS ( printed page 70375) document and SPRAVATO® labeling available on the FDA website.[19 20]
To facilitate prompt beneficiary access to the new, potentially life-saving treatment for TRD using esketamine, we created two new HCPCS G codes, G2082 ( Office or other outpatient visit for the evaluation and management of an established patient that requires the supervision of a physician or other qualified health care professional and provision of up to 56 mg of esketamine nasal self-administration, includes 2 hours post-administration observation) and G2083 ( Office or other outpatient visit for the evaluation and management of an established patient that requires the supervision of a physician or other qualified health care professional and provision of greater than 56 mg esketamine nasal self-administration, includes 2 hours post-administration observation), effective January 1, 2020. HCPCS code G2082 is for an outpatient visit for the evaluation and management of an established patient who requires the supervision of a physician or other qualified health care professional and provision of up to 56 mg of esketamine through nasal self-administration and includes two hours of post- administration observation. HCPCS code G2083 describes a similar service to HCPCS code G2082 but involves the administration of more than 56 mg of esketamine.
For CY 2026, HCPCS code G2082 was assigned to APC 1512 (New Technology—Level 12 ($1001-$1100)) with a payment rate of $1,050.50 and HCPCS code G2083 was assigned to APC 1518 (New Technology—Level 18 ($1601-$1700)) with a payment rate of $1,650.50.
For CY 2027, the OPPS payment rates were proposed based on available CY 2025 claims data as the available single frequency claims exceed the 100 claims threshold generally used for our universal low volume policy. Therefore, for CY 2027, we proposed to assign HCPCS codes G2082 and G2083 to New Technology APCs based on each of the codes' geometric mean costs. Specifically, we proposed to assign HCPCS code G2082 to APC 1513 New Technology—Level 13 ($1101-$1200) with a payment rate of $1,150.50 based on its geometric mean cost of $1,181 which was calculated using the available 742 single frequency claims from CY 2025 claims data. g. SAINT Neuromodulation System (APCs 1511 and 1525)
The SAINT Neuromodulation System is a non-invasive repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) system that identifies an individualized target and delivers navigationally directed repetitive magnetic pulses to that individualized target located within the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex to treat major depressive disorder (MDD). The patient first receives structural MRI and functional MRI scans that are analyzed by the provider to identify and localize the personalized stimulation target in the patient's dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Once the areas targeted for treatment are identified, the patient receives non-invasive magnetic stimulation in the targeted area. The patient has 10 treatment sessions per day with each treatment session lasting 10 minutes followed by 50 minutes of rest before another treatment session occurs. The treatment is administered over five days for a total of 50 sessions of non-invasive magnetic stimulation therapy. There are four CPT codes listed below that describe the MRI scans that are used to target the treatment and describe the administration of the non- invasive magnetic stimulation therapy.
0889T—Personalized target development for accelerated, repetitive high-dose functional connectivity MRI-guided theta-burst stimulation derived from a structural and resting-state functional MRI, including data preparation and transmission, generation of the target, motor threshold-starting location, neuronavigation files and target report, review and interpretation.
0890T—Accelerated, repetitive high-dose functional connectivity MRI-guided theta-burst stimulation, including target assessment, initial motor threshold determination, neuronavigation, delivery and management, initial treatment day.
0891T—Accelerated, repetitive high-dose functional connectivity MRI-guided theta-burst stimulation, including neuronavigation, delivery and management, subsequent treatment day.
0892T—Accelerated, repetitive high-dose functional connectivity MRI-guided theta-burst stimulation, including neuronavigation, delivery and management, subsequent motor threshold redetermination with delivery and management, per treatment day.

h. Skin Cell Suspension Autograft (SCSA) Procedures (CPT Codes 15006 Through 15009) (APC 1575)
Effective January 1, 2025, both CPT code 15013 (Preparation of skin cell suspension autograft, requiring enzymatic processing, manual mechanical disaggregation of skin cells, and filtration; first 25 sq cm or less of harvested skin) and HCPCS code C8002 (Preparation of skin cell suspension autograft, automated, including all enzymatic processing and device components (do not report with manual suspension preparation)) describe the preparation step of a skin cell suspension autograft (SCSA) procedure to treat acute thermal burn injuries. Both codes describe the preparation step of a three-step SCSA procedure: harvesting, preparation, and application. The difference between the codes is that CPT code 15013 describes the manual preparation of the SCSA, and HCPCS code C8002 describes the automated preparation of the SCSA. Due to the similarities between the procedures, in the CY 2025 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, we assigned both CPT code 15013 and HCPCS code C8002 to APC 1567 (New Technology—Level 30 ($6,001-$6,500)) with a payment rate of $6,250.50 and status indicator “T”. In the CY 2025 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, we noted that we believed the sum of the payment rates for the three-step process should approximate ( printed page 70378) $10,000. However, because of the effect of the multiple procedure reduction, the total payment for the skin cell suspension autograft furnished using the RECELL System would have been approximately $8,000, contrary to the intended target of $10,000 as stated in the CY 2025 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period. To correct this error, in the CY 2025 OPPS/ASC Correction Notice, we assigned both CPT code 15013 and HCPCS code C8002 to APC 1532 (New Technology—Level 32 ($7,001-$7,500)) with a payment rate of $7,250.50 and status indicator “S” (Procedure or service, not discounted when multiple, paid under OPPS; separate APC payment).
For CY 2026, the OPPS payment rates were based on available CY 2024 claims data. Since CPT code 15013 and HCPCS code C8002 were not effective until January 1, 2025, we did not have any claims for either code for CY 2024. Therefore, for CY 2026, we finalized to continue to assign CPT code 15013 and HCPCS code C8002 to APC 1532 (New Technology—Level 32 ($7,001-$7,500)) with a payment rate of $7,250.50 (91 FR 41801).

CPT 15007 (placeholder CPT code 15X20): each additional 100 sq cm, or each additional 1 percent of body area of infants and children, or part thereof (List separately in addition to code for primary procedure)

i. Renal Histotripsy Service (APC 1575)
HCPCS code C9790 (Histotripsy (ie, non-thermal ablation via acoustic energy delivery) of malignant renal tissue, including image guidance)) was created October 1, 2023, and was used to describe the Medicare approved Category B IDE (investigational device exemption) clinical study involving the renal histotripsy procedure associated with the use of the HistoSonics Edison System. CPT code 0888T (Histotripsy (ie, non-thermal ablation via acoustic energy delivery) of malignant renal tissue, including image guidance) replaced HCPCS code C9790 effective July 1, 2024.
Renal histotripsy is a non-invasive, non-thermal, mechanical process that uses a focused beam of sonic energy to destroy solid renal tumors and is currently in a prospective, multi-center, single-arm pivotal trial designed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of the device for the destruction of kidney tissue by treating primary solid renal tumors. Because the renal histotripsy clinical study is designated as a Category B (non-experimental/investigational) IDE study, the Medicare payment for CPT code 0888T reflects payment for both the service that is performed, and the device used each time it is reported on a claim. j. Implantable Glucose Monitoring System (APC 1563)
Effective January 1, 2017, the AMA CPT Editorial Panel established CPT codes 0446T ( Creation of subcutaneous pocket with insertion of implantable interstitial glucose sensor, including system activation and patient training) and 0448T ( Removal of implantable interstitial glucose sensor with creation of subcutaneous pocket at different anatomic site and insertion of new implantable sensor, including system activation) to describe an implantable glucose sensor for patients with diabetes. These codes were used to describe sensors with a 90-day or 180-day battery life. Although these CPT codes were effective January 1, 2017, the implantable interstitial glucose sensor did not receive FDA authorization for marketing until June 6, 2019.
For CY 2021, we assigned CPT codes 0446T and 0448T to APC 5054 (Level 4 Skin Procedures) and a status indicator of “T” (Procedure or Service, Multiple Procedure Reduction Applies; Paid under OPPS; separate APC payment.) and maintained those APC assignments until April 1, 2025.
In the CY 2025 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, we created the following two HCPCS G-codes effective January 1, 2025, to describe the implantable interstitial glucose sensor with a 365-day battery life.
G0546 (Creation of subcutaneous pocket with insertion of 365 day implantable interstitial glucose sensor, including system activation and patient training); and
G0565 (Removal of implantable interstitial glucose sensor with creation of subcutaneous pocket at different anatomic site and insertion of new 365 day implantable sensor, including system activation).
We assigned HCPCS codes G0564 and G0565 to APC 1561 (New Technology—Level 24 ($3001-$3500)) with a payment rate of $3,250.50.
For the April 1, 2025, quarterly update, we deleted HCPCS codes G0564 and G0565 and assigned 0446T and 0448T to APC 1561 (New Technology—Level 24 ($3001-$3500)) with a payment rate of $3,250.50 to describe the new implantable interstitial glucose sensor with a 365-day battery life. The 365-day glucose sensor replaced previous versions of the implantable interstitial glucose sensor with shorter battery lives. Therefore, the 365-day sensor is the only sensor on the market and can only be described by CPT codes 0446T and 0448T.
For CY 2026, we finalized maintaining the APC assignments for CPT codes 0446T and 0448T to APC 1561 (New Technology—Level 24 ($3001-$3500)) with a payment rate of $3,250.50. Because CPT codes 0446T and 0448T were assigned to New Technology APCs to describe this new sensor for the April 2025 quarterly update and the G-codes that described this service were only effective for one quarter, we did not have any claims data for the service (90 FR 53556).
For CY 2027, the OPPS payment rates were proposed based on available CY 2025 claims data. Both CPT codes 0446T and 0448T had less than 10 claims, so we proposed to maintain their current APC assignment to APC 1563 (New Technology—Level 26 ($4001-$4500)), status indicator of `T' and a payment rate of $4,250.50.
We received public comments on this proposal. The following is a summary of the comments we received and our responses.
Comment: Several commenters requested that we maintain the APC assignment for CPT codes 0446T and 0448T in a New Technology APC, stating continuous glucose monitoring is an important tool for diabetic patients, especially patients with transportation barriers, limited access to specialty care, and patients who may not be as compliant with follow-up visits. Maintaining the APC assignments, the commenters contended, would protect beneficiary access to this service while allowing CMS to gather claims data and get a better idea of the true costs of this service.
A commenter requested that CMS reassign CPT codes 0446T and 0448T to APC 1530 (New Technology—Level 30 ($6001-$6500)) with a payment of $6,250.50. The commenter cited the increased cost of the implanted 365-day glucose sensor as the reason for their request and the value of the longer sensor duration, including fewer insertion and removal procedures and better adherence to therapy. They explained that extensive research and development, along with high manufacturing costs, have contributed to the cost of the implantable continuous glucose monitoring system (iCGM system) which they state is $6,800. The commenter also requested that the OPPS payment align with the PFS payment which they state is approximately $5,800, to provide consistent payment regardless of the setting. The commenter notes that the utilization in other care settings has increased while usage in the hospital outpatient setting has been limited.
It was also noted that the continuous glucose monitoring system is under consideration for a Category I CPT code, which would allow the service to be valued through the CPT and RUC processes and support appropriate future reimbursement.
Response: We appreciate the public comment and understand the implicated value that a longer life sensor brings to Medicare beneficiaries. We agree that there would be inherently increased costs to hospitals for the new technology of a 365-day system, but as we stated last year, we do not agree that the costs to hospitals would be almost double the costs of the 180-day system. (90 FR 53556) We also remind the commenter that the OPPS pays for operational costs for hospital facilities, while the PFS pays for the professional ( printed page 70381) services. As such, we do not believe that the costs will always be aligned between the two fee schedules.
Since the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule was published, we note that there were no changes in claims data for CPT code 0446T, but CPT 0448T now has 10 single frequency claims in the 4-year lookback period and therefore is subject to our low volume policy. Using this claims data from CY 2025, our analysis found the arithmetic mean cost is $1,779, the median cost is $1,394, and the geometric mean cost is $1,278. Because the arithmetic mean cost is the statistical methodology that estimates the highest cost for the service, we would usually assign CPT 0448T to APC 1551 (New Technology—Level 14 ($1201-$1300)), status indicator of `T' and a payment of $1,250.50. However, we believe it is important to maintain both of these codes in their current APC assignments.
In summary, after consideration of the public comment we received, we are finalizing our proposal based on our statutory authority set out at section 1833(t)(2)(E) of the Act, to assign both CPT codes 0446T and 0448T to APC 1563 (New Technology—Level 26 ($4001-$4500)) with a payment of $4,250.50 and a status indicator of `T'.

k. Scalp Cooling Fitting CPT Code 97007 (APC 1516)
Scalp cooling is a service furnished during chemotherapy to prevent or minimize hair loss, a common side effect of chemotherapy treatment for cancer. Effective July 1, 2021, scalp cooling was described by CPT codes 0662T (Scalp cooling, mechanical; initial measurement and calibration of cap) and 0633T (Scalp cooling, mechanical; placement of device, monitoring, and removal of device (list separately in addition to code for primary procedure)).
However, effective January 1, 2026, CPT codes 0662T and 0663T were deleted and replaced by three Category I CPT codes:
97007—Mechanical scalp cooling, including individual cap supply with head measurement, fitting, and patient education.
97008—Mechanical scalp cooling; including hair preparation, individual cap placement, therapy initiation, and precooling period).
97009—Mechanical scalp cooling; provided after discontinuation of chemotherapy, each 30 minutes (List separately in addition to code for primary procedure).
CPT code 97007 describes the fitting and supply of the cap, which happens on a different date of service than a chemotherapy session, while CPT codes 97008 and 97009 describe the scalp cooling therapy on the same date of service as the chemotherapy session. For CY 2026, we assigned status indicator “N” to CPT codes 97008 and 97009 to align with our packaging policies generally, and specifically with regard to packaging of CPT code 0663T, which we believed served as a predecessor code for CPT codes 97008 and 97009 (90 FR 53597).
For CY 2027, we proposed to assign CPT code 97007 to APC 1516 (New Technology—Level 16 ($1401—$1500)) with a payment rate of $1,450.50 using the geometric mean cost of $1,425.11 based on 109 single frequency claims for the predecessor code, CPT code 0662T, that were available for the proposed rule. Additionally, we refer readers to section III.E. to this final rule for preamble on our final policy for CPT code 97008.
We received a public comment on our proposal for CPT code 97007. The following is a summary of the comment we received and our response.

Instead, the commenter asked that we use invoice data to assign CPT code 97007 to APC 1519 until there is reliable claims data upon which to base payment.

However, interested parties have indicated that there are substantial resource costs associated with calibrating and fitting the cap, which has informed payment policy for scalp cooling.

Because claims data is available here, we do not believe invoice pricing is the appropriate basis for setting the final payment rate for CPT code 97007, and we decline to adopt the commenter's suggested approach. D. Universal Low Volume APC Policy for Clinical and Brachytherapy APCs
In the CY 2022 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (86 FR 63743 through 63747), we adopted a policy to designate clinical and brachytherapy APCs as low volume APCs if they have fewer than 100 single claims that can be used for ratesetting purposes in the claims year used for ratesetting for the prospective year. For the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC proposed rule, CY 2024 claims were generally the claims used for ratesetting; and clinical and brachytherapy APCs with fewer than 100 single claims from CY 2024 that can be used for ratesetting would be low volume APCs subject to our universal low volume APC policy. As we stated in the CY 2022 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, we adopted this policy to reduce the volatility in the payment rate for those APCs with fewer than 100 single claims. Where a clinical or brachytherapy APC has fewer than 100 single claims that can be used for ratesetting, under our low volume APC payment adjustment policy, we determine the APC cost as the greatest of the geometric mean cost, arithmetic mean cost, or median cost based on up to 4 years of claims data. We excluded APC 5853 (Partial Hospitalization for CMHCs) and APC 5863 (Partial Hospitalization for Hospital-based PHPs) from our universal low volume APC policy given the different nature of policies that affect the partial hospitalization program. We also excluded APC 2698 (Brachytx, stranded, nos) and APC 2699 (Brachytx, non-stranded, nos) as our current methodology for determining payment rates for non-specified brachytherapy sources is appropriate.
Based on claims data available for the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule, we proposed to designate five brachytherapy APCs and four clinical APCs as low volume APCs under the OPPS. The five brachytherapy APCs and four clinical APCs meet our criteria of having fewer than 100 single claims in the claims' year used for ratesetting (CY 2025 for the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule). Nine of the 10 APCs were designated as low volume APCs in CY 2025. Based on data for the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule, APC 2645 (Brachytx, non-stranded, gold-198) had 87 single claims and met our criteria to be designated as a low volume APC (91 FR 41807).
Comment: Commenters supported our proposal to continue our low volume APC policy for CY 2027.
Response: We thank commenters for their support.
After consideration of the public comments received, based on CY 2025 claims data available for this final rule with comment period, we are finalizing our proposal to designate five brachytherapy APCs and four clinical APCs as low volume APCs under the OPPS. Table 28 includes the CY 2025 claims available for ratesetting for each of the APCs we are designating as low volume APCs for CY 2027. The final cost statistics for our CY 2027 low volume APCs, such as the median, arithmetic mean, and geometric mean cost are available for download with this final rule with comment period on the CMS website. We refer readers to our website at https://www.cms.gov/​medicare/​payment/​prospective-payment-systems/​hospital-outpatient/​regulations-notices; click on the relevant regulation to download the low volume APC cost statistics under the comprehensive (OPPS) ratesetting methodology in the downloads section of the web page.
1. Creation and/or Revisions of Clinical APCs
Neurostimulator and Related Procedures (APCs 5461 Through 5465)
In prior rulemaking, some interested parties have requested that we create a Level 6 Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC, due to their concerns around clinical and resource cost similarity in the Level 5 Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC. We most recently responded to this request in the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (90 FR 53584). We noted that we believed that the current 5 level APC structure for the Neurostimulator and Related Procedures series provided for an appropriate distribution of clinical and cost similarity at the different APC levels.
As discussed in the CY 2021 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, we reiterate that the OPPS is a prospective payment system. We group procedures with similar clinical characteristics and resource costs into APCs and establish a payment rate that reflects the geometric mean of all services in the group even though the cost of any individual service within the APC may be higher or lower than the APC's geometric mean. As a result, in the OPPS, any individual procedure may potentially be paid more or less than the cost of the services because the payment rate is based on the geometric mean of the entire group of services in the APC. However, the impact of these payment differences should be mitigated when distributed across a large number of APCs (85 FR 85968).
We continued to believe that a five-level structure for the Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC series remained appropriate, and therefore in the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule our proposed assignments for the structure and for many codes in the APC series remained the same as they were in the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule.
Comment: A commenter supported the assignment of CPT code 61885 (Insertion or replacement of cranial neurostimulator pulse generator or receiver, direct or inductive coupling; with connection to a single electrode array) to APC 5465. Commenters supported maintaining the assignment of CPT code 33276 (Insertion of phrenic nerve stimulator system (pulse generator and stimulating lead[s]), including vessel catheterization, all imaging guidance, and pulse generator initial analysis with diagnostic mode activation, when performed) to New Technology APC 1580. Other commenters supported our proposal to maintain the assignment of CPT code 64568 (Open implantation of cranial nerve ( e.g., vagus nerve) neurostimulator electrode array and pulse generator) to New Technology APC 1580.
Some commenters noted that the claims used in modeling the estimated costs for CPT code 64568 appeared to be restricting procedure pairings to HCPCS codes C1767 (Generator, neurostimulator (implantable), non-rechargeable) and C1778 (Lead, neurostimulator (implantable)) and requested that the customary methodology be applied when evaluating CPT code 64568. Commenters also requested that CMS remove hypoglossal nerve stimulation claims for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea from the determination of the geometric mean cost of CPT code 64568.
Response: We appreciate the commenters' support for the proposed assignments of CPT codes 33276 and 64568 to New Technology APC 1580, and of CPT code 61885 to APC 5465. We agree that it is appropriate to maintain the current temporary New Technology APC assignments for CPT codes 33276 and 64568. We will continue to monitor the claims data for the code as additional claims become available.
In reviewing the claims data for CPT code 64568, we agree that the claims were restricted to only allow specific procedure-device combinations under the device dependent APC methodology for the specific code. Based on the proposed and finalized assignment of the code to New Technology APC 1580, we note that there will not be a specific impact on the CY 2027 OPPS status indicator and APC assignment for CPT code 64568. We no longer restrict those procedure-device combinations.
We recognize the concerns commenters raised with regards to the claims data for CPT code 64568 and how they may describe varying degrees of resource complexity as a result of describing different types of nerve stimulation procedures and the associated clinical indications. However, we believe that with the assignment of CPT code 64568 to New Tech APC 1580, and the future availability of CY 2026 claims that would separate those hypoglossal nerve stimulation services based on distinct C codes, we do not believe it is necessary to update the final rule claims data and associated cost files to assume which claims describe each type of service.
Comment: Some commenters requested the creation of a Level 6 Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC, with some requesting that specific ( printed page 70384) codes or codes with similar costs be included in that Level 6 APC. Those commenters believed that establishing the Level 6 APC would be a permanent way of addressing disparities between payment and resource costs for high-cost, low-volume neurostimulator procedures. They also noted that creating a Level 6 APC would be a way to use more claims for ratesetting based on the estimated costs of the procedures, under a comprehensive APC methodology. Commenters also noted that restructuring and creation of new clinical APCs would allow for efficient payment for services being phased out of the IPO list.
Response: We appreciate the thoughtful responses commenters have provided with regard to the Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC series. At this time, we continue to believe the 5-level APC structure for the APC series remains appropriate and that the individual New Technology APC assignments with respect to the high-cost procedures in this evolving area resolve the concerns around procedure payment relative to cost. Finally, we note that for the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC final rule we are not removing any codes from the IPO list to the Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC series. We will continue to monitor the claims data for these procedures as more information around their volume and estimated costs become available.
After consideration of public comments, we are finalizing the proposed assignments of CPT codes 33276 and 64568 to New Technology APC 1580, finalizing the proposed assignment of 61885 to APC 5465, and maintaining the 5-level APC structure for the Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC series for CY 2027.
Laparoscopy and Related Services (APCs 5361 Through 5362)
As part of the CY 2016 OPPS APC restructuring process, the four level APC series for Laparoscopy and Related Services was consolidated into a 2-level APC series (80 FR 70379). Since that time, we have maintained that 2- level APC structure based on the clinical and resource homogeneity of the services assigned to those APCs.
Comment: A commenter noted that several of the codes newly proposed to be removed from the inpatient only list and assigned to the Level 2 Laparaoscopy and Related Services APC have higher geometric mean costs relative to the APC geometric mean cost for this APC, including for CPT codes 32663 (Thoracoscopy, surgical; with lobectomy (single lobe)), 32666 (Thoracoscopy, surgical; with therapeutic wedge resection ( e.g., mass, nodule), initial unilateral), and 32669 (Thoracoscopy, surgical; with removal of a single lung segment (segmentectomy)). The commenter requested that CMS consider whether a higher level Laparoscopy and Related Services APC is needed to establish appropriate payment for these services in the outpatient setting.
Response: While we monitor the structure of the OPPS and the various APCs, we note that some of the principles guiding the CY 2016 OPPS APC restructuring and consolidation included improved resource and clinical homogeneity, as well as reduced resource overlap in APCs within a clinical family (80 FR 70379). APC 5362 (Level 2 Laparoscopy and Related Services) has an estimated geometric mean cost of $11,401, with a range of geometric mean costs for two times rule purposes ranging from $9,347 for CPT code 58552 (Laparoscopy, surgical, with vaginal hysterectomy, for uterus 250 g or less; with removal of tube(s) and/or ovary(s)) to $13,534 for CPT code 55866 (Laparoscopy, surgical prostatectomy, retropubic radical, including nerve sparing, includes robotic assistance, when performed). While we recognize the commenter's concern around estimated costs for services removed from the IPO list being assigned to the Laparaoscopy and Related Services APC series, we note that geometric mean costs for CPT codes 32666 and 32669 fall well within that range of significant costs for the APC, and that all three codes have limited outpatient claims volume. We do not believe that there is a current need for an additional APC level for the Laparoscopy and Related Services APC series. However, we will continue to monitor the claims data as more claims become available and consider the need for additional APC levels in the future.
After consideration of the public comments, we are finalizing the 2-level APC structure for the Laparoscopy and Related Services APC series in this final rule with comment period as proposed.
Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC Series (APC 5591 Through 5594)
The Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC series was created as part of the broader APC restructuring and consolidation in the CY 2016 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (80 FR 70392 through 70397). The APC series was developed from what were previously separate APC groupings primarily organized by anatomy and imaging modality. Since the initial establishment of the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services series in the CY 2016 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, we have maintained the four-level APC structure for the series.
In the CY 2025 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, we finalized a policy of paying separately for diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals with estimated per day costs higher than a packaging threshold specific to diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals (89 FR 93948 through 93963). Because certain diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals are paid separately under the policy, the nuclear medicine and other services these diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals would otherwise be packaged into would no longer include those costs. As a result, based on the associated changes to the ratesetting process, we observed impacts on the estimated cost of services assigned to the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC series such that the range of cost significant codes across the various APC levels became less distinct, in particular between Levels 3 and 4.
As part of our standard process of reviewing updated claims and cost report data, we continued to observe in the CY 2027 OPPS data that the differences between the four levels of APC geometric means were less distinct than they were previously, in part due to the policy of paying separately for diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals. Specifically, under a four-level APC structure using the 2027 NPRM claims data and maintaining the same APC assignments as in the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, the geometric mean cost of the Level 3 APC would have been $1,367.99 while the geometric mean cost of the Level 4 APC would have been $1,497.06. The range of cost significant codes in the Level 3 APC would have been from $812 to $1,404, while the range for the Level 4 APC would have been from $1,024 to $1,676; indicating a high degree of overlap in the estimated costs of the services assigned to those APC levels. Given the relative proximity of the APC geometric mean costs and the clinical and cost similarities of the services between the APCs in the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services series, we believed that it was appropriate to reorganize the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC series for the CY 2027 OPPS (91 FR 41808).
Additionally, we noted that CPT codes 78431 (Myocardial imaging, positron emission tomography (pet), perfusion study (including ventricular wall motion[s] and/or ejection fraction[s], when performed); multiple studies at rest and stress (exercise or ( printed page 70385) pharmacologic), with concurrently acquired computed tomography transmission scan), 78432 (Myocardial imaging, positron emission tomography (pet), combined perfusion with metabolic evaluation study (including ventricular wall motion[s] and/or ejection fraction[s], when performed), dual radiotracer (e.g., myocardial viability);), and 78433 (Myocardial imaging, positron emission tomography (pet), combined perfusion with metabolic evaluation study (including ventricular wall motion[s] and/or ejection fraction[s], when performed), dual radiotracer (e,g., myocardial viability); with concurrently acquired computed tomography transmission scan) had sufficient CY 2025 claims data available to be appropriately assigned to clinical APCs for CY 2027 OPPS ratesetting. We believed the restructuring of the series now made it appropriate to propose to assign these codes to APC 5594 (Level 4 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services) and we proposed to assign these three CPT codes to APC 5594 for CY 2027 (91 FR 41808).
Based on our review of the updated claims data, we proposed to reassign a number of services to revised levels in the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC series for CY 2027 and to assign CPT codes 78431, 78432, and 78433 to APC 5594 (Level 4 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services) in the CY 2027 OPPS. Please see the APC- sorted Two Times Listing for the proposed rule on the CMS website or Addendum B to the proposed rule to see the Nuclear Medicine APC we proposed to assign each HCPCS code in the series.
Comment: Commenters supported the proposed reorganization of the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC series and the proposed assignment of PET/CT procedures to APC 5594 (Level 4 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services).
Response: We appreciate the commenters' support.
Comment: Two commenters expressed concern regarding the proposed reassignment of CPT code 78830 (Radiopharmaceutical localization of tumor, inflammatory process or distribution of radiopharmaceutical agent(s) (includes vascular flow and blood pool imaging, when performed); tomographic (spect) with concurrently acquired computed tomography (ct) transmission scan for anatomical review, localization and determination/detection of pathology, single area (e.g., head, neck, chest, pelvis) or acquisition, single day imaging) to APC 5592 (Level 2 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services). One of the commenters was concerned that the change would cause a move to more expensive, more invasive tests and that a phased in approach while more claims data continue to be collected.
A commenter expressed concern about the proposed assignment of CPT codes 78075 (Adrenal imaging, cortex and/or medulla), 78454 (Myocardial perfusion imaging, planar (including qualitative or quantitative wall motion, ejection fraction by first pass or gated technique, additional quantification, when performed); multiple studies, at rest and/or stress (exercise or pharmacologic) and/or redistribution and/or rest reinjection), 78811 (Positron emission tomography (pet) imaging; limited area (e.g., chest, head/neck)), and 78831 (Radiopharmaceutical localization of tumor, inflammatory process or distribution of radiopharmaceutical agent(s) (includes vascular flow and blood pool imaging, when performed); tomographic (spect), minimum 2 areas (e.g., pelvis and knees, chest and abdomen) or separate acquisitions (e.g., lung ventilation and perfusion), single day imaging, or single area or acquisition over 2 or more days) to APC 5592 (Level 2 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services) and recommended assignment to APC 5593 (Level 3 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services) instead.
Response: We understand the commenter's concern. Based on the data in this final rule, the geometric mean costs for these codes range from $746.48 for CPT code 78811 to $899.39 for CPT code 78831. We believe that these codes are more appropriately placed based on their estimated costs in APC 5592, with a geometric mean cost of $591.45 rather than the Level 3 APC 5593, which has an estimated geometric mean cost $1,433.70. Additionally, in reviewing the prior year's claims data, the geometric mean cost for these codes were similarly situated. While we will continue to monitor the claims data for these codes in the future, we do not believe a phased approach is necessary, as they are appropriately assigned to APC 5592 based on the geometric mean cost of these services.
After consideration of the public comments we received, we are finalizing the HCPCS assignments for CPT codes 78075, 78454, 78811, 78830, and 78831 to APC 5592, as proposed.
2. Cochlear Infusion of a Pharmacologic Agent, CPT Code 1056T (APC 5165)
For CY 2027, the AMA CPT Editorial Board created a new Category I CPT code 1056T (Placeholder code X565T) to describe a cochlear infusion procedure required for the administration of OTARMENITM which is the first FDA-approved gene therapy for genetic hearing loss.
Later, the AMA CPT Editorial Board changed the effective date of the CPT code 1056T, Cochlear infusion of pharmacologic agent (ie, gene therapy vector), including mastoidectomy, labyrinthotomy, and repair of fenestrations, from January 1, 2027, to October 1, 2026. OTARMENITM is an adeno-associated virus vector-based gene therapy indicated for the treatment of pediatric and adult patients with severe-to-profound and profound sensorineural hearing loss (any frequency >90 dB HL) associated with molecularly confirmed biallelic variants in the OTOF gene, preserved outer hair cell function, and no prior cochlear implant in the same ear.
OTARMENITM is administered as a single dose intracochlear infusion. The recommended dose for each ear is 7.2 × 1012 vector genomes in a total volume of 0.24 ml.
In the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule, we proposed to assign CPT code 1056T to SI “J1”, APC 5163 (Level 3 ENT Procedures) with a proposed payment rate of $1,755.96.
We received public comments on this proposal. The following is a summary of the comments we received.
Comment: The commenters requested that CMS reassign CPT code 1056T from APC 5163 (Level 3 ENT Procedures) to APC 5165 (Level 5 ENT Procedures).
They stated that CPT code 1056T describes a highly specialized surgical procedure that requires significant operative expertise, dedicated training, substantial facility resources, and multidisciplinary coordination. The procedure includes complex otologic surgical components such as mastoidectomy and labyrinthotomy, which are more comparable to higher-acuity ENT procedures than to those typically associated with a Level 3 APC assignment. Because CPT code 1056T includes mastoidectomy as well as additional work associated with intracochlear infusion of a gene therapy vector, the commenters believe that APC 5165 better reflects the resources required to perform the cochlear infusion procedure and represents the most appropriate APC assignment for 1056T.
Commenters also noted that cochlear infusion reported with CPT code 1056T, differs substantially from the procedure described by CPT code 69801 ( Labyrinthotomy, with perfusion of vestibuloactive drug(s), transcanal), which per our proposed rule review was ( printed page 70386) determined to be similar to CPT code 1056T and is assigned to APC 5163. CPT code 1056T describes an open surgical approach that includes mastoidectomy, labyrinthotomy, repair of fenestrations, and intracochlear infusion of a gene therapy vector, whereas CPT code 69801 describes a minimally invasive transcanal drug perfusion procedure that does not include mastoidectomy.
Response: We appreciate the commenters' feedback on this new CPT code, and we agree with the commenters' recommendation to change the APC assignment for this code. Because CPT code 1056T describes an open surgical approach that includes mastoidectomy, which differs from a minimally invasive transcanal drug perfusion procedure described by CPT code 69801, we now believe that CPT code 1056T is more appropriately assigned to APC 5165 (Level 5 ENT Procedures).
In summary, after consideration of the public comments we received, we are not adopting our proposal as final. Instead, we are assigning CPT code 1056T to APC 5165 (Level 5 ENT Procedures) for CY 2027.
Table 29 shows the finalized status indicator and APC assignment for this procedure code. We refer readers to Addendum B of this final rule with comment period for the payment rates for all codes reportable under the OPPS. Addendum B is available via the internet on the CMS website.
2. Vestibular Testing Codes, CPT Codes 92513, 92514, and 92527 (APC 5721)
For CY 2027, the AMA CPT Editorial Board created 4 New Category I CPT codes 92513, 92514, 92527 and 92528 (placeholder CPT codes 92X10, 92X11, 92XX5, and 92XX6). These new codes reflect advances in vestibular testing and provide greater specificity for reporting services used by audiologists to evaluate vestibular function.
92513—Video head impulse testing (vHIT), with recording, interpretation, and report; of lateral semicircular canal function;
92514—Video head impulse testing (vHIT), with recording, interpretation, and report; of lateral and vertical semicircular canal function;
92527—Rotational vestibular assessment by sinusoidal harmonic acceleration (SHA) testing with calibrated, computer-controlled chair, with interpretation and report; and
92528—Rotational vestibular assessment by sinusoidal harmonic acceleration (SHA) testing with calibrated, computer-controlled chair, with interpretation and report; with velocity step testing (VST)
In the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule, we proposed to assign CPT codes 92513, 92514, and 92527 to APC 5721 (Level 1 Diagnostic Tests and Related Services) with status indicator “S” and proposed payment rate of $146.93. We proposed to assign CPT code 92528 to status indicator “N”.
Comment: We received one public comment on this proposal. The commenter supported our assignment of CPT codes 92513, 92514, and 92527 to APC 5721 for CY 2027; however, they were concerned with our proposed assignment of status indicator “N” to CPT code 92528 which would package payment for VST into payment for the base rotational vestibular assessment service (CPT code 92527). The commenter stated that the additional velocity step testing represented by CPT code 92528 requires clinical work and resources beyond those necessary to perform the base SHA testing service represented by CPT code 92527. This, according to the commenter, includes additional provider time and greater work intensity associated with CPT code 92528. The new CPT code family distinguishes the base SHA assessment from the additional VST service. The commenter also recognized our longstanding policy of packaging most procedures described by add-on codes. However, they believed that the distinct resource requirements associated with CPT code 92528 warranted reconsideration.
Response: We thank the commenter for their feedback. Our medical advisors reviewed the service described by CPT code 92528, and we do not believe that it takes significant additional time or hospital resources to perform this service. Therefore, we concluded that VST service described by an add-on CPT code 92528 is appropriately packaged into the base SHA testing service described by CPT code 92527. This is consistent with our packaging policy outlined at 42 CFR 419.2(b), which lists the types of items and services for which payment is packaged under the OPPS. Specifically, certain services described by add-on codes.
Therefore, we believe our proposed assignment of status indicator “N” to CPT code 92528 remains appropriate. As a result, we are finalizing our proposal without modification to assign CPT code 92528 to status indicator “N” for CY 2027.
We refer readers to Addendum D1 to this final rule with comment period for the SI meanings for all codes reported under the OPPS. Addenda D1 is available via the internet on the CMS website.
4. Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) Imaging, CPT Codes 75557, 75559, 75561, 75563 (APCs 5523, 5524, 5572, and 5573)
For CY 2027, we proposed to continue to assign the following cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) CPT codes to APC 5523 (Level 3 Imaging without Contrast), APC 5524 (Level 4 Imaging without Contrast), APC 5572 (Level 2 Imaging with Contrast), and APC 5573 (Level 3 Imaging with Contrast). The codes, long descriptors and payment assignments are listed below.
CPT code 75557—Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging for morphology and function without contrast material. CPT code 75557 is currently assigned to APC 5523 (Level 3 Imaging without Contrast) and has a geometric mean cost of $305 based on 1,453 single frequency claims used for ratesetting; ( printed page 70387)
CPT code 75559—Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging for morphology and function without contrast material; with stress imaging. CPT code 7559 is currently assigned to APC 5524 (Level 4 Imaging without Contrast) and has a geometric mean cost of $378, based on 19 single frequency claims used for ratesetting;
CPT code 75561—Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging for morphology and function without contrast material(s), followed by contrast material(s) and further sequences. CPT code 75561 is assigned to APC 5572 (Level 2 Imaging with Contrast) and has a geometric mean cost of $460, based on 33,824 single frequency claims used for ratesetting; and
CPT code 75563—Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging for morphology and function without contrast material(s), followed by contrast material(s) and further sequences; with stress imaging. CPT code 75563 is assigned to APC 5573 (Level 3 Imaging with Contrast) and has a geometric mean cost of $783 based on 3,401 single frequency claims used for ratesetting.
We received one public comment on these codes.
Comment: The commenter states that our “current modality-based APC structure creates a substantial and increasingly difficult-to-justify payment disparity between clinically comparable advanced cardiac imaging services.” The commenter suggests that contrast-enhanced cardiac MRI (CMR) requires more hospital resources than single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) and positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging and should not be placed in general imaging APCs with/without contrast APCs that also include non-cardiac related imaging examinations requiring very different resources. According to the commenter, the payment for SPECT and PET is influenced by advanced cardiac imaging while the payment for CMR is influenced by a much broader range of imaging procedures. The commenter refers to the historical placement of CPT 75563 in APC 5593 (Level 3 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services)—before the CY 2017 APC restructuring—and how there is resource and clinical homogeneity between CMR and nuclear cardiac imaging. This is especially important, the commenter continues, because these codes include contrast-enhanced imaging and pharmacologic stress. The commenter notes that these services are paid approximately 40-60 percent less despite the commenter's belief that there is comparable or greater clinical resource intensity.
The commenter requested that we reassign CPT code 75561 to APC 5593 and reassign CPT code 75563 to APC 5594. The commenter also requested that we evaluate the appropriate placement of CPT code 75557 which is currently assigned to APC 5523 and CPT code 75559 which is currently assigned to APC 5524.
Response: We thank the commenter for their thoughtful input. The OPPS payment rates were proposed based on available CY 2025 claims data. Our claims data shows that APC 5593 (Level 3 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services) has a geometric mean cost of approximately $1,433 which is significantly higher than the geometric mean costs of the cardiac MRI codes ($305 to $783).
As stated in last year's final rule (90 FR 53567), we do not believe that cardiac MRI with stress imaging is very similar to myocardial perfusion imaging just because both tests are performed under a stress protocol, and therefore should be assigned to a nuclear medicine APC. APC 5593 contains procedures that describe nuclear medicine tests, not MRI services. We continue to believe (and have stated in previous rulemaking), that MRI services should not be assigned to the nuclear medicine APCs (81 FR 79630 and 90 FR 53567).
In summary, after consideration of the public comment, we are finalizing our proposal without modification to maintain the APC assignments for the cardiac MRI codes for CY 2027. The final CY 2027 payment rates for these codes can be found in Addendum B to this final rule with comment period. In addition, we refer readers to Addendum D1 to this final rule with comment period for the status indicator definitions for all codes reported under the OPPS. Addenda B and D1 are available via the internet on the CMS website.
5. Cardiac CT Services, CPT Codes 75572, 75573, and 75574 (APC 5572)
Cardiac computed tomography services are described by the following Category I CPT codes and have been effective since January 1, 2010:
75572—Computed tomography, heart, with contrast material, for evaluation of cardiac structure and morphology (including 3D image postprocessing, assessment of cardiac function, and evaluation of venous structures, if performed);
75573—Computed tomography, heart, with contrast material, for evaluation of cardiac structure and morphology in the setting of congenital heart disease (including 3D image postprocessing, assessment of left ventricular [LV] cardiac function, right ventricular [RV] structure and function and evaluation of vascular structures, if performed); and
75574—Computed tomographic angiography, heart, coronary arteries and bypass grafts (when present), with contrast material, including 3D image postprocessing (including evaluation of cardiac structure and morphology, assessment of cardiac function, and evaluation of venous structures, if performed).
For CY 2027, the OPPS payment rates were proposed based on available CY 2025 claims data for ratesetting. We note that CPT code 75572 has a geometric mean cost of $183 calculated using 41,211 single frequency claims; CPT code 75573 has a geometric mean cost of $234 calculated using 559 claims; and CPT code 75574 has a geometric mean cost of $227 calculated using 116,963 claims. For CY 2027, we proposed to maintain these codes to APC 5572 (Level 2 Imaging with Contrast) with a payment rate of around $400.
As a reminder to readers, we reassigned these codes to APC 5572 in CY 2025 because of the assumption that facilities would have chosen the cardiology revenue code if they had been able to versus the CT scan (035X) and Radiology Diagnostic (032X) revenue codes. We became aware of an edit (that we removed in December 2024) that was prohibiting hospitals from reporting these codes with a cardiology revenue code (048X) which maps to the cardiology cost center (03140). The cardiology cost center has a higher cost-to-charge ratio (CCR) than the imaging cost centers. Utilizing cost centers with lower CCRs results in a lower OPPS payment compared to utilizing cost centers with higher CCRs. With the edit no longer in place, hospitals are able to bill for cardiac CT services with whichever revenue code they believe is appropriate for these services, including cardiology revenue code 048X. For a full discussion of this issue, we refer readers to 89 FR 94057 through 94062. We received public comments on these codes.
Comment: We received numerous comments in support of maintaining the current APC assignment. Commenters requested that we continue to maintain the APC assignment while they continue their efforts to educate their providers and hospitals to change their billing practices. They note that there is continued hesitancy surrounding the selection of appropriate revenue codes because of `CT' in the coding descriptors. The revenue codes hospitals use to report cardiac CT ( printed page 70388) services materially affects whether OPPS payment accurately reflects the resources involved in furnishing them. Reporting cardiac CT services under cardiology revenue codes (048x) more accurately reflects the resources associated with furnishing the service. Additionally, a commenter requested that CMS issue sub-regulatory guidance and provider education confirming that cardiology revenue codes are appropriate to report for cardiac CT services, so that facility cost data and OPPS rate-setting better reflect the clinical resources used to provide the services.
Response: We appreciate the commenters' support. Once again, we agree with commenters that effectuating change in any health system can be challenging. As we stated in the CY 2025 OPPS/ASC final rule, we will continue to monitor the claims data for these services, knowing that it may take a number of years before we see changes in the claims data.
As noted previously, commenters continue to request guidance that explicitly states that it is appropriate to use the cardiology revenue codes when billing for cardiac CT services. As a reminder to our readers and as we have previously stated, we do not provide specific coding guidance. We refer our readers to section 20.5 in Chapter 4 (Part B Hospital) of the Medicare Claims Processing Manual, “CMS does not instruct hospitals on the assignment of HCPCS codes to revenue codes for services provided under OPPS since hospitals' assignments of cost vary. Where explicit instructions are not provided, HOPDs should report their charges under the revenue code that will result in the charges being assigned to the same cost center to which the cost of those services are assigned in the cost report.” We have consistently stated that hospital outpatient facilities must determine the most appropriate cost center and revenue code for the cardiac CT codes (87 FR 71849, 88 FR 81664, and 90 FR 53566).
In summary for CY 2027, we are finalizing our proposal without modification and assigning CT codes 75572, 75573, and 75574 to APC 5572 (Level 2 Imaging with Contrast). The final CY 2027 payment rates for these codes can be found in Addendum B to this final rule with comment period. In addition, we refer readers to Addendum D1 to this final rule with comment period for the status indicator definitions for all codes reported under the OPPs. Addenda B and D1 are available via the internet on the CMS website.
6. Cardiac Leadless Pacemaker Procedures, CPT Codes 0823T, 0796T, 0795T, 0801T, 0802T, and 0825T (APCs 5231 and 5232)
CPT codes 0823T and 0796T describe the insertion of a permanent single-chamber leadless pacemaker and the insertion of a permanent dual-chamber leadless pacemaker when a right ventricular single leadless pacemaker already exists. Their long descriptors and current APC and status indicators are listed below.

7. C-Codes Describing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With Drug-Eluting Stents
Effective January 1, 2013, CMS created several HCPCS C-codes to describe certain percutaneous coronary intervention procedures utilizing drug eluting stents to mirror those PCI CPT codes that do not utilize drug eluting stents. The AMA CPT Editorial Board deleted several of those CPT codes effective January 1, 2026. For CY 2027, we proposed to delete the following C-codes that mirrored the deleted CPT codes, specifically revising the status indicators to “D” (Discontinued Codes) indicating that they are no longer active codes (91 FR 41811). The C-codes and their long descriptors are listed below.
C9601—Percutaneous transcatheter placement of drug-eluting intracoronary stent(s), with coronary angioplasty when performed; each additional branch of a major coronary artery (list separately in addition to code for primary procedure).
C9603—Percutaneous transluminal coronary atherectomy, with drug-eluting intracoronary stent, with coronary angioplasty when performed; each additional branch of a major coronary artery (list separately in addition to code for primary procedure).
C9605—Percutaneous transluminal revascularization of or through coronary artery bypass graft (internal mammary, free arterial, venous), any combination of drug-eluting intracoronary stent, atherectomy and angioplasty, including distal protection when performed; each additional branch subtended by the bypass graft (list separately in addition to code for primary procedure).
C9608—Percutaneous transluminal revascularization of chronic total occlusion, coronary artery, coronary artery branch, or coronary artery bypass graft, any combination of drug-eluting intracoronary stent, atherectomy and angioplasty; each additional coronary artery, coronary artery branch, or bypass graft (list separately in addition to code for primary procedure).
We received several comments related to this proposal.
Comments: Commenters supported the deletion of these C-codes but a couple of commenters requested that we create a new C-code to mirror CPT code 92930 ( Percutaneous transcatheter placement of intracoronary stent(s), with coronary angioplasty when performed, single major coronary artery and/or its branch(es); 2 or more distinct ( printed page 70390) coronary lesions with 2 or more coronary stents deployed in 2 or more coronary segments, or a bifurcation lesion requiring angioplasty and/or stenting in both the main artery and the side branch ) when two drug eluting stents are used in two or more distinct lesions. The commenters stated that without an equivalent C-code for this scenario, there would be a CPT/HCPCS mismatch.
Response: We thank the commenters for their support to delete the previous C-codes. We disagree with commenters that a new C-code should be created to mirror CPT code 92930. The deleted C-codes were created when drug-eluting stents were novel and had significantly higher costs associated with them and we needed a mechanism to capture those costs. We believe that the gap between the costs of drug-eluting stents and bare metal stents are not as significant as they were over ten years ago when these C-codes were created.
In summary, after consideration of the public comments we received, we are finalizing our proposal without modification to delete the previous HCPCS C-codes and decline to create a C-code at this time to mirror CPT code 92930.
8. Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR-T) Administration, CPT Code 38228 (APC 5694)

Dialysis Related Services and Technologies
11. Dialysis-Related Amyloidosis (DRA) Treatment With LIXELLE® Apheresis Columns and Dialysis Technologies
LIXELLE® b2-microglobulinApheresis Column is indicated for use in the treatment of dialysis-related amyloidosis (DRA), a disease that affects people with end-stage renal disease (ESRD). DRA is a metabolic disorder from the failure of the kidney to filter and remove b2 microglobulin, typically from chronic hemodialysis (typically 5 years or longer). The LIXELLE® device is used in an apheresis procedure that selectively removes b2-microglobulin from circulating blood and is used in accordance with a physician prescription in conjunction with hemodialysis. It is intended to be used at each hemodialysis session (that is, frequency of treatment is expected to be 3 times per week). In March 2015, FDA approved a Humanitarian Device Exemption (HDE) application for LIXELLE® a Class III Humanitarian Use Device (HUD).
For CY 2027, there are currently no specific HCPCS or CPT codes that represent the service performed with the LIXELLE® apheresis device. We received public comments on this topic. The following is a summary of the comments we received and our responses.
Comment: A commenter notes that access to LIXELLE® has been limited by the lack of a clear reimbursement pathway, and they urge CMS to clarify coverage in the OPPS Final Rule for the benefit of the small number of patients with DRA. The commenter states that the FDA recognizes that there continues to be no feasible alternative treatments for DRA in the United States, and that extensive clinical evidence supports LIXELLE® as reasonable and necessary for the treatment of DRA.
The commenter understands that CMS continues to evaluate how to facilitate Medicare reimbursement for treatments of medical devices that are administered during dialysis procedures but that are not “renal dialysis services” and supports a CMS policy clarification that such treatments and dialysis procedures that accompany them are appropriately reimbursed through OPPS benefit. The commenter reminded CMS ( printed page 70392) that the FDA further clarified that “qualified health care professionals such as physician assistants, nurse practitioner or registered nurses are qualified to supervise hemodialysis procedures” to alleviate previous clinical supervision concerns.
Another commenter supported the payment of dialysis technologies not included in the End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) bundle through the OPPS and urged CMS to assign an appropriate APC to facilitate payment for the apheresis procedure with LIXELLE® in the OPPS.
Response: We appreciate the comments and continued interest regarding coverage and payment for medical device technologies used in conjunction with dialysis services, such as LIXELLE® for the treatment of DRA. We understand that DRA represents a serious complication for long-term dialysis patients and the need for effective treatment options. We continue to contemplate coverage pathways for innovative treatments that address unmet medical needs in the ESRD population and note this complex, ongoing issue is still under consideration.
We remind commenters that routine outpatient maintenance dialysis for End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) is not paid under the OPPS and because the treatment with Lixelle is used at each hemodialysis session ( e.g., routine maintenance dialysis), we do not believe that the OPPS is a viable option for payment for the DRA treatment with LIXELLE® at this time. We also recognize the challenges of ensuring appropriate payment pathways for innovative treatments that may be administered during dialysis but fall outside the definition of a renal dialysis service under § 413.171 and thus are not paid for under the ESRD PPS.
We will continue to evaluate the appropriate payment mechanisms for such technologies for future rulemaking.

15. Venous Mechanical Thrombectomy, CPT Code 37187 (APC 5193)
CPT code 37187 (Percutaneous transluminal mechanical thrombectomy, vein(s), including intraprocedural pharmacological thrombolytic injections and fluoroscopic guidance) was made effective January 1, 2006 and discussed in the CY 2007 OPPS final rule. Since the CY 2018 OPPS, this code has been assigned to the Endovascular Procedures APC series and has been assigned to APC 5193 since the CY 2021 OPPS (85 FR 85987).
Comment: A commenter requested that CMS reconsider the current methodology used to determine claims for ratesetting for CPT code 37187 and the proposed assignment of the code to APC 5193. The commenter opined that the current rate does not adequately reflect the reported geometric mean cost for the procedure and variation in the costs at the claim level. The commenter, using the growth in Medicare usage of venous thrombectomy and increased utilization of the hospital outpatient setting, asked CMS to consider whether the rate-setting claims adequately reflect current practice patterns and the adoption of technology, variation in coding, complexity of patients, and site-of-service trends, and to consider whether additional data or a different methodology would better determine accurate payments.
Response: We appreciate the commenter's concerns regarding payment for CPT code 37187. CMS previously reassigned CPT 37187 from APC 5192 to APC 5193 for CY 2021 after finding that its geometric mean cost was comparable to other clinically related thrombectomy and endovascular services in APC 5193 (85 FR 85987). We reviewed the most updated claims data available for CY 2027 rate setting and continue to believe that APC 5193 appropriately reflects the clinical characteristics and relative resource costs of CPT code 37187. Under the OPPS, payment rates are established at the APC level based on the geometric mean cost of all applicable services assigned to the APC based on clinical and cost similarity. The number of claims used to calculate the geometric mean cost for CPT code 37187 represents claims remaining after application of the comprehensive APC rate-setting methodology and should not be interpreted as total Medicare utilization. Under that methodology, qualifying higher-cost combinations involving CPT code 37187 receive a complexity adjustment and are reassigned to the next higher-level endovascular APC. Consequently, those complexity-adjusted claims are removed from the cost calculation for CPT code 37187 in APC 5193 and included separately in APC 5194. We further note that most claims containing CPT code 37187 that were available were used for OPPS ratesetting purposes, whether for the code itself or as part of a code combination qualifying for complexity adjustment.
Although the commenter identified variation among CPT code 37187 claims, this variation does not, by itself, demonstrate that the claims are inaccurate or that the service is inappropriately assigned. Moreover, we believe that some of that variation is a reflection of the varying practice patterns in the claims containing codes, most of which we are using in our OPPS ratesetting process. Therefore, we are finalizing the assignment of CPT code 37187 to APC 5193.
16. Simulation Angiogram for Radioembolization of Tumors, HCPCS Code C8004 (APC 5194)
CMS created HCPCS code C9797 ( Vascular embolization or occlusion procedure with use of a pressure-generating catheter (e.g., one-way valve or occlusion balloon, intermittently or temporarily occluding), inclusive of all radiological supervision and interpretation, intraprocedural roadmapping, and imaging guidance necessary to complete the intervention; for tumors, organ ischemia, or infarction) to describe a vascular embolization or occlusion procedure with use of a pressure-generating catheter effective April 1, 2024. We assigned C9797 to APC 5194 (Level 4 Endovascular Procedures) and a status indicator of `J1'.
CMS then created HCPCS C8004 (Simulation angiogram with use of a pressure-generating catheter (e.g., one-way valve or occlusion balloon, intermittently or temporarily occluding), inclusive of all radiological supervision and interpretation, intraprocedural roadmapping, and imaging guidance necessary to complete the angiogram, for subsequent therapeutic radioembolization of tumors) to describe the simulation angiogram service using a pressure-generating catheter effective April 1, 2025. The simulation procedure has a nearly identical workflow to the embolization procedure, including the use of the same pressure-generating catheter, and allows delivery of the diagnostic radioactive tracer to maximize the radiation dose to the tumor and avoid the normal liver tissue. The device code is currently assigned to status indicator `N' which means it is packaged with the procedure code.

We are also aware of the new HCPCS G-code G0577 (Vascular embolization or occlusion procedure with use of a pressure-generating catheter (e.g., one-way valve, intermittently occluding), inclusive of all radiological supervision and interpretation, intraprocedural roadmapping, and imaging guidance necessary to complete the intervention; for tumors, organ ischemia, or infarction performed in the non-facility setting) that was created for the non-facility setting and is retroactive to July 1, 2026. Comment: A commenter requested that CMS reassign CPT code 74263 from APC 5523 (Level 3 Imaging without contrast) to APC 5524 (Level 4 Imaging without Contrast). The commenter notes that reimbursement for Computed Tomographic Colonography (CTC) remains substantially lower than payment for comparable CT imaging services. They state that unlike other imaging services assigned to non-contrast imaging APC's, CTC requires significant radiologist and technologist involvement, as well as increased resource costs, and an APC assignment to 5524 (Level 4 Imaging without Contrast) would better align payment with complexity and recourse costs. They encourage CMS to consider exceptions, safeguards, or transition policies for preventive screenings, which will ensure that payment changes do not reduce beneficiary access or discourage adherence to recommended screening guidelines.

We recognize that CTC involves bowel preparation, oral contrast administration, insufflation, multiple image acquisitions, image postprocessing and technologist involvement. Our claims data shows that APC 5523 (Level 3 Imaging without contrast) has a geometric mean cost (GMC) of $250, and APC 5524 (Level 4 Imaging without contrast) has a GMC of $577. We reviewed CPT code 74263 and noted that the GMC is $88 based on 692 single frequency claims.
While we understand the commenter's rationale, we believe that reassigning CPT code 74263 to APC 5524 would result in overpayments based on the GMC for the code of $88, compared to the GMC of APC 5524 which is $577.

22. Breast Imaging Service Performed With QT Scanner, CPT Code 1079T (APC 5522)
Effective October 1, 2026, CPT code 1079T (placeholder code X579T) (3D quantitative transmission water bath volumetric ultrasound tomography, breast, with augmentative algorithmic derivation of breast tissue composition (ie, fibroglandular volume), bilateral, with physician or other qualified health care professional interpretation and report) describes the breast imaging service performed with QT Scanner. The device uses a 360-degree moving transducer to generate quantitative 3D breast images. The QT Scanner 2000 Model A is indicated to provide reflection-mode and transmission-mode breast images and calculates fibroglandular tissue volume (breast density), and is “not intended to be used as a replacement for screening mammography.”
For CY 2027, we proposed to assign CPT code 1079T to status indicator “E1” because we did not believe the QT Scanner service would fall under an existing benefit category.
We received a public comment on this proposal. The following is a summary of the comment we received and our response.
Comment: A commenter, the manufacturer of QT Scanner, requested that we revise the proposed “E1” status indicator to status indicator “S” for CPT code 1079T and assign the code to a new technology APC. Per the commenter, physician-ordered diagnostic use of the QT Scanner falls within an existing Medicare benefit category under section 1861(s)(3) and section 1861(s)(2)(B) of the Social Security Act, and NCD 220.5 (Ultrasound Diagnostic Procedures (Effective May 22, 2007)) provides coverage either as breast sonography under Category I or as an unenumerated diagnostic ultrasound procedure subject to local MAC discretion under Section D. The commenter also cited FDA clearance of the QT Scanner 2000 Model ( printed page 70398) A (K253898) and CPT's creation of the Category III CPT code as support for the existence of a diagnostic use distinct from screening.
Response: After reviewing the comment, we agree, on a narrow basis, that assignment of status indicator E1 is not appropriate for CPT code 1079T. We agree that physician-ordered use of a QT Scanner to evaluate a specific clinical finding could be capable of falling within the existing diagnostic ultrasound benefit category described in NCD 220.5 Ultrasound Diagnostic Procedures, consistent with CMS's treatment of other forms of breast sonography. In the event this code is covered, and determined to be reasonable and necessary, we believe an appropriate APC assignment for CPT code 1079T is APC 5522 (Level 2 Imaging without Contrast), based on similar codes in that APC series, for example CPT code 76641 (Ultrasound, breast, unilateral or bilateral, real-time with image documentation, complete). Therefore, for CY 2027, in response to the commenter, we are revising our proposal in this final rule and assigning CPT code 1079T to APC 5522 with status indicator “S.”
As we have consistently stated in past OPPS/ASC final rules with comment period (see, for example, 87 FR 71879 and 88 FR 81660 through 81661), the fact that a drug, device, procedure or service is assigned a HCPCS code and a payment rate under the OPPS does not imply coverage by the Medicare program, but indicates only how the product, procedure, or service may be paid if covered by the program. Coverage of a claim where the QT Scanner is used would require an independent showing, made at the time the claim is adjudicated, that the service was reasonable and necessary for the individual beneficiary under section 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Act, ordered by a physician to address a specific diagnostic question.
While our decision to finalize payment rests on the plausible diagnostic use of this technology within the existing framework of NCD 220.5, under current rules, use of the QT Scanner would not be covered by Medicare as a screening service. Coverage of breast ultrasonography as a screening service would require either a statutory change or a qualifying recommendation from the United States Preventive Services Task Force under section 1861(ddd) of the Act. Neither condition currently exists. Therefore, claims for QT Scanner where the service is furnished for routine screening of asymptomatic beneficiaries would not currently be covered. Additionally, we clarify that the indication for the FDA-cleared device, itself, does not support the use of the QT Scanner device for breast cancer screening.
In summary, we are not finalizing our proposal to assign CPT code 1079T to status indicator “E1” as proposed. In response to the commenter, for CY 2027, we are assigning CPT code 1079T to APC 5522 and status indicator “S.” Refer to Table 36 for the final CY 2027 OPPS APC and status indicator assignments for CPT code 1079T. The final CY 2027 payment rates for this code can be found in Addendum B to this final rule with comment period. In addition, we refer readers to Addendum D1 to this final rule with comment period for the status indicator definitions for all codes reported under the OPPS. Addenda B and D1 are available via the internet on the CMS website.

Comment: Commenters offered appreciation for the OPPS inclusion of APC assignments for the new code and expressed concern that the proposed APC assignments do not adequately distinguish between certain maternity services in terms of clinical and resource requirements. Commenters encouraged CMS to ensure that the upper levels of the Gynecologic Procedures APC family maintain appropriate clinical and resource homogeneity and sufficient payment differentiation for exceptionally ( printed page 70399) resource-intensive gynecologic and obstetric procedures. Commenters noted that complex labor management can involve greater monitoring, staffing, clinical intervention, and other hospital resources than straightforward labor management. Commenters stated that assigning both services to the same APC effectively eliminates resource distinctions for hospital outpatient payment purposes. Commenters stated that it would be more appropriate to assign complex labor management codes to APC 5415, Level 5 Gynecologic Procedures.

They also stated that the abdominal surgical procedure of cesarean deliveries requires an operating room, a surgical, sterile environment, and the necessary equipment for an abdominal incision and closure, not dissimilar to the requirements in APC 5342, Level 2 Abdominal/Peritoneal/Biliary and Related Procedures, or APC 5361, Level 1 Laparoscopy and Related Services. However, we continue to believe that CPT codes 59081, 59082, 59083, 59431, 59502, 59503, and 59504 are appropriately assigned. We note that we will continue to monitor the APC series as more claims data are available for the procedures assigned to this series and remain interested in suggestions and supporting materials regarding changes to those assignments for future years.
In summary, for CY 2027, CMS will finalize the maternity care service codes as proposed, with the modification of assigning CPT code 59432 to APC 5415.
