A lengthy resolution on “full and rigorous party self-governance” adopted at the end of the plenum makes clear that the campaign to strengthen discipline is far from complete.  Front and center are concerns that cadres are unwilling or unable to deliver on policy tasks, the need to keep in check those in high-powered, central positions, and the perceived lack of “party spirit,” especially among younger CCP officials. The document formally elevates the growing body of Xi’s “thought on party building” and portrays him as having rescued the party from internal corrosion and a fading grasp on power.   To address disciplinary and performance failures and ensure that cadres do not engage in corruption, the resolution lays out expanded party rules, stricter performance and promotion standards, and stronger supervisory mechanisms. It also prescribes extensive political education to strengthen loyalty and identification with the CCP. Together, these measures are meant to cultivate a cohort of high-caliber officials capable, in the words of the Central Committee, of “shouldering the mission of national rejuvenation.” At the same time, the document reveals persistent tensions within Xi’s governance model. Efforts to reduce formalism rely on additional layers of oversight and bureaucracy. Cadres are encouraged to be innovative and proactive, but only within approved boundaries and after securing authorization. They are expected to voice concerns, yet not challenge decisions handed down from the party center. Navigating these at times contradictory demands requires skill, loyalty and political savvy. “Xi’s purges and disciplinary measures are not just tools for maintaining personal power but a matter of ideological conviction. They will now cover all testing facilities in countries that lack a Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA) with the US, which allows the reciprocal recognition of testing results. The People’s Bank of China (PBOC), the country’s central bank, jumped in this week to stem further losses – highlighting the government’s concern about investor confidence in a market driven significantly by household investment. What does this rare move outside of a Party Congress signal? The timing of Zhang’s appointment was unusual, as well as the fact that Zhang, at 68, is already past the customary age limit of 67 for new Politburo members. His current position of Central Military Commission (CMC) Vice-Chairman is, however, typically aligned with a spot in the Politburo. Pulling the appointment forward from next year’s Party Congress could be related to plans for a potential restructuring or restocking of the CMC, where Zhang’s experience would be highly useful. As CMC Vice-Chairman and the general in charge of Xi’s recent military purges, he is a veteran of the PLA’s discipline system – the internal oversight structure for rooting out corruption and ensuring party loyalty among the armed forces. Next year’s Party Congress could be an opportunity for his retirement. Yet the fact that no other PLA officer was promoted to full membership in the Central Committee also signals that Xi Jinping is in no rush to fill vacant positions, and that the anticipated generational and post-purge transition may still take time. There were also more purges than usual at the Plenum. Who was ousted and why? This Plenum saw the lowest turnout of the post-Mao era – around a quarter of all Central Committee members did not attend – an indication of the scale of the recent CCP purges. The Plenum formally ratified the expulsion of several high-level officials such as Ma Xingrui, the former Party Secretary of Xinjiang – the so-called autonomous region where Uyghurs and other ethnic groups have lived under decades of repressive policies, as well as the two top PLA Generals Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli. The additional expulsion of Liu Jianchao, former Head of the CCP’s International Department, an important instrument of China’s global influence, confirms the growing impact of the purges on China’s foreign relations apparatus. While these purges may be an attempt to reinforce Xi’s control over the party, they also risk creating a climate of fear and uncertainty inside and raise questions about the institutional capacity of the state. But as officials were pushed out, some younger figures managed to move up. Why? While many more positions were left empty in the Central Committee, ten of its alternate members were promoted to full membership. They are all civilians, and some of these officials have profiles that set them up for a potentially bright future in central leadership and decision-making organs, especially those who are currently in their early to mid-fifties. One of them is Liu Jie, the Deputy Party Secretary and Governor of Zhejiang province, Xi Jinping’s former power base. The Plenum’s resolution hints at the leadership’s anxieties around the character and core beliefs of younger leaders, especially those born after 1978 – the beginning of China’s reform and opening. Many of the efforts laid out in the resolution – intensified education on Communist ideals or training in conduct and discipline – will be directed toward these future leaders. This not only aims to secure excellent performance, but also to “forge” their political conviction, love for the party, and loyalty to Xi Jinping, so that his legacy can continue long after he is gone. Whether that will work once the new generation rises to power will be another question. content:
波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那上个月举行大选时，使用了生物识别选民身份识别和选票扫描仪——这项改革因产生快速、准确的结果而受到广泛赞誉。这是一项真正的成就。但该地区的数字基础仍然脆弱，该地区的对手也知道这一点。巴尔干棋盘依然错综复杂，在欧盟和俄罗斯之间左右为难，而中国则在谋求筹码。波斯尼亚民族主义者，包括分离主义者、亲俄罗斯的塞尔​​维亚人，赢得了最近的投票。但塞尔维亚人在十月的另一次选举中让亲欧洲的学生领导的运动获得了明显多数，而黑山和阿尔巴尼亚则结束了入盟谈判。改变权力平衡的最便宜的方法是破坏对选票的信任。对于该地区来说，网络安全不是一个技术问题。这是一项战略性的任务。华盛顿正在意识到这一风险，但需要加强对数字危险的关注。欧盟已经在敦促采取行动，但也必须加强审查。在整个地区，国家网络响应团队仍然规模较小且资金不足，公共系统过时，责任分散。从税收和健康记录到波斯尼亚新的生物识别选民数据，大量敏感数据都保存在很少经过审计的数据库中。电信和监控网络依赖中国设备。
中国提供的贝尔格莱德“安全城市”面部识别系统就是最著名的例子。克里姆林宫资助的媒体和匿名网络随时准备放大虚假信息，人工智能现在可以廉价地以当地语言生产这些信息。中国华为仍然是波斯尼亚两家最大移动运营商 BH Telecom 和 Republika Srpska's M:Tel 的主要供应商。这种选择的安全风险从未被认真考虑过。西方资金支付了大部分基础设施的费用。波斯尼亚的生物识别投票携带了公民的通话、数据和生物识别记录——它的可信度取决于所部署的设备和供应商。获取最新注册以定期接收带宽电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作情况。电子邮件提交 Δ document.getElementById( "ak_js_6" ).setAttribute( "value", ( new Date() ).getTime() ); gform.initializeOnLoaded( function() {jQuery('#gform_ajax_frame_9').on('load',function(){var content = jQuery(this).contents().find('*').html();var is_postback =contents.indexOf('GF_AJAX_POSTBACK') >= 0;if(!is_postback){return;}var form_content = jQuery(this).contents().find('#gform_wrapper_9');var is_confirmation = jQuery(this).contents().find('#gform_confirmation_wrapper_9').length > 0;var is_redirect =contents.indexOf('gformRedirect(){') >= 0;var is_form = form_content.length > 0 && is_redirect &&！

When Bosnia and Herzegovina held general elections last month, it  used  biometric voter identification and ballot scanners — a reform widely praised for producing fast and accurate results. That’s a real achievement. But the region’s digital foundations remain fragile, and the region’s adversaries know it. The Balkan chessboard remains checkered, torn between attraction to the European Union and to Russia, with China maneuvering for leverage. Bosnian nationalists, including separatist, pro-Russian Serbs,  won  the recent vote. But Serbs  gave  a pro-European student-led movement a clear majority in another October election, while Montenegro and Albania  closed chapters  in their EU accession talks.  The cheapest way to shift the balance of power is to undermine trust in the ballot. For the region, cybersecurity is not a technical issue. It is a strategic one. Washington is waking up to the risk — but needs to increase its focus on digital dangers. The EU is already pressing for action but must also increase its scrutiny.  Across the region, national cyber-response teams remain small and underfunded, public systems are outdated, and responsibility is fragmented. Large volumes of sensitive data, from tax and health records to the new biometric voter data in Bosnia, are held in databases that are rarely audited.  Telecommunications and surveillance networks rely on Chinese equipment. Belgrade’s Chinese-supplied “ safe city ” facial-recognition system represents the best-known example. Kremlin-funded media and anonymous networks are ready to amplify disinformation, which artificial intelligence now makes cheap to produce in local languages. China’s Huawei remains the dominant supplier to Bosnia’s two largest mobile operators, BH Telecom and Republika Srpska’s M:Tel. The security risks of that choice have never been seriously considered. Western money paid for much of that infrastructure. Bosnia’s biometric voting carries its citizens’ calls, data, and biometric records — and it is only as trustworthy as the equipment and the vendors deployed. For a hostile power, this represents an attractive environment. It does not need to defeat Balkan institutions, only to find the least-protected one. Access gained can be used to collect data on officials, NATO personnel, and diaspora communities; to map energy grids and transport hubs; and to prepare disruption that can be switched on in a crisis. Consider Albania. Earlier this year, HomeLand Justice, a hacker group that the Albanian government links to Iran,  broke  into the national parliament, deleted data, and published lawmakers’ emails on Telegram. Investigators believe the attackers had administrative access well before they revealed themselves; passwords had reportedly not been changed for years, and intrusion alarms did not sound. It was the group’s third major attack on Albanian institutions since 2022.  There are other notable attacks. Ransomware paralyzed Montenegro’s government networks in 2022. Bosnia lacks a fully functioning state-level cyber emergency response team. A 2022 ransomware attack crippled the country’s Parliamentary Assembly, taking its servers, website, and email offline. Thousands of employees in state institutions were locked out of their networks for more than two weeks. No public report on the incident or its lessons was ever released . The pattern persists. In early 2024, hackers breached the Bosnian Republika Srpska’s health information system and its tax administration. Washington has started to worry. Representatives Ritchie Torres and Joe Wilson have introduced H.R. 10748 , the Balkans Security Cooperation Act, which asks the Pentagon to report on every Western Balkan country’s security cooperation with Russia, China, the US, and NATO, including arms deals, exercises, agreements, and intelligence ties. It also asks for an assessment of the Russian-Serbian Humanitarian Center in Niš, which has signed a new development plan with Serbia’s interior ministry for 2025-2027 and whose request for diplomatic status for its staff the US and EU have resisted since 2014. The bill counts tanks, missiles, and agreements. It does not count code, vendors, or data. That gap matters, because the most likely next attack on a Balkan state will not arrive by air. As the bill moves forward, Congress should add a cyber and data annex covering four questions: Which hostile cyber operations have targeted each country since 2012, and by whom? Which foreign vendors supply critical telecommunications, energy, surveillance, and election systems, and under what legal obligations to their home governments? How well are sensitive government and citizen data protected, including biometric data? Where would US, NATO, and EU assistance close gaps fastest? Iran, whose operations in Albania are well-documented, should be included alongside Russia and China. Europe should not wait for Washington. The EU already demands cybersecurity and data protection standards as part of the accession process, and Montenegro and Albania are moving quickly through the chapters. Brussels and NATO should make cyber-resilience a visible, funded priority across the region: shared incident response, regular audits of critical databases, support for election security, and clear rules on high-risk vendors in critical networks. The new political moment creates an opening. Serbia’s incoming government has promised transparency and the rule of law while keeping military neutrality. Cyber cooperation is one area where it can work closely with EU and NATO partners without changing that stance. Bosnia’s successful use of election technology shows what is possible, and also creates a new duty to protect biometric data. Western Balkan citizens want accountable institutions. Protecting that legitimacy means protecting their networks. （德国之声中文网）台湾将于11月28日举行“九合一”选举，其中台北市长选情尤其受到关注。
民进党候选人沈伯洋近来选情升温。这位被北京列入制裁名单、指控为“台独顽固分子”的政治人物掀起一股“洋流”，对现任台北市长、国民党籍的蒋万安构成强劲挑战。部分民调显示，沈伯洋的支持度已与蒋万安不相上下，甚至一度实现反超。
沈伯洋近日接受路透社专访时表示，台北市长选举无论最终由谁胜出，都将是台湾民主在面对中国压力下的一次胜利。
他告诉路透社，中国对于台湾民众能够自由选择领导人这件事感到不满。“对我来说，即便蒋万安当选，也是打了中国一记耳光。因为这证明了民主在台湾行得通，而且我们不受中国干预。”
沈伯洋：即使蒋万安当选，也是台湾民主赢了图像来源: I-Hwa Cheng/Cheng Yu-chen/AFP
蒋万安竞选团队也在一份声明中表示，此次选举是“民主体制的具体展现”，并强调“任何外部势力都不应对台湾的民主选举施加政治压力”。
在谈及若当选台北市长，“双城论坛”是否会续办时，沈伯洋表示，只要没有政治前提或“骚扰”，他愿意延续双城论坛，并认为如果自己当选市长，中方可能也正在思考如何处理这项交流机制。
他说：“因为他们仍然需要台北与上海之间某种形式的交流。他们需要这个机制。所以我的假设是，中国还是有这个需求，他们还是需要交流，还是想跟你谈。”
沈伯洋表示，他此次竞选并未刻意聚焦中国议题，因为他参选的是市长而非总统。吸引选民支持的主要原因仍是他推动的民生议题。
他说：“你必须去和过去不支持你的人对话，或是那些在中国问题上与我看法截然不同的人。”

北京香山论坛多国代表对军用人工智能的潜在风险深表担忧。在美中两国准备举行高层会晤之际，武器自主化正急剧压缩决策时间，大国在此类技术管控上的分歧再度引发广泛讨论。

Physicl raises $10M to make the digital world real enough for robots
5:00 AM PST · November 6, 2026
Alex de Vigan’s last business got swamped by the rise of generative AI, but now he’s betting the tech that team had built, a platform for creating tempting product renderings for e-commerce, can be re-purposed to make robots more useful.
His new venture, Physicl, has raised $10 million in seed funding led by Inovia Capital to help world model designers and robot builders solve thorny training problems with more realistic simulations.
Founder and CEO de Vigan spent the last decade building nfinite, which made it easy for brands and retailers to create 3D models of their goods and display them online. The arrival of transformer-based AI models led that company to focus more on generative imagery, but de Vigan saw a new purpose for his team and the tech stack they’d built to faithfully render 3D environments.
“What we were super unique about doing in 3D, AI was going to replace, but something was missing in AI: its ability to understand, interact, and manipulate space and objects,” de Vigan says.
Researchers developing physical AI models to make robots more capable of tasks like handling diverse, small objects have been frustrated by the returns of training them on video, and the expense of gathering data through remote operations.
Simulations in digital worlds are seen as a promising solution, but ensuring that these simulated worlds are faithful to real-world physics has proven difficult. de Vigan believes that the pipeline his previous company built to “transform unstructured, incomplete, heterogeneous real-world information into a high-fidelity physical representation… with correct geometry, materials, and physics” can now be used to make physical AI models more effective.
Physicl is entering a crowded category of startups vying to provide data and tooling to foundation model builders and robot operators. “The space is very young and very blurry sometimes,” de Vigan admits. There are a variety of companies collecting, labeling, or generating data in different modalities as their customers try to figure out the secret sauce that will make robots live up to their promise.
In particular, Physicl wants to focus on post-training models on difficult edge cases. The startup is releasing a product called Studio with 10,000 3D environments and 100,000 assets that represent various objects. It lets users create scenes to generate synthetic data for training robots on specific problems. For example, Studio could be used to generate training data to help a robot that has trouble discerning a cup on a cluttered counter-top, or while the cup is in shadow.
SpAItial, a world model builder, collaborated with Physicl as an early customer to improve the fidelity of its products, the latest of which, Echo-3, was released last week. SpAItial’s tool generates 3D simulations from 2D imagery, and to do that effectively, its CEO and founder Matthias Niessner said they needed to train on the kind of high-fidelity synthetic data Physicl offers.
However, Physicl wants to be more than a data provider; it sees itself as the tooling for ongoing synthetic data generation. “What we created 10 years ago, without knowing it, was basically an agentic workflow to transform unstructured information into high fidelity 3D,” de Vigan said. He imagines customers bringing trillions of images or millions of hours of LIDAR capture data to feed into his platform and turn them into high-quality 3D representations that can be used to generate billions of permutations to train their models.
“The real challenge is, you have to curate the data by hand, and this is a very long cycle,” Niessner, also a professor of robotics at the Technical University of Munich, told TechCrunch. “To us what seems very attractive is you can just do this on the fly […] You’re running Claude, and it checks, ‘Oh, I need more data of this in my training,’ and then it auto generates that data, depending on the training state. That, to me, is super exciting, and this is exactly what Physicl is offering.”

content: 2026年9月初，黃之鋒勾結外國勢力案定罪當天，移居英國的攝影記者 Peter Wong 終於打開電腦硬盤內，拍攝學民思潮的舊照片。 與黃之鋒同年、30歲的Peter是攝影師，也曾是學民思潮成員，他在14年前記錄了學民初始誕生的面貌。那是他攝影的起點，也是黃之鋒一代中學生，投身香港社會運動的起點。14年間，他由一個喜歡拍攝的中學生變成攝影記者；同時間，黃之鋒由一個關心社會、國際知名的中學生踏入30歲，變成國安法下被定罪判囚10年的囚犯。 在黃之鋒被判刑的一天，回望14年前「學民思潮」的橙色直幡，它們烙在菲林與像素之間，留下了近十年香港年輕社運參與者的身影。 請他為這輯影像命名，他回答：「Hi Joshua Wong, I hope you are fine」。 2015年12月4日，我不記得是什麼源起，15年我在大學有一份功課我選擇了跟拍黃子悅，這裡是學民思潮第二個會址。攝影：Peter Wong 一個攝影記者的起點 2012年夏天，中四學生 Peter 在 YouTube 看到另一個中四學生黃之鋒對答如流的 訪問 短片。 短片中，黃之鋒以學民思潮召集人的身份接受訪問，反對政府設立「德育及國民教育科」為中小學必修課。短片在兩日間爆紅，在網絡突破10萬點擊率，也是這一條短片吸引 Peter 加入學民思潮。 「當時社會比較思潮起動，就像『民智初開』，別人是大學生太遠，我才中四，中學生（組織）好像近一點。」他說。 學民思潮最初是由「九十後動員」鍾曉晴、兩名直資中學滙基書院學生黃之鋒與林朗彥，於2011年一起創立的反國民教育學生聯盟。翌年，聯盟簡化名字為學民思潮，連英文名「Scholarism」也是由黃之鋒 造字創立 。 十年後再聚：獄中黃之鋒和一代學民的成長 投放青春參與的社會運動時光愈來愈遠，年輕社運參與者的過去，亦不斷消散解體。在「無」之中，還可以怎樣自處？ 就在這個平台，Peter 遇上黃之鋒，許多政治想法相近的年輕人相遇了。Peter 覺得，當時學民思潮聚集的是一班不被主流教育制度完全擁抱的中學生。 很快，這群中學生行動起來——反國教的學民十區街站，從銅鑼灣鵝頸橋、旺角行人專用區，擺到將軍澳、屯門、荃灣。 Peter 記得，當時學民的氣勢與活動密集程度，就像同時期的立法會選舉。他自嘲參與程度不高，因為他忙著在校內籌組中學學生會、玩口琴，一星期只有兩、三天會隨伙伴一起擺街站。有一次，黃之鋒要上教會，Peter先到對方海怡半島的家，幫忙把傳單與橙色直幡帶去街站。 2012年6月，旺角行人專用區的街站；那時沉迷菲林，應該是一隻過期的Kodak Royal Gold 菲林。攝影：Peter Wong 拿著父母剛買給他的 Nikon 單反相機，Peter 與黃之鋒另一個交集，是拍攝記錄同樣喜歡拍照的黃之鋒。一整個夏天，黃之鋒全情投身了學民思潮，從街站、電台訪問、城市論壇，再到公民廣場的9萬人面前。 鏡頭下的黃之鋒影像逐漸鮮活起來：仍一臉稚氣的黃之鋒在已不復在的立法會示威區鐵馬前與保安對峙；黃之鋒在學民辦公室戴上道具眼鏡玩耍，露出自然的微笑；黃之鋒站在陽光下一邊思考，一邊用力吸啜紙包飲品。 相對於當年傳媒和黃之鋒自己共同建構的學生領袖形象，這些影像顯得新鮮而質樸。14年後重看這些照片，Peter知道這是自己當年有意或無意記錄黃之鋒的起點，「自己如果那時多影一些，現在就會很有用了。」那是初踏政壇、仍沒成年的黃之鋒與同齡朋友相處的畫面，鏡頭錯過了就沒有。 90後一代眼中的可能性 回望過去，人生第一次有自主意識參與社會運動的時刻，對 Peter 仍舊具有重量。 「認識貧富差距算不算？」Peter 在港島屋邨 Band 3中學讀書，中學成績不算好。學民思潮完全突破他的生活圈子與慣常認知：有中學生家住半山區、讀國際學校，後來早早出國升學；也有人家住新界公屋，文憑試後留在香港讀大學。這個中學生組織讓他眼界大開，大至一班人聚在一起談Game Theory，小至一起聽本地獨立樂隊my little airport的音樂，不同原石的光折射進Peter的生活。 2012年，黃之鋒在已停刊的《壹週刊》訪問裡，如此總結他們一代年輕人的想法：「我們沒有目睹八九六四，○三七一時是小學雞。但一場反國教，我們和所有香港人都覺醒。⋯⋯八十後追逐香港社區情懷。但當我們九十後懂性時，香港已沒有什麼餘下。我們沒有背負香港的歷史，我們，是來創造歷史。」 可能性是他們本身，也是2010年代的他們所看見的未來。 2012年暑假的《黑紙》。 數年間，香港社會思潮起動，學民思潮縱然是一些年輕人的起點，但也僅是百家爭鳴時代的其中一家。尤其學民最初為關注單一議題組織，當成功爭取擱置國教科後，成員和義工各自為著升學、理念分歧、甚或組織內的派系不同，決定去或留。有人升讀大學後加入院校學生會成為學聯一份子，有人走向更「本土」的組織，也有人加入社民連，形形式式的選項曾經存在。 雨傘運動前，Peter 也因忙於考試、升學，在2014年7月離開學民思潮。「它作為一個春秋戰國時期，尚且比較自由的時期，就好像『做乜都無事』的時空入面存在。」 之後，Peter 在大學裡學習新聞攝影。他想換一個身份去觀察社會變化與人類的走向。他多年沒有向新認識的人提起自己「學民仔」的身份。 「我也是個普通人，也不認為有title有什麼特別。而我又開始有新的事情要去做。」他說。不僅是他，當時的年輕一代，都各自有事要做。 昔日在學民認識的朋友活躍於社運現場，變成他鏡頭攝下的對象。「黃之鋒」是他大學二年級拍攝人像功課的素材，題目是「參與雨傘運動的學生」。2016年，大學生黃之鋒與部分學民思潮、學聯成員創黨成立「香港眾志」，走入參政路。 在Peter心中，2016年是對香港重要的一年：香港出現主權移交以來的首次「暴動」，首次有立法會參選人被DQ（取消參選資格）。「2016年是承載所有事情的起點。」 當時對攝影記者抱有無限憧憬的Peter開始想像，自己會不會像著名攝影師Pete Souza跟拍奧巴馬8年一樣，能持續追縱一個未來立法會議員的成長？ 2012年9月7日，可能我當日入黑後才到，人很多，我看我硬碟內的相底，只有27張，我不太記得發生了什麼。攝影：Peter Wong 打開封塵記憶 反修例運動後，香港社會經歷大規模的移民潮，Peter的家人決定移民英國。父母問他，我們想移民了，你有沒有什麼打算？Peter 當下近乎不加思索：「去啊，我都去啦。」他覺得，自己不過20來歲，他還想見識一下世界。 倒數離港的那段日子，他仍透過鏡頭追蹤著黃之鋒，直至他入獄，因民主派初選案再次被控。 Peter 最後與黃之鋒有關的攝影工作，是爬上九龍荔枝角的山頭，用長鏡拍攝從收押所走入囚車的黃之鋒。Peter本身有畏高症，但他向公司自薦爬上山頭，拍攝準備上庭的黃之鋒。 由組織到行業，建構身份的一切逐一瓦解，當年的中學生早已離「學生」身份遠遠，各自在新的時空建立自己的腳下未來。 判詞速讀：黃之鋒涉勾結外國勢力罪判囚10年，官指與羅冠聰同屬主腦 如今加控及判刑，黃之鋒須服刑至2036年，出獄時他或約已40歲。 2026年，黃之鋒在獄中面對再多10年以上的監禁。學民思潮的眾人，或散落在旁聽席、法庭，或遠離政治，甚至身處海外。Peter數過當年參加過學民思潮、如今身處英國的人應能坐滿兩桌，而加拿大也應該有7、8人。逐漸在英國紮根的他，放下全職攝影新聞的生活，偶有接案香港新聞的攝影工作。 現實逐漸沖淡了他成為Pete Souza的想像，他也很多年沒有提及自己的中學回憶。「阿叔我都30歲人，也沒理由總是強調自己少時參與學生運動，當年參與也不是很多。」 2012年12月21日，那時人們想說2012會有世界末日，有電影災難片，學民思潮舉行了一個末日倒數街站，那時氣氛比較輕鬆。攝影：Peter Wong 但是，黃之鋒被定罪、被判刑，還是讓他內心泛起漣漪。9月初，他把硬盤內青澀的影像上傳到Instagram。老朋友看後對他說，這是文物庫級別的歷史存檔。 Peter說那不過是成長後透過相片話當年的感覺。學民思潮當年帶給他的震撼與充權的感受很強大，以至往後他當攝影記者時，也會覺得自己已退後一步，是做一個社會觀察，用旁觀者的身份去寫一份紀錄。 30歲的他，在短短的訪問裡不斷形容自己已經是「阿叔」。與2019年投身社會運動的一代相比，他常常自覺是個老人」，重看這批學民舊照，「有種在Wikipedia回望高山大會的感覺。」他說。 （按：高山大會是香港民主派團體在1986年假高山劇場合辦的民主集會，商討香港未來政制） 學民思潮對他而言的意義，是擁有一班一輩子的朋友，即使已經過了10多年，即使彼此不再常見。 圖片故事：學民思潮成人禮 學民思潮停運，即將組成新參政團體，這群90後學生在政治運動中走過怎樣的成人禮？未來又可能給香港政治帶來什麼新想像？ 遙遠的起點與今天的關係，30歲的Peter仍然未有明確的答案。他覺得要不是這次判刑，他也不會打開那些封塵的檔案。「以前的事，我從來也沒有梳理過。當我回看舊時，可能會找到新的東西。」 2012年8月14日，到各政黨詢問對國民教育科獨立成科立場，最近看舊文才回想起，應該大約差不多時間，或再數兩三個星期，學民思潮中真的有組成一個攝影組。攝影：Peter Wong 2012年10月1日清晨，我記得那天很早，這張相片，看相機的時間是7:51，印象中應該是學民思潮首次十月一日示威，應該是港灣道的M記出發。攝影：Peter Wong 2012年9月8日金鐘，佔領政總抗議行動的周末；現在回想有點後悔，那時應該用相機多拍多一點相。攝影：Peter Wong 2012年9月1日，記得那年的開學日應該不是9月1日，是過多一兩日。攝影：Peter Wong 2012年9月3日，廣場上的集會。攝影：Peter Wong 2014年1月29日，維園年宵，學民思潮第一次參與，推出了T恤，好像還有Tote Bag。攝影：Peter Wong 2012年5月27日，六四遊行，這次是我第一次參與學民思潮的活動。攝影：Peter Wong

title: Police say linking mall cameras to AI facial recognition network complies with Hong Kong privacy laws
zh_title: 警方表示，将商场摄像头连接到人工智能面部识别网络符合香港隐私法
summary: 警方表示，为香港的闭路电视网络配备人工智能面部识别软件并将其连接到购物中心的安全摄像头不会违反当地的隐私法。旺角的闭路电视摄像机。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。据当地媒体周五报道，警方表示，人工智能面部识别功能最早将于本月添加到该市的 SmartView 监控系统中，今年将有四家私人购物中心连接到该网络。据了解，这四间商场分别为大角咀奥海城、屯门市广场、葵涌商场及四二商场
content:
警方表示，为香港的闭路电视网络配备人工智能面部识别软件并将其连接到购物中心的安全摄像头不会违反当地的隐私法。旺角的闭路电视摄像机。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。据当地媒体周五报道，警方表示，人工智能面部识别功能最早将于本月添加到该市的 SmartView 监控系统中，今年将有四家私人购物中心连接到该网络。据当地媒体报道，这四家商场分别是大角咀的奥海城、屯门市广场、葵涌商场和粉岭的Sierra Life。警方行动科高级警司梁明亮表示，人工智能面部识别系统不会全天候运行，而是需要督察或以上级别的警官批准。 “我们首先要问的是，使用SmartView对于破案是否至关重要。必须审查多少个摄像头和多少镜头？这个范围是否符合调查目标？在批准任何申请之前，必须解决这些问题，”梁用粤语说。他表示，该技术将通过自动识别嫌疑人或失踪人员的面部是否在特定时间范围内的特定区域被摄像机捕捉到，帮助警察追查嫌疑人或失踪人员。梁补充说，或者，该系统可以实时追踪一个人的脸部，提醒警察他们出现的时间和地点。
闭路电视录像将在捕获后30天自动删除，而时间戳和位置等元数据将保留长达180天。“额外好处”梁还表示，根据警方法律团队和个人资料私隐专员的评估，与购物中心的连接不会违反隐私法。旺角的闭路电视摄像机。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 “这些商场已经配备了安全摄像头，通常与我们的 SmartView 系统具有相同的公共安全目的。连接到它们只是一个额外的好处，”他说。 SmartView项目于2024年启动，截至上个月，已帮助破获2,000起犯罪案件，并逮捕了约2,800名涉嫌谋杀和纵火等罪名的嫌疑人。当局的目标是到 2028 年，通过安装新摄像头并将私人系统和其他政府部门运营的系统连接到警察网络，将全市 60,000 个监控摄像头纳入该系统。 SmartView 第三阶段计划在 2028 年至 2031 年间再安装 6,500 个监控摄像头。

【原文 English Original】
Equipping Hong Kong’s CCTV network with AI facial recognition software and connecting it to shopping mall security cameras would not breach local privacy laws, police have said. A CCTV camera in Mong Kok. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Police have said that the AI facial recognition feature will be added to the city’s SmartView surveillance system as early as this month, with four private shopping malls set to be connected to the network this year, local media reported on Friday. The four malls are understood to be Olympian City in Tai Kok Tsui, Tuen Mun Town Plaza, Kwai Chung Shopping Centre, and Sierra Life in Fanling, local media reported . Leung Ming-leung, a senior superintendent in the police’s Operations Bureau, said the AI facial recognition system would not operate round-the-clock, but would instead require sign-off from an officer ranked inspector or above. “We first ask whether using SmartView is essential to solving the crime. How many cameras and how much footage must be reviewed? Does that scope align with the investigation’s objectives? These points must be settled before any application is approved,” Leung said in Cantonese. He said the technology would help officers track down suspects or missing persons by automatically identifying whether their faces had been caught on camera in a particular area during a specific timeframe. Alternatively, the system could trace an individual’s face in real time, alerting officers to when and where they appear, Leung added. The CCTV footage will be automatically deleted 30 days after capture, while metadata such as timestamps and locations will be retained for up to 180 days. ‘Added bonus’ Leung also said that the connections to shopping malls would not breach privacy laws, based on assessments by the police’s legal team and the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data. A CCTV camera in Mong Kok. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “These malls are already equipped with security cameras, often serving the same public safety purpose as our SmartView system. Linking into them is merely an added bonus,” he said. The SmartView project was launched in 2024 and, as of last month, had helped solve 2,000 crimes and led to the arrest of about 2,800 suspects on charges including murder and arson. Authorities aim to incorporate 60,000 surveillance cameras across the city into the system by 2028, by installing new cameras and linking private systems and those operated by other government departments to the police network. A further 6,500 surveillance cameras are planned between 2028 and 2031 under SmartView’s third phase.

title: Hong Kong installs HK$5m ‘anti-terrorism’ crash bollards outside Causeway Bay dep’t store
zh_title: 香港在铜锣湾百货商店外安装价值 500 万港元的“反恐”防撞柱
summary: 香港当局在香港最繁忙的购物区之一铜锣湾的一家百货公司外安装了“反恐”防撞柱，该项目耗资 500 万港元。 2026 年 11 月 6 日，铜锣湾的“反恐”交通路柱。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周四早上，这些护柱仍被泡沫板包裹着，最初是由警方、运输部和路政部在一月份作为反恐工作组的一部分提出的。 500万港元的临时预算还包括维修费用
content:
香港当局在香港最繁忙的购物区之一铜锣湾的一家百货公司外安装了“反恐”防撞柱，该项目耗资 500 万港元。 2026 年 11 月 6 日，铜锣湾的“反恐”交通路柱。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周四早上，这些护柱仍被泡沫板包裹着，最初是由警方、运输部和路政部在一月份作为反恐工作组的一部分提出的。根据提交给湾仔区议会的一份文件，500万港元的临时预算还包括护柱的维护费用。这些护柱计划安装在轩尼诗道 555 号外和百德新街沿线。 2026 年 11 月 6 日，铜锣湾崇光百货外的“反恐”交通标杆。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。会议记录显示，工作组建议安装60个防撞柱，其中固定式柱43个，伸缩式柱17个。 “护柱之间将留有足够的间距，以便轮椅、婴儿车和担架可以顺利通过，而不会受到阻碍，”它说。警方指出，铜锣湾是港岛区的“核心商业区和旅游区”，人流繁忙，“如果车辆在该地区冲撞人群，可能会造成严重伤亡。” 2026年11月6日，铜锣湾的“反恐”交通路柱。
照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。“通过这些设施，可以采用最直接的物理隔离方法，有效防止车辆故意冲撞行人专用区，从而最大限度地降低人员伤亡的风险。”崇光百货外的区域历史上曾是香港抗议活动的主要聚集区，距离天安门广场镇压守夜活动的旧址维多利亚公园仅一箭之遥。 2026 年 11 月 6 日，铜锣湾崇光百货外的“反恐”交通标杆。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。近年来，在6月4日镇压周年纪念日当天，警察在维多利亚公园和铜锣湾周围保持大量警力，拦截和拘留活动人士和进行象征性哀悼活动的个人。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong authorities have installed “anti-terrorism” collision bollards outside a department store in Causeway Bay, one of the city’s busiest shopping districts – a project with a HK$5 million price tag. “Anti-terrorism” traffic bollards in Causeway Bay on November 6, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The bollards, which were still wrapped in foam sheeting on Thursday morning, were initially proposed in January by the police, the Transport Department, and the Highways Department as part of a counter-terrorism working group. The provisional budget of HK$5 million also includes maintenance costs for the bollards, according to a document submitted to the Wan Chai District Council. The bollards were planned for installation outside 555 Hennessy Road and along Paterson Street. “Anti-terrorism” traffic bollards outside Sogo in Causeway Bay on November 6, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Meeting records show that the working group proposed installing 60 anti-collision bollards, including 43 fixed bollards and 17 retractable ones. “Sufficient spacing would be left between the bollards so that wheelchairs, baby strollers and stretchers could pass through smoothly without being obstructed,” it said. Noting that Causeway Bay is a “core business district and tourist area” on Hong Kong Island with heavy foot traffic, the police said that “[i]f vehicles were to ram into crowds at the location, serious casualties could result.” “Anti-terrorism” traffic bollards in Causeway Bay on November 6, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Through these facilities, the most direct physical separation method could be used to effectively prevent vehicles from deliberately ramming into pedestrian areas, thereby minimising the risk of casualties,” it said. The area outside the Sogo department store historically served as a major gathering zone for protests in Hong Kong, and is a stone’s throw away from Victoria Park, the former site of the city’s Tiananmen Square crackdown vigils. “Anti-terrorism” traffic bollards outside Sogo in Causeway Bay on November 6, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In recent years, police officers have maintained a heavy presence around Victoria Park and Causeway Bay on the anniversary of the crackdown on June 4 , stopping and detaining activists and individuals who engaged in symbolic acts of mourning.

Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

10 月 12 日，在曼谷举行的国际货币基金组织-世界银行年会期间，借款人平台召开了第一次理事会，并确定了第一个年度周期的优先事项。该平台于四月启动，由联合国贸易和发展会议（UNCTAD）作为秘书处，是借款国加强债务管理、协调立场并在全球债务讨论中发出更强有力的集体声音的论坛。一些发展中国家已经正式加入，还有更多国家已受邀参加。
曼谷会议的主题是与西亚战争有关的能源供应冲击，该冲击与利率上升和公共债务一起达到了二战以来的最高水平。发展中国家今年面临着向外部债权人支付约 4000 亿美元的款项。
在这些头条新闻的背后，亚洲的发展融资正在发生微妙的转变。中国是2010年代该地区最具活力的贷款国，现在从发展中国家收取的资金多于放出的贷款，而世界银行和亚洲开发银行（亚行）已成为更重要的新资金来源。亚洲债务外交的下一阶段将不仅取决于谁提供新资本，还取决于借款国如何协调债权人谈判、管理净资金流动以及为未来发展保留财政空间。
中国“一带一路”倡议的算术已经发生转变。 2010 年代中期贷款热潮期间收缩的贷款（通常有三到五年的宽限期）现在已进入还款阶段。事实上，数据显示，2024年，中国对发展中国家的净流入下降至负340亿美元，中国净流入的国家数量从2012年的18个增加到2023年的60个。仅2025年，发展中国家预计将向北京支付约350亿美元的偿债。
与此同时，多边贷款机构正在增加贷款。根据世界银行《2025年国际债务报告》，其流向低收入和中等收入国家的净流量在2024年达到创纪录的约360亿美元，其中多边债权人提供了全部长期净融资的近一半。相比之下，双边净流量降至约 45 亿美元，为全球金融危机以来的最低水平。
中国尚未退出贷款领域。北京继续展期到期贷款，延长互换额度，并推迟对其风险最大的合作伙伴的还款。但其参与的性质已经从绿地项目融资转变为流动性管理，让借款人保持最新状态，而不是扩大他们的投资领域。

On October 12, on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, the Borrowers’ Platform held its first Governing Council and set out priorities for its first annual cycle. Launched in April with U.N. Trade and Development (UNCTAD) as its secretariat, the platform is a forum for borrowing countries to strengthen debt management, coordinate positions, and speak with a stronger collective voice in global debt discussions. Several developing countries have already formally joined, and many more have been invited to participate.
The Bangkok meetings were dominated by an energy supply shock linked to the war in West Asia, which has landed alongside rising interest rates and public debt at its highest level since World War II. Developing countries are facing some $400 billion in payments to external creditors this year.
Beneath these headlines, a subtler shift is underway in Asia’s development finance. China, the region’s most dynamic lender in the 2010s, now collects more from developing countries than it lends, while the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) have become more important sources of new money. The next phase of Asia’s debt diplomacy will be shaped not merely by who supplies fresh capital, but by how borrowing countries coordinate creditor negotiations, manage net financial flows, and preserve fiscal space for future development.
The arithmetic of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) has turned. Loans contracted during the lending boom of the mid-2010s, typically with grace periods of three to five years, have now entered their repayment phase. In fact, data show that China’s net flows to developing countries fell to negative $34 billion in 2024, and the number of countries for which China was a net drain rose from 18 in 2012 to 60 in 2023. In 2025 alone, developing countries were expected to pay an estimated $35 billion in debt service to Beijing.
Multilateral lenders, meanwhile, are lending more. According to the World Bank’s International Debt Report 2025, its own net flows to low- and middle-income countries reached a record of about $36 billion in 2024, with multilateral creditors providing nearly half of all long-term net financing. Bilateral net flows, by contrast, fell to about $4.5 billion, the lowest since the global financial crisis.
China has not exited the loan landscape. Beijing continues to roll over maturing loans, extend swap lines, and defer repayments for its most exposed partners. But the character of its engagement has changed from greenfield project finance toward liquidity management, keeping borrowers current rather than expanding their investment frontier.
This change can be seen playing out in Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Laos – three economies with deep BRI exposure, where multilateral finance increasingly sits alongside, and is shaped by, legacy Chinese obligations.
In Pakistan, the fiscal calendar is dominated by repayments. In July 2026, Islamabad paid $1.3 billion in Chinese commercial loans used to fund CPEC projects. Pakistan’s government has asked Beijing to fast-track the refinancing of this debt. During the current fiscal year, Pakistan will need about $12 billion in rollovers from China and Saudi Arabia.
At the same time, the World Bank has committed to a 10-year partnership with Pakistan, envisaging about $20 billion in financing over 2026-35. The most telling case is the modernization of the Main Line-1 railway from Karachi to Peshawar, long described as a flagship project of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor. After years of negotiations failed to produce a Chinese concessional package, its Karachi-Rohri section is now set to begin with proposed ADB financing of $1.1 billion, a sequencing the government says was agreed with Beijing.
Sri Lanka, which signed agreements in June 2024 to restructure about $4.2 billion owed to China’s Export-Import Bank, now relies heavily on multilateral liquidity. In 2025, the IMF and ADB together provided nearly 80 percent of the roughly $1.48 billion in foreign development financing disbursed to Colombo, and the ADB has since raised its 2026 allocation to US$480 million following Cyclone Ditwah.
Laos illustrates the other extreme: continued reliance on Chinese lending. Rather than restructure its debt, since 2020 Vientiane has relied on repeated deferrals from Beijing that total $3.23 billion, about 19 percent of its GDP. The World Bank projects Lao debt service will equate to 13 percent of GDP in 2026, a fiscal burden that directly limits spending on health, education, and social protection.
Multilateral loans are earmarked for railways, social protection, or disaster recovery, but money is fungible at the level of the budget and the balance of payments. Every dollar that a development bank finances frees up a dollar of domestic revenue or foreign reserves that can be used to service bilateral debt. Fresh multilateral finance may therefore be expanding investment capacity on paper while, in practice, buying fiscal breathing room to meet legacy Chinese obligations.
A more diverse creditor base can strengthen a borrower’s hand, since multilateral lending brings concessional terms, competitive procurement, and greater transparency, and credible alternatives are themselves a source of leverage when negotiating with several creditors at once. Yet the shift carries costs of its own.
Multilateral finance comes with policy conditions, and because multilateral development banks enjoy preferred creditor status, their loans are effectively excluded from restructuring. As their share of the debt stock rises, more of a country’s debt becomes non-negotiable, and any future crisis would weigh more heavily on the remaining bilateral and private creditors. If multilateral resources are also seen to be financing repayments to another official creditor, shareholder support for continued lending could become harder to sustain. Asian borrowers could thus exchange one form of dependence for another, with less room to maneuver in the next downturn.
This is where the Borrowers’ Platform could add value, mainly through technical cooperation rather than collective bargaining. For instance, Sri Lanka’s experience of negotiating in parallel with an official creditor committee, China, and bondholders is precisely the kind of institutional knowledge that Laos or Pakistan could use. Members could also share approaches to tracking net flows by creditor, sequencing refinancing to avoid repayment cliffs, and adopting debt pause clauses that suspend payments during climate disasters and other crises.
In this setting, the central question is no longer simply whether Beijing or the development banks will finance Asia’s next decade, but whether borrowing countries can manage the transition on their own terms. The post-BRI era will therefore reward governments that track net flows rather than headline pledges and, most importantly, protect space for development spending.

（德国之声中文网）美国国务院周四宣布的这轮新制裁，目标涵盖了古巴的石油和电子行业。
制裁名单中首次包括了两家中国企业，美方指控它们向古巴军方提供了电子产品及其他安全设备。
中国外交部对此表示强烈反对，称这些制裁是非法的，属于典型的“长臂管辖”。
中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆在新闻发布会上表示：“中方坚决反对美方干涉和破坏中古合作。”
他警告称，北京将采取“一切必要措施”来维护本国企业的权益。
自1月以来，华盛顿对古巴实施了破坏力极强的新制裁及石油封锁，导致古巴经济陷入瘫痪，并引发了大范围停电和生活必需品短缺。
美国总统特朗普曾暗示可能采取军事干预，以推翻古巴执政的共产党。上个月，美国国务卿还敦促古巴民众与美国情报机构开展合作。
周四被列入制裁名单的中国企业包括国有企业中国电子进出口总公司（CEIEC），以及民营企业北京华成昊普科技有限公司（Beijing H&C Technologies）。
制裁名单还涵盖了安妮·罗德里格斯·拉斯特雷斯（Any Rodriguez Lastres），她是古巴最大军方控股商业集团古巴企业管理集团（GAESA）负责人之女。

香港和广东省表彰 MiMEP 高效建筑奖得主 |中国劳工公告栏
星期六, 7 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港和广东颁授 MiMEP 高效建筑奖得主
香港机电工程署和建筑署于 11 月 6 日颁发 MiMEP 奖项。比赛共吸引了来自大湾区的80余份参赛作品，最终产生52名优胜者，其中包括大型医疗设施、医疗设备等项目的四项顶级“无限奖”。
香港特别行政区政府机电工程署（机电工程署）和建筑署于11月6日颁发奖项，以推广在建造中使用模块化机电水管一体化系统（MiMEP）。
发展局副局长林志文在仪式上致辞时表示，大赛为香港及粤港澳大湾区业界提供了一个互相学习、探讨MiMEP未来发展的平台。他指出，发展局今年已发出工务技术通告，要求在合适的工务项目中采用MiMEP。他补充说，明年，该局将与内地当局合作，为MiMEP发布跨境贸易指南，以促进跨境发展。政府将继续通过政策引导、技术推广和人才培训推动MiMEP的广泛应用。
住建厅二级巡视员郭建华表示，她很高兴见证MiMEP为大湾区带来的新生产力和创新成果。她表示，希望粤港两地进一步深化科技创新和产业建设合作，共同推动大湾区MiMEP产业链协调发展。
竞赛设有四个主要奖项类别——新建项目、在建项目、翻新和加建工程以及工厂和制造商——以及三个特别奖项类别。共收到来自大湾区各城市的80余份参赛作品。评审团评选出52支获奖队伍，其中4支队伍荣获最高荣誉“无限奖”，项目涉及大湾区大型医疗设施、重点商业地标、政府建筑节能改造、先进制造业等。

Saturday, 7 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong and Guangdong honour MiMEP award winners for efficient construction
Hong Kong's Electrical and Mechanical Services Department and Architectural Services Department presented MiMEP awards on 6 November. The competition drew over 80 entries from the Greater Bay Area, with 52 winners including four top 'Infinity Awards' for projects such as large medical facilities and
The Electrical and Mechanical Services Department (EMSD) and the Architectural Services Department of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government presented awards on 6 November to promote the use of Modular Integrated Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing (MiMEP) in construction.
Speaking at the ceremony, Deputy Director of the Development Bureau Lin Zhiwen said the competition provided a platform for industry players from Hong Kong and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (Greater Bay Area) to learn from each other and explore the future development of MiMEP. He noted that the Development Bureau had issued a public works technical circular this year requiring the adoption of MiMEP in suitable public works projects. Next year, he added, the bureau would work with mainland authorities to publish a cross-border trade guide for MiMEP to facilitate cross-boundary development. The government would continue to promote wider use of MiMEP through policy guidance, technology promotion and talent training.
Guo Jianhua, a second-level inspector from the Housing Construction Department, said she was pleased to witness the new productivity and innovative outcomes MiMEP had brought to the Greater Bay Area. She expressed hope that Guangdong and Hong Kong would further deepen technological innovation and industrial collaboration in construction to jointly drive the coordinated development of the MiMEP industrial chain in the Greater Bay Area.
The competition featured four main award categories – new construction projects, projects under construction, renovation and addition works, and factories and manufacturers – and three special award categories. It received more than 80 entries from cities across the Greater Bay Area. The judging panel selected 52 winning teams, of which four received the top honour, the 'Infinity Award', for projects including large medical facilities, key commercial landmarks, energy-saving retrofits of government buildings and advanced manufacturing in the Greater Bay Area.

第四届融合发展法治论坛于11月5日举行，由中央人民政府驻香港联络办公室法律部支持、律政司及外交部驻香港特派员公署协办。中联办副主任袁古杰、外交部办公厅特派员崔建春致欢迎辞。外交部参赞王晨、高等法院首席法官潘伟强分别发表主旨演讲。论坛设有两场小组讨论，探讨香港作为综合性国际争议解决中心的角色及其在国家涉外法治发展中的作用。
第二届粤港澳大湾区律师论坛于11月6日圆满结束，论坛主题为“湾区法律智慧——融合融合”。司法部领导王利民致开幕辞并作支持港澳法律工作者服务国家法治建设的主旨演讲。律政司司长陈家祥，高级大律师；陈旭东 广东省司法厅厅长；澳门特别行政区政府行政法务司司长办公室主任曾翔分别致开幕辞。
陈先生表示，大湾区具有“一国、两种制度、三种司法管辖区”的特点，双师律师是化差异为优势的先行者。大湾区律师制度9月常态化，700多名港澳法律执业者取得执业资格。陈肇始鼓励香港法律人才报考，称这是香港特区政府第一个五年计划的目标。
粤港澳大湾区律师协会、香港律师会、香港大律师公会代表就律师制度正规化、法律人才整合、香港律师在争议解决中的作用等问题分享了见解。以“大湾区律师跨境企业发展的实践与新机遇”为主题的圆桌论坛，汇聚了顶尖律师，探讨双资格律师如何利用大湾区在跨境商事诉讼、法律科技和绿色金融方面的独特优势，帮助内地企业拓展全球业务。
下午的环节，来自香港、内地、澳门的调解员齐聚一堂，利用《粤港澳大湾区跨境纠纷调解示范规则》进行模拟调解，展示了规则的实际运用。

Saturday, 7 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong Legal Week 2026 concludes with focus on Greater Bay Area integration
Hong Kong Legal Week 2026 ended on 6 November with forums on cross-border dispute resolution and the Greater Bay Area lawyer scheme. More than 700 lawyers have obtained dual-qualification status under a regularised system that took effect in September. A new government task force will accelerate rul
6 Nov 2026 at 20:58 HKT · updated 6 Nov, 21:19 · 3 min read
The fourth edition of the Integration and Development Rule of Law Forum was held on 5 November, supported by the Legal Affairs Department of the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in Hong Kong, and co-organised by the Department of Justice and the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Hong Kong. Yuan Gujie, deputy director of the Liaison Office, and Cui Jianchun, commissioner of the foreign ministry office, delivered welcome addresses. Wang Chen, counsellor of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Justice Patrick Poon, Chief Judge of the High Court, gave keynote speeches. The forum featured two panel discussions examining Hong Kong's role as a comprehensive international dispute resolution hub and its part in the nation's foreign-related rule-of-law development.
The second Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area Lawyers Forum concluded the week on 6 November, under the theme 'Legal Wisdom Bay Area – Convergence and Integration'. Wang Limin, a leading official of the Ministry of Justice, delivered the opening address and keynote on supporting Hong Kong and Macau legal professionals in serving national rule-of-law construction. Secretary for Justice Eric Chan, Senior Counsel; Chen Xudong, director of the Guangdong Provincial Department of Justice; and Zeng Xiang, head of the Office of the Secretary for Administration and Justice of the Macau SAR government, each gave opening remarks.
Chan said the Greater Bay Area features 'one country, two systems, three legal jurisdictions' and that dually qualified lawyers are the pioneers turning differences into advantages. The Greater Bay Area lawyer scheme was regularised in September, and more than 700 Hong Kong and Macau legal practitioners have obtained practising qualifications. Chan encouraged Hong Kong legal talents to sit for the examination, calling it a target of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government's First Five-Year Plan.
Representatives of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area Lawyers Association, the Law Society of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Bar Association shared insights on the regularisation of the lawyer scheme, the integration of legal talent, and the role of Hong Kong practitioners in dispute resolution. A panel titled 'Practices and New Opportunities for Greater Bay Area Lawyers in Cross-border Corporate Development' featured top lawyers discussing how dually qualified practitioners can leverage the region's unique advantages in cross-border commercial litigation, legal technology and green finance to help mainland enterprises expand globally.
An afternoon session brought together mediators from Hong Kong, the mainland and Macau for a simulated mediation using the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area Cross-border Dispute Mediation Model Rules, demonstrating practical application of rules alignment. Deputy Secretary for Justice Dr Thomas Cheung delivered closing remarks, announcing that the 2026 Policy Address had established a task force to accelerate rules and mechanisms alignment across the three jurisdictions. Cheung said the target is to formally set up the task force early next year, begin research and consultation with stakeholders, and compile a list of items for alignment work with the mainland.
The First Five-Year Plan of Hong Kong aligns with the national 15th Five-Year Plan and proposes better use of the common-law advantages under 'one country, two systems' to improve diversified, high-level dispute resolution services including litigation, arbitration and mediation. The Department of Justice will continue organising events to promote exchanges and cooperation among legal professionals from Hong Kong, the mainland and other jurisdictions on international dispute resolution, foreign-related rule of law and legal technology.

星期六, 7 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港海关从入境旅客身上检获481支未税香烟
10月31日，一名68岁香港男子在落马洲管制站被海关人员发现481支未税香烟，被判入狱。海关对这一判决表示欢迎，并警告公众不要走私漏税香烟。
2026 年 11 月 6 日 18:35 香港时间 · 更新于 11 月 6 日 19:19 · 阅读时间 1 分钟
香港海关人员于10月31日在落马洲管制站截查一名68岁本地男性旅客，并从其身上检获481支未税香烟。该批香烟估计市值约为2,400港元，应缴税款约为1,600港元。该男子立即被捕。
海关在11月6日的一份声明中表示，对法庭的判决表示欢迎，指出监禁具有重大威慑作用，反映了罪行的严重性。它呼吁公众不要违法。
根据香港相关条例，香烟属于应课税品。任何人进口、处理、拥有、出售或购买非法香烟即属犯罪。一经定罪，最高刑罚为罚款港币 200 万元及监禁七年。
海关提醒市民，可透过24小时热线182 8080、专用电邮帐户[email protected]或网上表格eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002举报怀疑私烟活动。

Saturday, 7 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong Customs seize 481 untaxed cigarettes from arriving passenger
A 68-year-old Hong Kong man was sentenced to jail after Customs officers found 481 untaxed cigarettes on him at Lok Ma Chau Control Point on 31 October. Customs welcomed the sentence, warning the public against smuggling duty-not-paid cigarettes.
6 Nov 2026 at 18:35 HKT · updated 6 Nov, 19:19 · 1 min read
Hong Kong Customs officers intercepted a 68-year-old local male passenger at the Lok Ma Chau Control Point on 31 October and seized 481 untaxed cigarettes from his person. The cigarettes have an estimated market value of about HK$2,400, with duty payable of approximately HK$1,600. The man was immediately arrested.
Customs said in a statement on 6 November that it welcomed the court's sentencing, noting that the jail term serves as a significant deterrent and reflects the seriousness of the offence. It urged the public not to break the law.
Under Hong Kong's relevant ordinance, cigarettes are dutiable goods. Any person who imports, handles, possesses, sells or purchases illicit cigarettes commits an offence. Upon conviction, the maximum penalty is a fine of HK$2 million and imprisonment for seven years.
Customs reminded the public to report suspected illicit cigarette activities via its 24-hour hotline 182 8080, the dedicated email account [email protected], or the online form at eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002.

民主党大胜冲击AI前景 全球股市一天蒸发3.5兆美元
原文链接www.cna.com.tw/news/afe/202611060340.aspx
（中央社记者戴雅真东京6日专电）美国民主党在期中选举大获全胜，市场忧心数据中心建设将面临更严格监管，冲击人工智能（AI）产业投资前景，引发全球AI及半导体类股抛售潮。全球股市市值一天内蒸发3.5兆美元（约550兆日圆、新台币115兆元），日本、台湾及韩国股市也遭受重创。
日本经济新闻报导，根据QUICK FactSet统计，截至5日，全球股市总市值降至154兆美元，较前一天减少3.5兆美元。日本东京证券交易所Prime市场今天也蒸发77兆日圆市值，显示AI概念股卖压已从美国蔓延至亚洲市场。
美国股市5日全面重挫，以科技股为主的那斯达克综合指数下跌5.5%，其中AI及半导体类股成为重灾区。由英伟达（NVIDIA）、美光科技等主要半导体企业组成的费城半导体指数（SOX）暴跌12.2%。
日本股市今天同样遭遇猛烈卖压。日经平均指数终场下跌3643点，跌幅近6%，收在57434点，不仅跌破6万点大关，也创下7个月以来新低。单日下跌点数仅次于2024年8月股灾及1987年「黑色星期一」，为史上第3大跌点。
高盛证券副总裁石桥隆行形容，「与过去股市下跌时不同，这次市场看不到能让股价迅速反弹的利多因素，投资人之间弥漫着某种近乎放弃的情绪。」
市场分析认为，这波全球AI概念股暴跌的导火线，是美国3日举行的期中选举。民主党不仅取得参众两院过半席次，也在德州等州长选举中胜出。由于民主党主张加强数据中心监管，市场开始担忧，AI产业不可或缺的数据中心建设计划可能遭到延后，甚至停摆。
过去几年，AI概念股持续上涨，主要创建在人工智能市场快速扩张，以及企业将不断增加数据中心和半导体投资的预期之上。然而，随着美国政治局势出现变化，数据中心开发面临监管风险，原本支撑AI股高估值的投资扩张前景也开始动摇。
景顺资产管理全球市场策略师木下智夫指出，一旦数据中心投资受到限制，半导体等整个AI供应链都将直接受到冲击。由于过去AI相关股票是在市场近乎狂热的气氛下持续上涨，一旦投资人转向抛售，跌势也容易迅速扩大。
自美国OpenAI于2022年11月推出ChatGPT以来，全球股市总市值已膨胀至当时的1.6倍。过去，投资资金持续涌入AI相关企业，是创建在AI需求将不断成长的假设之上。
不过，随着美国数据中心建设可能面临更严格监管，市场开始重新评估AI产业未来的投资规模与成长速度。这波全球科技股抛售潮，也凸显AI投资热潮在高度依赖基础设施持续扩张的情况下，容易受到政策变化冲击。

content:
香港：人权组织谴责对黄之锋的不公正判决 zevans@freedom… 星期四，11/05/2026 - 15:23 输入联合声明 国家香港页面屏蔽 我们，以下签名组织，谴责香港高等法院 11 月 5 日对香港民主倡导者黄之锋判处 10 年徒刑。这是他第二次根据北京实施的国家安全法被判刑，该法导致香港的基本自由迅速恶化。三周前，约书亚在监狱里度过了自己的 30 岁生日，十几岁时，他作为学生团体学民思潮的联合创始人而声名鹊起，该团体反对将亲北京的宣传引入香港学校。他帮助领导了 2014 年历史性的雨伞运动，并于 2016 年创建了亲民主的众志党，该党在 2020 年《国家安全法》获得批准后被迫解散。他因其民主行动主义而获得国际赞誉，包括多次获得诺贝尔和平奖提名。由于这种宣传，约书亚一再入狱，自2020年11月以来一直被拘留。2024年，他因参加第一次也是唯一一次全市民主初选而被以阴谋颠覆罪判处四年零八个月监禁。
他预计将于 2027 年 1 月获释，但在 2025 年 6 月面临额外指控，罪名是因之前的活动而与外国势力合谋。 作为这些指控的一部分，检察官提到了约书亚与美国政府官员（包括当时的参议员马可·卢比奥）的会面。这是中国共产党一系列令人担忧的尝试之一，不仅限制和控制中国公民和香港人可以会见哪些人，还限制和控制外国政府官员可以联系谁以及他们可以收到哪些信息。此外，北京支持的香港政府强烈劝阻居民观看并考虑对获奖纪录片《约书亚：青少年与超级大国》采取进一步行动，该片记录了约书亚早期的活动，进一步表明其压制香港民主运动独立报道的努力。约书亚的拘留也凸显了中共如何继续藐视《中英联合声明》。该条约是 1997 年香港主权移交过程​​中谈判达成的，其中规定了“一国两种制度”的原则，该原则本应持续到 2047 年。中共对这一原则的漠视——约书亚因行使基本自由而被拘留就证明了这一点——令人质疑中共在贸易或其他问题上谈判达成的协议是否会得到遵守。
我们呼吁香港当局立即无条件释放约书亚，并要求民主政府更有力地要求释放他。具体来说，我们要求白宫和国务院承诺在唐纳德·特朗普总统和中国领导人习近平即将举行的双边会议上提出约书亚的案件并呼吁释放他，特别是在我们即将于11月在深圳举行的亚太经合组织（APEC）会议和12月在佛罗里达州举行的20国集团（G20）峰会之际。特朗普政府在优先释放世界各地政治犯方面做了值得称赞的工作。政治犯金明日牧师从中国拘留所获释

Hong Kong: Human Rights Organizations Condemn Unjust Sentencing of Joshua Wong zevans@freedom… Thu, 11/05/2026 - 15:23 Type Joint Statement Countries Hong Kong Page blocks We, the undersigned organizations, condemn the November 5th sentencing of Hong Kong prodemocracy advocate Joshua Wong to a 10-year sentence by the Hong Kong High Court. This is the second time he has been sentenced under the Beijing-imposed National Security Law (NSL), which has contributed to the rapid deterioration of basic freedoms in Hong Kong. Joshua, who marked his 30th birthday in prison three weeks ago, rose to prominence as a teenager as the cofounder of the student group Scholarism, which opposed the introduction of pro-Beijing propaganda into Hong Kong's schools. He helped lead the historic 2014 Umbrella Movement and in 2016 created the prodemocracy Demosistō party, which was forced to disband after the approval of the NSL in 2020. He has received international acclaim for his democratic activism, including multiple nominations for the Nobel Peace Prize. As a result of this advocacy, Joshua has been repeatedly imprisoned, and has been detained continuously since November 2020. In 2024, he was sentenced to four years and eight months’ imprisonment on charges of conspiracy to commit subversion in connection with him taking part in the first and only city-wide democratic primary. He was expected to be released in January 2027, but faced additional charges in June 2025 of conspiring to collude with foreign forces for his earlier activism. As part of these charges, prosecutors referred to meetings that Joshua had with US government officials, including then Senator Marco Rubio. This is among a worrying series of attempts by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) to restrict and control not only who Chinese citizens and Hong Kongers may meet, but also who foreign government officials may contact and what information they can receive. Additionally, the Beijing-backed Hong Kong government is strongly discouraging residents from viewing and considering further action on the award-winning documentary Joshua: Teenager vs. Superpower, which chronicles Joshua's early activism, further demonstrating its efforts to suppress independent accounts of Hong Kong's prodemocracy movement. Joshua's detention also highlights how the CCP continues to flout the Sino-British Joint Declaration. That treaty, negotiated as part of Hong Kong's 1997 handover, enshrines the "one country, two systems" principle that was supposed to prevail until 2047. The CCP's disregard for that principle—demonstrated by Joshua's detention for exercising his fundamental freedoms—calls into question whether deals the CCP negotiates on trade or other issues will be honored. We call on Hong Kong authorities to release Joshua immediately and unconditionally, and we ask that democratic governments more forcefully demand his release. Specifically, we request that the White House and the State Department commit to raising Joshua’s case and calling for his release in the upcoming bilateral meetings between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, particularly as we look to the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in November in Shenzhen, and the Group of 20 (G20) Summit in Florida in December. The Trump administration has done a commendable job prioritizing the release of political prisoners around the world. The release of political prisoner Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri from detention in China earlier this year demonstrates that when the president of the United States intervenes directly, it can make a real, lifesaving difference. content: ——从我的牢狱经历看权力与良心 【大纪元2026年11月02日讯】1990年，我因参加1989年中国民主运动被捕入狱。 在看守所里，我不止一次听见警察对我说：“我是执行公务。”“这是上级命令。”“领导让我干的，我也没有办法。” 说这些话的，不是一个人。我渐渐听出另一层意思：事情做得对不对，出了什么后果，都不该由他们负责。 我一直想问：你没有自己的思想吗？ 一个人穿上制服，就不再有感情、不再能够分辨是非了吗？他知道什么是痛苦，也不愿意自己的家人受到羞辱和伤害，为什么面对别人时，却可以把判断完全交给上级？ 我不认为每个人都有能力违抗命令。但我的亲身经历告诉我，即使身处同样的环境，人仍然可能作出不同选择。 被关进看守所后，我连续多日喊冤。后来，所长把我叫进办公室，给我倒了一杯水。他说，看过我的案卷，觉得案件可能存在问题，但自己没有权力放人。 “我就是一个仓库保管员，”他说，“看守所就是仓库，我的责任是把你们像物品一样保管好。”他还说，如果擅自放我出去，自己就得进牢房。 我听得很难受。一个活生生的人，竟被比作仓库里的物品。但我也记住了那杯水。他不能释放我，却可以不羞辱我。 还有一名审讯人员，见我始终不愿回答问题，后来对我说：“王立君，我也要吃饭，这是我的工作，领导派我来的。”他告诉我，想说就说，不想说可以不说，还问我饿不饿，提出给我买点吃的和水。 他没有改变我的处境，却没有把逼迫我当成非完成不可的任务。同样是执行公务，有人选威胁，有人选克制。职务限制了一个人能动用的权力，却没有取消他的判断。 1990年，我的父母到十堰市张湾区法院了解我的案件。事后他们告诉我，法院一名负责人曾劝我所在学校把我接回去，认为我的问题没有那么严重。但学校领导拒绝了。 父母转述，那位领导说：“王立君口才又好，又有文化，他要回来了，我们的日子怎么过？” 学校的态度是不是直接决定了判决，我不能断定。可这句话，我记了几十年。学校本来是教书育人的地方，为什么不能为一个受到政治调查的人争取一点保护？ 1991年出狱以后，我曾在法院附近遇见当年审理我案件的一位法官。律师问起我的案件，他说：“那是上边定了嘛！我有那个权力吗？” 可他后来又告诉我，如果将来政策改变，我可以找他，他愿意帮助我平反，争取国家赔偿。 我不知道他当时究竟受到怎样的干预，也不知道他有多大的决定权。可司法责任，不能靠一句“上边定了”就解释完。一个案子是不是依法审的，法官做过什么、能做什么，总要接受事实的检验。 那些年，也有人在危险中帮助我。被捕以前，童老师曾悄悄提醒我，公安机关可能准备抓我。后来我被秘密关押，家人不知道我的下落。我借到医院检查的机会，请护士联系童老师。他的妻子赶到医院，悄悄答应替我通知家人，还给了我三十元钱。 他们手里没有什么权力，却愿意帮一个困境中的人。这件事让我明白，看一个人，不能只看他处在什么制度里，还要看在他能自己作主的事情上，他做了什么。 多年以后，我又从王作训那里听到一件事。据我记忆，王作训曾任地矿部外事司司长，与1989年经常出现在新闻媒体上的政府发言人袁木住在同一个干部家属区。 王作训亲口告诉我，六四以后，他经常在院子里见到袁木。有人拿袁木当年关于天安门广场有没有开枪的公开说法讽刺他。袁木往往低着头，没有回答。 我没有亲眼见到这个场景，也不知道袁木当时心里在想什么。但它让我想到：一个人离开话筒以后，他说过的话不会因此消失。 警察脱下制服，法官离开法庭，政府发言人走下讲台，他们仍然要面对别人对自己行为的评价。 我还记得一个与我被捕有关的人。多年以后，他曾请求我不要公开当年的事情，担心一旦别人知道，自己就无法做人了。 我不知道他当年承受了怎样的压力，但他的请求说明，至少他十分在意别人会怎样看待那段往事。权力能够影响一个人的命运，却不能保证掌权者永远不必面对历史的追问。 当然，历史责任不能只凭愤怒来认定。下达命令的人、受到胁迫的人、主动扩大伤害的人，其行为和责任应当分别调查。法律责任更需要依据事实、证据和适用法律判断。 我反对的是把“执行公务”当作任意滥用权力的理由，把“服从命令”当作所有行为都无需负责的借口。 我写下这些，不是为了羞辱谁，更不是要求以报复代替法律。我希望历史档案能够公开，证人能够自由讲述，受害者得到公正对待，被指控者也有机会作出解释。 我永远记得那个给我倒水的所长，也记得童老师夫妇的帮助。他们让我看到，即使在艰难的环境里，一个人仍然可以保留善良。 三十多年过去，我越来越相信：制服可以脱下，职务会结束，命令也有停止的一天。可一个人作过的选择，不会跟着从历史里消失。 执行公务，不是滥用权力的许可证；服从命令，也不能自动免掉一个人的责任。 （ 作者简介：王立君，独立记者、自由撰稿人。曾在大学任教，高级工程师职称。因支持1989年学生民主运动被捕入狱，狱中遭受酷刑。此后信仰基督教，立足亲身经历写作，揭露教育腐败、司法不公、权力滥用与宗教迫害，呼吁社会正义、法治与人的尊严。作品发表于《北京之春》《在野党》《大纪元》《希望之声》等媒体。 ）

title: US Air Force eyes reviving WWII air bases in the Pacific
zh_title: 美国空军着眼于复兴太平洋地区的二战空军基地
summary: 据美国空军部发布的公告称，美国空军希望每年在西北太平洋三个美国岛屿上的四个机场执行超过 6000 架次的飞机行动，其中包括一个正在翻新的二战时期主要机场。该部门发布了一份准备环境影响报告的意向通知，该报告将评估塞班国际机场、天宁岛国际机场、天宁岛北机场和罗塔国际机场的培训和运营的“潜在社会、经济和环境影响”。岛屿
content:
据美国空军部发布的公告称，美国空军希望每年在西北太平洋三个美国岛屿上的四个机场执行超过 6000 架次的飞机行动，其中包括一个正在翻新的二战时期主要机场。该部门发布了一份准备环境影响报告的意向通知，该报告将评估塞班国际机场、天宁岛国际机场、天宁岛北机场和罗塔国际机场的培训和运营的“潜在社会、经济和环境影响”。这些岛屿是北马里亚纳群岛联邦的一部分，是美国的非建制领土。拟议的训练和演习将支持空军的敏捷作战作战概念，该概念强调部队在机场之间的分散以及在各种条件下维持作战的同时在机场之间进行机动的能力，目的是挫败对手通过瞄准单个基地来关闭这些作战的能力。众所周知，ACE 的发展很大程度上是为了应对中国军队不断扩大的影响力和不断扩大的导弹库。
通知称，这四个机场为支持 ACE 提供了“独特的机会”，其基础设施从“完全开发的商业机场到远征作战地点”各不相同。这三个岛屿彼此相距不到几十海里，这将允许进行反映分布式行动复杂性的训练，同时减少它们之间的运输时间。它们距离美国另一个领土关岛的主要军事基地以北不到100海里，该基地将为这些演习提供部队的集结和部署。通知中写道，这三个机场“共同提供了一个训练环境，使[空军]能够进行分布式作战、测试和使用可定制的部队包、加强保障和机动能力以及增强作战弹性”。环境影响报告将评估拟议活动的潜在影响，其中包括每年举行几次、每次为期几周的小型、中型和大型训练和演习，包括每年在每个机场进行多达 1,200 次固定翼和 320 次旋转翼操作，例如起飞和着陆。
它还将评估替代方案，即每个机场每年最多进行 1,400 次固定翼飞机和 384 次旋转翼飞机运行，以及“无行动替代方案”。训练和演习将由每个机场最多 550,000 加仑的燃料、每个机场最多 1,000 名人员、远征基础设施的临时安装、箔条和照明弹等弹药的处理以及支持服务以及训练和演习前后的活动提供支持。拟议的活动是在经过数年的升级相关机场的工作之后进行的，特别是天宁岛的机场，这些机场是在第二次世界大战。北机场在战后处于闲置状态，在 2023 年底开始修复工作时，大部分被植被覆盖。空军还升级了港口和道路基础设施、燃料管道和机场表面以及公用设施，以促进天宁岛的扩大行动。机场修复工作引起了空军领导人对资源和资金的一些疑问，特别是在与伊朗的战争提出了新的要求的情况下

【原文 English Original】
The U.S. Air Force hopes to conduct more than 6,000 aircraft operations annually at four airfields on three American islands in the northwest Pacific Ocean, including a major WWII-era airfield that is being refurbished , according to an announcement from the Department of the Air Force. The department published a notice of intent to prepare an environmental impact statement that will assess “potential social, economic, and environmental effects” of training and operations at Saipan International Airport, Tinian International Airport, Tinian North Field and Rota International Airport. The islands are part of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, an unincorporated U.S. territory. The proposed training and exercises will support the Air Force’s Agile Combat Operations concept, which emphasizes dispersal of forces across airfields and the ability to maneuver between them while sustaining operations under a range of conditions, with the goal of thwarting an adversary’s ability to shut down those operations by targeting a single base. ACE, as it’s known, has developed largely in response to the Chinese military’s growing reach and expanding missile arsenal.  The notice said the four airfields provide “a unique opportunity” to support ACE, with infrastructure that varies from “fully developed commercial airfields to expeditionary operating locations.” The three islands are within a few dozen nautical miles of each other, which would allow for training that reflects the complexity of distributed operations while reducing transit time between them. They are less than 100 nautical miles north of the major military bases on Guam, another U.S. territory, which would support the staging and deployment of forces for those exercises. The three airfields “collectively provide a training environment that enables [the Air Force] to exercise distributed operations, test and employ tailorable force packages, strengthen sustainment and maneuver capabilities, and enhance operational resilience,” the notice reads. The environmental impact statement will evaluate the potential effects of the proposed activities, which include small, medium and large trainings and exercises held several times a year for a few weeks at a time and consisting of up to 1,200 fixed-wing and 320 rotary-wing operations, like takeoffs and landings, annually at each airfield. It will also assess an alternative scenario with up to 1,400 fixed-wing and 384 rotary-wing operations per airfield annually and a “No Action Alternative.” The trainings and exercises would be supported by up to 550,000 gallons of fuel at each airfield, up to 1,000 personnel per airfield, the temporary installation of expeditionary infrastructure, the handling of munitions like chaff and flares, as well as support services and pre-and post-training and exercise activities.  The proposed activity comes after several years of work to upgrade the airfields in question, especially the airfields on Tinian, which were built and heavily used during WWII. North Field was inactive after the war and was largely covered with vegetation when the rehabilitation effort began in late 2023. The Air Force also upgraded port and roadway infrastructure, fuel pipelines and airfield surfaces, and utilities to facilitate expanded operations on Tinian . The airfield rehabilitation efforts have created some questions among Air Force leaders about resourcing and funding, particularly as the war with Iran has placed new demands on the force. Island residents also have misgivings about the projects. While some welcome the investment that the construction and military operations will bring, others have doubts that the increased activity will really benefit the islands’ populations and that the Pentagon will be transparent about its activity and responsive to local concerns.  The Department of the Air Force will hold public meetings this month on Saipan, Tinian and Rota to get feedback on the proposal, with written comments due by Nov. 29. The department plans to produce a draft environmental impact statement for public comment in fall 2027 and a final version in mid-2028.

Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years. It is estimated that up to three million Uyghurs have been interned, imprisoned, and enslaved in detention centers, prisons, and forced labor facilities throughout China since 2017.
In 2021, the Uyghur Tribunal found that China was committing genocide and other crimes against humanity against Uyghurs. In 2022, the United Nations also concluded that China was committing human rights violations against Uyghurs amounting to crimes against humanity. Countries including the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, United Kingdom, Lithuania, Belgium, and France have all declared a genocide in East Turkestan. Despite these declarations of genocide and related reports by various human rights organizations, atrocities against Uyghurs continue today with very limited international recognition and accountability.
During this time of ongoing genocide and cultural erasure in their Indigenous homeland, Uyghurs of the diaspora are working to preserve their culture and identity as a matter of survival. Uyghur education has been eradicated by the Chinese State, Uyghur texts are forbidden and in danger of being eliminated, and the Uyghur language itself is prohibited.
Uyghur scholars, linguists, and other specialists in the diaspora worldwide serve on the Uyghur Language and Education Committee of the Uyghur Academy to preserve the work of Uyghur intellectuals who have been persecuted and forcibly disappeared. This work has been ongoing since 2009 and is continuing to expand.
The Committee has created standards-aligned K-5 textbooks, which include classic and contemperory Uyghur literature, poetry, historical texts, and biographies for Uyghur children to learn about their own culture and identity in their native language. The Committee is seeking funding to expand and revise the existing K-5 textbooks, create teacher’s edition textbooks for educators, and design supplemental resources. They also hope to develop Middle and High School textbooks and related supplemental resources. To effectively implement these educational materials, they would also like to provide training for teachers.
Please consider supporting this urgent work of the Uyghur Academic Foundation as a matter of cultural survival for future generations of the Uyghur people.
