title: Hong Kong: Cruel Joshua Wong sentence a grim reminder of city’s disdain for human rights
zh_title: 香港：残酷的黄之锋判决严酷地提醒人们该城市对人权的蔑视
source: 当局如何使用防火墙和其他互联网控制工具？- 国际特赦组织
summary: 在回应香港活动人士黄之锋因“勾结外国势力”而被判处 10 年徒刑时，国际特赦组织区域副主任萨拉·布鲁克斯 (Sarah Brooks) 表示：“香港当局对黄之锋的迫害仍在继续，最新的国家安全定罪是残酷的——也许是故意的——就在他根据之前的定罪获得释放的几个月前。”黄之锋向权力讲真话的勇气值得赞扬，但在香港，让他成为一个罪犯。今天的这句话再次严峻地提醒我们
content:
在回应香港活动人士黄之锋因“勾结外国势力”而被判处 10 年徒刑时，国际特赦组织区域副主任萨拉·布鲁克斯 (Sarah Brooks) 表示：“香港当局对黄之锋的迫害仍在继续，最新的国家安全定罪是残酷的——也许是故意的——就在他根据之前的定罪获得释放的几个月前。”黄之锋向权力讲真话的勇气值得赞扬，但在香港，让他成为一个罪犯。今天的判决再次严峻地提醒人们，香港的国家安全法如何成为惩罚异议的工具，而不是真正保护国家安全的工具。 “国际社会不应接受继续将合法活动定罪为香港的新常态。各国政府必须继续施压，要求保护人权并释放那些仅仅因为行使权利而被监禁的人。国际特赦组织再次呼吁香港当局推翻黄之锋的国家安全定罪，并废除所有违反香港国际人权义务的立法。”背景 黄之锋今天根据北京实施的香港国家安全法（NSL）承认串谋外国势力罪名，被判处 10 年监禁。
根据第二次国家安全定罪，黄被指控在 2020 年 7 月至 2020 年 11 月期间与自我流亡的活动人士罗冠聪和“其他不明人士”合谋，要求外国或组织对香港或中国实施制裁、封锁或从事其他敌对活动。这位著名活动人士于 2024 年被判处四年零八个月的徒刑，这是《国家安全法》迄今为止最大规模的起诉，罪名是“串谋颠覆国家政权”。他是因参加 2020 年非官方“初选”而被监禁的 45 名反对派人士之一，联合国专家认为这些指控与受国际人权法保护的活动有关。此前的判决预计于 2027 年 1 月结束。自 2020 年以来，香港的人权状况急剧恶化，有 300 多人因违反《国家安全法》或殖民时代的“煽动叛乱”法而被捕。此外，地方当局于2024年推出的所谓“23条”立法进一步加深了镇压，压制了该市的反对声音。 《香港：残酷的黄之锋的判决，残酷地提醒人们香港对人权的蔑视》一文首先出现在国际特赦组织上。

【原文 English Original】
Responding to the 10-year sentence handed to Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong for “colluding with foreign forces”, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director Sarah Brooks said: “The Hong Kong authorities’ persecution of Joshua Wong continues with this latest national security conviction, which cruelly – and perhaps deliberately – comes mere months before he would have been eligible for release under his previous conviction. “Joshua Wong’s bravery in speaking truth to power should be commended, but instead in Hong Kong it makes him a criminal. Today’s sentence is another grim reminder of how Hong Kong’s National Security Law has become a tool to punish dissent rather than to genuinely protect national security. “The international community should not accept the continued criminalization of legitimate activism as the new normal in Hong Kong. Governments must continue to press for the protection of human rights and the release of those imprisoned solely for exercising their rights. “Amnesty International reiterates its call on the Hong Kong authorities to overturn Joshua Wong’s national security convictions and to repeal all legislation that violates Hong Kong’s international human rights obligations.” Background Joshua Wong was today sentenced to 10 years in prison after pleading guilty to conspiring to collude with foreign forces under Hong Kong’s Beijing-imposed National Security Law (NSL). Under his second national security conviction, Wong was accused of conspiring with self-exiled activist Nathan Law and “other persons unknown” between July 2020 and November 2020 to request foreign countries or organizations to impose sanctions, blockades or engage in other hostile activities against Hong Kong or China. The prominent activist had been sentenced in 2024, in the largest mass prosecution under the NSL to date, to four years and eight months for “conspiracy to commit subversion”. He was one of 45 opposition figures jailed due to their participation in unofficial “primaries” in 2020, on charges which UN experts considered to relate to activities protected under international human rights law. This previous sentence is scheduled to end in January 2027. Hong Kong’s human rights situation has deteriorated dramatically since 2020, with more than 300 people arrested for violating the NSL or a colonial-era “sedition” law. In addition, the so-called Article 23 legislation introduced by the local authorities in 2024 has further deepened repression and silenced opposition voices in the city. The post Hong Kong: Cruel Joshua Wong sentence a grim reminder of city’s disdain for human rights appeared first on Amnesty International .

title: Tai Po fire: Former top official urges gov’t to publish building inspection report to clear buyout doubts
zh_title: 大埔火警：前高官促政府公布验楼报告以释买断疑虑
summary: 一名香港前高级官员呼吁政府公布遭受火灾的宏福苑的结构检查报告，以打消那些拒绝政府公寓回购提议的房主的担忧。前运输及房屋局局长张建良。资料图片：香港政府一站通。香港前运输及房屋局局长张永明周三在《明报》发表的一篇评论文章中表示，利用专门立法从拒绝政府回购计划的业主手中买下公寓，将与私人财产权相抵触。
content:
一名香港前高级官员呼吁政府公布遭受火灾的宏福苑的结构检查报告，以打消那些拒绝政府公寓回购提议的房主的担忧。前运输及房屋局局长张建良。资料图片：香港政府一站通。香港前运输及房屋局局长张永明周三在《明报》发表的一篇评论文章中表示，利用专门立法从拒绝政府回购计划的业主手中买下公寓，将与私人财产权相抵触。截至10月中旬，宏福苑超过93%的房主已签署正式销售协议，将其公寓出售给政府，作为近一年前致命火灾后买​​断计划的一部分。政府表示，对于那些未签字的人，可以诉诸法律手段。 “《基本法》保护私人财产权，如果没有明确的‘公共利益’理由或合法的公共目的，政府不能征用私人资产，”张用中文写道。去年11月26日，大埔发生大火，吞没了正在进行大规模翻修工程的政府资助屋村的七栋建筑物。大火导致 168 人死亡，4,600 多名居民流离失所。
张说：“通过特别立法授权强制收购很容易引发人们对开创政府征用私人财产先例的担忧；必须极其谨慎地处理它，因为它可能面临无限期拖延的司法审查。”宏福法院，2026 年 8 月 20 日。照片：Kyle Lam。张说，迄今为止，房屋局尚未发布结构检查报告，“损坏的真实程度尚不清楚”。一些居民，包括一些拒绝政府买断的居民，对他们的房屋是否无法挽救表示怀疑。这位前部长表示：“少数持怀疑态度的业主仍与政府存在争议，其中一些人拒绝收购提议。” “结构检查报告应尽快公布，以消除公众疑虑。”张还对上周提交给政府的独立调查委员会的最终报告进行了评论，强调“邪恶的平庸”，强调“双重机构失败”，即政府未能发现不法行为，而私营部门看门人也未能履行职责。他形容官僚机构内部存在“平庸的邪恶”，检查肤浅，部门互相推诿。 2026 年 10 月 29 日，香港行政长官李家超和其他高级官员就 2025 年宏福苑致命火灾鞠躬致歉。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
他写道：“职业诚信崩溃，欺诈性玩忽职守，专业认证和第三方把关人沦为橡皮图章练习。”关于政府拟议的改革，张表示，组织文化需要“真正的转型”，“避免新瓶装旧酒”——这是立法者在李明博宣布改革方案后表达的担忧。在文中，张还谈到了前房屋部长何永琼的辞职以及围绕政治问责的讨论。何领导了住房局，该局负责监管声名狼藉的独立检查组。调查委员会报告还称，消防处

【原文 English Original】
A former top Hong Kong official has called on the government to release a structural inspection report of the fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court to dispel the concerns of homeowners who have rejected the government’s apartment buyback offer. Former secretary for transport and housing Anthony Cheung. File Photo: GovHK. Hong Kong’s former secretary for transport and housing Anthony Cheung said in an op-ed published in Ming Pao on Wednesday that the use of specialised legislation to buy out flats from owners who have refused the government’s buyback scheme would be at odds with private property rights. As of mid-October, over 93 per cent of Wang Fuk Court homeowners have signed a formal sales agreement to sell their flats to the government as part of a buyout scheme following the deadly fire almost a year ago. The government has said it could resort to legal means for those who did not sign. “The Basic Law protects private property rights, and the government cannot expropriate private assets without a clear ‘public interest’ justification or a legitimate public purpose,” Cheung wrote in Chinese. The Tai Po fire broke out on November 26 last year, engulfing seven buildings in the government-subsidised estate during large-scale renovation works. The blaze killed 168 people and displaced over 4,600 residents. “Passing special legislation to authorise compulsory acquisition would easily stoke fears of setting a precedent for government expropriation of private property; it must be handled with extreme prudence, as it risks facing judicial reviews that could drag on indefinitely,” Cheung said. Wang Fuk Court on August 20, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam. To date, the Housing Bureau has yet to release the structural inspection report, “leaving the true extent of the damage unclear,” Cheung said. Some residents, including some who have rejected the government’s buyout, have expressed doubts that their homes are not salvageable. “A sceptical minority of owners remain locked in disputes with the government, with some rejecting the buyout proposal,” the former minister said. “The structural inspection report should be published as soon as possible to dispel public doubts.” ‘The banality of evil’ Cheung also commented on an independent probe committee’s final report that was submitted to the government last week, highlighting “dual institutional failures” where the government failed to detect wrongdoing and private sector gatekeepers failed to do their duty. He described a “banality of evil” within the bureaucracy, with superficial inspections and departments passing the buck. Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee and other top officials bow in apology on October 29, 2026 over the deadly 2025 Wang Fuk Court blaze. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “[There was] a collapse of professional integrity and fraudulent neglect of duty, where professional certification and third-party gatekeepers were reduced to mere rubber-stamp exercises,” he wrote. Regarding the government’s proposed reforms, Cheung said that “genuine transformation” was needed in organisational culture “to avoid putting old wine into new bottles” – a concern that lawmakers voiced after city leader Lee announced the reform package. In the article, Cheung also addressed former housing minister Winnie Ho’s resignation and the discussions around political accountability. Ho led the Housing Bureau, which oversaw the disgraced Independent Checking Unit. The probe committee report also said that the Fire Services Department, the Buildings Department, and the Labour Department, bore a share of the responsibility for the fire. “Naturally, the public questions why other bureau directors who also oversee implicated departments have remained in office. While the chief executive’s explanation that this was a ‘political decision’ may not entirely lay the public’s doubts to rest, such is life.”

title: Britain's tech ambitions depend on minerals made in China, MPs warn
zh_title: 议员警告称，英国的科技雄心依赖于中国制造的矿物
summary: 英国对人工智能、先进芯片和清洁能源的雄心依赖于中国主导的矿产供应链，议员们表示，他们无法确定部长们是否有可靠的计划来减少这种依赖。下议院商业、创新、科学和贸易委员会为部长们设定了十项测试，以确保关键矿物的安全。它的裁决并不乐观——它不能确信政府会通过其中任何一项。这些测试涵盖部长们是否知道哪些行业和技术需要保护、他们需要哪些矿物、哪些地方的供应可能会受到干扰，以及国内如何保护这些产业和技术。
content:
英国对人工智能、先进芯片和清洁能源的雄心依赖于中国主导的矿产供应链，议员们表示，他们无法确定部长们是否有可靠的计划来减少这种依赖。下议院商业、创新、科学和贸易委员会为部长们设定了十项测试，以确保关键矿物的安全。它的裁决并不乐观——它不能确信政府会通过其中任何一项。这些测试涵盖部长们是否知道哪些行业和技术需要保护、需要哪些矿产、哪些地方的供应可能会受到干扰，以及国内生产、海外合作伙伴关系、技能和融资将如何缩小差距。在今天发布的一份报告中，该委员会警告说，供应多样化将需要 10 到 15 年的时间，并且需要持续的投资以及与盟友的合作。报告称，将中国完全排除在外既不现实也不可取。让北京拥有如此大的影响力则是另一回事。关键矿物支撑着从电池和半导体到数据中心和军事设备的一切。该称号反映了它们的经济或安全重要性以及对供应中断的脆弱性，而不是一个特别独特的地质俱乐部的成员资格。英国与包括美国、欧盟、日本和印度在内的几乎所有主要工业化经济体一样，几乎完全依赖这些材料和矿产品的进口。
但在中国境外开采更多矿石只能解决部分问题。更大的瓶颈是加工。该委员会援引国际能源署的数据称，中国是 20 种战略矿产中 19 种的领先炼油国，平均市场份额为 70%。矿井上方的不同旗帜并不一定意味着通过炼油厂的路线不同。暴露的范围不仅仅限于芯片和电池。正如《The Register》八月份报道的那样，铒用于放大光纤链路中的信号，而钇则用于陶瓷电容器等组件。 IEEE Spectrum 警告说，中国实际上垄断了制造商所需的工业可用材料的加工。这种集中已经造成了破坏。中国于 2025 年 4 月在美国征收关税后实施稀土出口管制，波及制造业供应链，并迫使汽车工厂临时关闭。即使英国不是预定目标，英国制造商也可能遭受损失。该委员会还重点介绍了用于雷达、通信和电子战的先进半导体的镓和锗。报告显示，中国的产量分别占全球的 95% 和 93%。北京在芯片材料方面发挥影响力并不新鲜。随着西方对半导体技术的限制收紧，中国于 2023 年 7 月宣布了镓和锗的出口许可要求。
然而议员们表示，政府尚未明确确定要保护哪些国内工业和技术能力，因此很难确定哪些供应链值得优先考虑。进口统计数据也没有揭示全部风险。矿物质可能会进入电池、磁铁和其他制造部件内部，并作为单独的材料从视野中消失。企业本身可能并不确切地知道其供应链中的几层到底是什么。该委员会希望与c中的公司进行保密的映射和压力测试

【原文 English Original】
Britain's ambitions for AI, advanced chips, and clean energy rest on mineral supply chains dominated by China, and MPs say they cannot establish whether ministers have a credible plan to reduce that dependence. The House of Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee has set ministers ten tests for securing critical minerals. Its verdict is hardly glowing – it cannot be confident the government passes any of them. The tests cover whether ministers know which industries and technologies need protecting, what minerals they require, where supplies could be disrupted, and how domestic production, overseas partnerships, skills, and financing will close the gaps. In a report published today , the committee warns that diversifying supplies will take ten to 15 years, and will require sustained investment and cooperation with allies. Completely cutting China out is neither realistic nor desirable, it says. Leaving Beijing with so much leverage is another matter. Critical minerals underpin everything from batteries and semiconductors to datacenters and military equipment. The designation reflects their economic or security importance and vulnerability to supply disruption, rather than membership of an especially exclusive geological club. The UK – like pretty much all major industrialized economies including the US, the EU, Japan, and India – is almost entirely dependent on imports of these materials and mineral product s. But digging up more ore outside China would solve only part of the problem. The bigger bottleneck is processing. Citing International Energy Agency figures, the committee says China is the leading refiner for 19 of 20 strategic minerals, with an average market share of 70 percent. A different flag over the mine does not necessarily mean a different route through the refinery. The exposure extends beyond chips and batteries. As The Register reported in August , erbium is used to amplify signals in fiber-optic links, while yttrium goes into components including ceramic capacitors. IEEE Spectrum warned that China effectively monopolized the processing of both into the industrially usable materials manufacturers need. That concentration has already caused disruption. China's rare earth export controls in April 2025 , introduced following US tariffs, rippled through manufacturing supply chains and forced temporary automotive plant closures. British manufacturers can suffer even when Britain isn't the intended target. The committee also highlights gallium and germanium, used in advanced semiconductors for radar, communications, and electronic warfare. China accounts for 95 percent and 93 percent of their global production respectively, according to the report [PDF]. Beijing flexing its leverage over chip materials is not new. China announced export licensing requirements for gallium and germanium in July 2023 amid tightening Western restrictions on semiconductor technology. Yet MPs say the government has not clearly identified which domestic industrial and technological capabilities it wants to protect, making it difficult to determine which supply chains deserve priority. Nor do import statistics reveal the whole exposure. Minerals can arrive inside batteries, magnets, and other manufactured components, disappearing from view as individual materials. Businesses themselves may not know precisely what lies several layers down their supply chains. The committee wants confidential mapping and stress-testing with firms in critical sectors, followed by joint purchasing arrangements with allies to give new mining and refining projects dependable customers. Committee chair Liam Byrne said: "Critical minerals are the alpha of the new economy. We cannot re-arm Britain, build AI or deliver net zero unless we secure the minerals these technologies depend on. "Yet sixteen years after China first weaponised its chokehold over rare earths , Britain remains dangerously exposed. We don't know enough about what minerals we need or where to find them. Our energy costs make processing uneconomic, we're exporting valuable metal waste, and our public finance institutions are shackled by outdated rules." More than a shopping list The committee's five-part prescription is to identify the capabilities Britain must protect, map their mineral needs, expand domestic mining, processing, and recycling, pool purchasing power with allies, and establish a dedicated financing facility. The proposed facility would bring together public funding bodies to back projects through grants, equity, loans, guarantees, and long-term purchase agreements. "We're never going to eliminate Chinese minerals from our supply chains. But it's foolish to leave Britain exposed to economic coercion when we could be building alternative supplies," Byrne said. "That's why we need a new Critical Minerals Finance Facility with the financial firepower to invest in new mines, processing plants and recycling, working with our allies to share the costs." The report argues that existing institutions leave gaps, particularly for early-stage projects. It recommends expanding UK Export Finance's remit and allowing British International Investment to take equity stakes in overseas mineral projects. Long-term purchasing commitments and price guarantees could help keep strategically important projects commercially viable despite volatile mineral prices. There is also material closer to home. The report says 80 percent of UK metal products classified as waste are exported. MPs want better sorting and separation infrastructure, alongside more detailed trade data to establish exactly what valuable scrap is leaving the country. For domestic projects, they recommend designated critical mineral clusters with permitting deadlines, help navigating approvals, energy support, and priority grid access. Stockpiles could provide a short-term buffer too. The committee calls for an initial reserve covering approximately 60 days of minerals needed for defense capabilities, while stressing that warehouses are no substitute for diversified supply. None of this offers a quick escape from dependence on China. The committee's argument is that Britain needs to decide what it must protect, work out what those industries actually consume, and help finance alternatives before the next disruption. "De-risking even a prudent proportion of our supplies will take over a decade. Britain cannot afford to drift," Byrne said. "We must act now before dangerous dependencies become strategic liabilities." ®

title: 中国富豪铁心出走！狂砸钱抢买这国护照避险？

content: 【大纪元2026年10月29日讯】（大纪元记者季薇报导）对一些中国富豪来说，外国护照曾是方便出行、拓展海外生活的“加分项”；如今，随着北京加强对境外资产的税务监管，加上地缘政治不确定性升高，越来越多富裕中国人正在试图获得一个或多个国家的长期居留身份或国籍。 移民及财富顾问表示，近期有更多中国富裕家庭在认真考虑放弃中国国籍，重新安排海外资产、居留身份与家庭未来。 “我们有一些客户愿意放弃中国国籍，持有多个护照。”移民咨询公司Arton Capital的执行长 阿曼德‧阿顿 （Armand Arton）表示，选择哪种护照取决于他们的生活方式和商业需求。 中共在面临严重财政困境之下，正通过大数据升级、倒查海外资产、甚至推出新规等手段，锁定高收入、高净值族群及富裕阶层。 示意图。 (Shutterstock) 更多富豪认真考虑换国籍 美国消费者新闻与商业频道（CNBC）10月28日报导，湾岸律师事务所（Bayfront Law）董事林瑞安（Ryan Lin）表示，自今年7月北京推出离岸信托税务新规，对部分境外收益与交易课征20%税负以来，寻求放弃中国国籍的富裕客户明显增加。 林瑞安表示，以前客户多半只是讨论放弃国籍的可能性，如今已有更多人表达具体意向。 财富管理机构Farro Capital联合创办人 曼尼什‧ 蒂布雷瓦尔（Manish Tibrewal）也表示，越来越多中国家庭开始研究外国国籍选项。他的公司正协助部分家庭申请加勒比地区国籍，但能否入籍仍取决于当地政府审批。 投资移民机构Savory & Partners的数据显示，自7月以来，来自中国客户的咨询量增加33%；而Global Citizen Solutions的相关咨询量，较去年同期增加近40%。 专家也提醒，中共不承认双重国籍，取得外国国籍通常意味着必须放弃中国国籍，而更换国籍未必能逃过中共的税务追缴。 专家指出，是否可以逃过中共的税务追缴，视乎财富的配置方式与架构，即使已放弃中国国籍，相关人士仍可能须就过往收益缴税。不过，若国籍与税务居民身份确实发生变化，也可能会影响到未来的纳税义务。 林瑞安表示，比较愿意放弃中国国籍的人，通常与中国内地的业务联系已不多，大部分财富和营运早已转移至境外。对于企业和财富仍深深扎根中国内地的人来说，这项选择则意味着更大的牺牲。 安提瓜和巴布达 （Antigua and Barbuda） 的沙滩色白而细腻。（伊田／大纪元） 加勒比海地区：快速取得公民身份的途径 对希望直接取得外国国籍的人而言，加勒比地区是热门选项之一。 安提瓜和巴布达（Antigua and Barbuda）等国 提供投资入籍计划，符合资格的申请人可通过规定的投资或捐款取得国籍。 蒂布雷瓦尔表示，加勒比地区的部分入籍程序可能在六个月内完成，通常比必须先累积居留年限、再申请入籍的欧洲或美国途径更快。 阿顿 指出，对部分客户而言，取得加勒比护照并非为了永久搬迁，而是希望增加旅行弹性，并建立国际生活与商业据点。 根据Global Citizen Solutions，在其追踪的目的地中，加勒比地区今年来自中国的咨询增幅最为突出。 波尔图是葡萄牙第二大城市，也是联合国教科文组织世界遗产和重要商业中心。(Alexander Spatari/Getty Images) 欧洲：葡萄牙、意大利与匈牙利是热门 欧洲国家也逐渐受到关注，尽管许多国家提供居留途径而非直接公民身份。 阿顿 说：“对于不愿放弃国籍的中国高净值人士，拥有多份居留权或长期签证是更具吸引力的选择。” 葡萄牙因其黄金签证计划而受欢迎，该计划通过投资提供居留权及入籍途径。 阿顿补充说，意大利正凭借着针对符合条件的新移民，推出“优惠税制”、优质“国际学校”，以及完善的“金融服务基础设施”，吸引大量富裕家庭前来落户。 匈牙利是另一个新兴目的地，通过投资提供长期居留，起价为25万欧元（约29万美元）。 “匈牙利是让人感到意外的热门选择。”Global Citizen Solutions工作人员表示，“随着欧洲主流的黄金签证途径陆续关闭、或大幅调涨成本，匈牙利通过受监管的基金投资，为投资人提供了取得申根区居留权的机会。” 澳洲昆士兰大学圣露西亚（St Lucia）校区。（嘉义大学提供） 澳洲及东南亚等地各有吸引力 澳洲是另一个受欢迎的选择，特别适合重视教育和生活品质的家庭。 移民顾问公司指出，马来西亚也正吸引越来越多的关注，尤其是吉隆坡与槟城；当地较低的生活成本、华语社区以及高品质的国际学校，对许多家庭极具吸引力。 Global Citizen Solutions工作人员表示：“我们也看到外国家庭对亚洲传统热门枢纽（如新加坡、香港）以外地区的兴趣显著增加，包括马来西亚槟城以及泰国推出的长期居留签证；这些家庭更看重高品质的生活方式与更低廉的生活成本。” 同时，阿根廷及东欧部分地区正成为中国富人寻求多元化国际居留地的选项之一。 Arton Capital将阿根廷视为值得关注的市场，而Savory & Partners则强调中国富人对塞尔维亚、北马其顿和保加利亚日益增长的兴趣。 顾问提醒，对海外公民身份的兴趣不一定代表完全放弃国籍或实际搬迁。 阿顿说：“大家必须认识到，探索海外居留权、打造护照组合，以及将整个家庭迁往异国，是截然不同的决定。”

content:
新竹市长高虹安星期四（11月5日）到北区长和社区发展协会参与2026年幸福共餐巡礼，和长辈们一起吃饭、话家常，也帮大家打菜、盛装餐食，把热腾腾的饭菜送到长辈手中。 （取自高虹安脸书）
针对有媒体引述匿名人士爆料称，新竹市长高虹安已安排在12月中率领一级主管到海外参访，新竹市政府发文予以反驳，指相关报道造谣抹黑。
台湾九合一地方选举将于11月28日举行，亲绿台媒《自由时报》星期五（11月6日）引述匿名人士爆料称，新竹市长选举是蓝白合指标县市，高虹安虽以无党籍拼连任仍具优势，疑似用行政资源行选举绑桩，从今年初发5000元新台币（195新元）振兴消费现金、各种活动及发各种名目的加倍券，甚至办各种流水型烟火式活动都用公帑预算。
上述人士称，如今传出高虹安已认定会连任，将用公务预算支出，在12月中旬带一级主管及政务官到海外参访做为犒赏。
匿名人士透露，高虹安市府近期已在办理12月中旬到海外参访五至七天，被质疑是拿公家经费办庆功宴。
针对当天媒体引述匿名爆料指称新竹市政府年底出访是“选后庆功”一事，新竹市政府星期五在官网发布的声明中严正驳斥，相关指控完全是去脉络化的政治操作与恶意抹黑。
声明指出，新竹市作为台湾的科技首都，年底出访行程是应韩国原州市政府今年3月到访时的邀请，前往洽谈智慧医疗及尖端产业合作，同时也受合作伙伴LINE WORKS母公司NAVER Cloud积极邀请参访韩国总部，实地考察智慧城市与数位治理。
对于有心人士将正当公务出访扭曲为“公帑享乐、庆功犒赏”，新竹市政府表达强烈严厉谴责。
新竹市政府强调，市政建设与国际交流具备高度延续性，绝不可能因为政治算计或选举时程而陷入停摆，更不容许公务人员推动城市外交的努力遭到无理践踏。市府团队始终以新竹市的永续发展与全体市民的福祉为最高出发点，聚焦于实质市政考察与国际交流效益，不容歪曲误导。
新竹市政府说明，原州市为韩国政府指定的国家级生技产业聚落，与新竹市的产学研资源高度契合；而LINE WORKS母公司NAVER Cloud在智慧城市及数位公共治理领域的领先实务，更是新竹市推动城市转型的重要借镜。市府团队积极争取国际合作，正是为了新竹市的产业升级与公共服务注入崭新动能，绝非任何政治语言所能抹煞。
新竹市政府重申，面对国际竞争，新竹市绝不可能因为恶意抹黑而画地自限、停下带领城市走向世界的步伐。市府团队将持续秉持专业与坦荡态度，务实推动市政与国际产业链结，全力捍卫市民福祉与城市荣誉，并强烈呼吁各界立即停止无端抹黑与政治干扰，回归市政理性讨论。

信和集团与Bay Pickle扩大合作伙伴关系，推出青年人才孵化计划，并将中国匹克球巡回赛首次引入香港。此次合作包括该市首个室内湾泡菜学院，为 20 名青少年球员提供超过 1,000 个小时的训练，
信和集团与当地匹克球运营商Bay Pickle扩大了合作伙伴关系，以促进精英运动员的发展和社区参与，并宣布推出青少年人才孵化计划，同时全国中国匹克球巡回赛在当地首次亮相。该联合计划于11月6日在奥海城揭幕，重点关注专业教练、竞技平台和精英通道支持，为本地球员建立晋升阶梯。
此次合作将在信和集团旗下的 One SilverSea 物业开设该市第一家 Bay Pickle 学院，该学院设有两个室内竞赛级球场。该中心将提供由经验丰富的本地教练带领的结构化课程，并定期邀请海外和内地的专业教练和运动员进行专门的训练和诊所。该学院在美国职业棒球大联盟创始人史蒂夫·库恩 (Steve Kuhn) 的领导下运营，史蒂夫·库恩担任主席。其教练框架涵盖青少年发展、精英诊所和以国际人才为特色的大师班，其中包括 PPA 巡回赛中排名世界第一的青少年选手 Rex Thais。

Sino Group and Bay Pickle launch youth elite programme and China Pickleball Circuit in Hong Kong | China Labour Bulletin Board
Saturday, 7 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Sino Group and Bay Pickle launch youth elite programme and China Pickleball Circuit in Hong Kong
Sino Group and Bay Pickle have expanded their partnership to launch a youth talent incubation initiative and bring the China Pickleball Circuit to Hong Kong for the first time. The collaboration includes the city's first indoor Bay Pickle Academy, over 1,000 hours of training for 20 junior players,
Sino Group and local pickleball operator Bay Pickle have expanded their partnership to promote elite athlete development and community participation, announcing the rollout of a youth talent incubation initiative alongside the local debut of the national China Pickleball Circuit. Unveiled at Olympian City on 6 November, the joint initiative focuses on professional coaching, competitive platforms, and elite pathway support to build a progression ladder for local players.
The collaboration will see the opening of the city's first Bay Pickle Academy at Sino Group's One SilverSea property, featuring two indoor competition-grade courts. The facility will offer structured courses led by seasoned local instructors and will regularly invite overseas and mainland professional coaches and athletes for specialised training sessions and clinics. The academy operates under the leadership of Major League Pickleball founder Steve Kuhn, who serves as chairman. Its coaching framework encompasses youth development, elite clinics, and masterclasses featuring international talent, including world number one ranked junior on the PPA Tour, Rex Thais.
To expand competitive opportunities, Bay Pickle has secured the rights to stage the China Pickleball Circuit in Hong Kong for the first time, with registration opening immediately. Founded in 2024, the nationwide circuit has expanded to more than 1,000 tournament stops across nearly 100 cities. The Hong Kong tournament will take place across four days on 6, 12, 19, and 20 December at the Fairview Park Country Club in Yuen Long. The event features four competition categories: individual ranking events at CPC-100 and CPC-300 levels alongside junior divisions J-30 and J-60 for athletes under 18. Each category will contest men's singles, women's singles, men's doubles, women's doubles, and mixed doubles.
Organisers also pledged over 1,000 hours of training resources and subsidised court access to nurture 20 selected junior players during the scheme's inaugural year. The Sino and Bay Pickle Future Elite Cultivation Programme will open applications to local players under 18, targeting 20 promising juniors in its first cohort. Candidates will undergo screening, interviews, and technical assessments to qualify for personalised training pathways. Successful applicants will receive weekly complimentary court time at the Bay Pickle Academy, systematic technical assessments, and priority enrolment in advanced coaching workshops. Standout performers will be considered for travel sponsorships to represent Hong Kong in mainland and overseas tournaments.
Sino Group Chief Commercial Officer Bella Chhoa said building a sport's long-term future requires not only broadening public participation but also establishing a sustainable progression ladder for rising athletes. She noted that Sino Group will continue utilising its property portfolio and community networks to host open play sessions and school activities, balancing community outreach with high-performance sports development.

香港食物安全中心在从中国进口的冷冻鸡腿中发现强力霉素超标。进口商已被责令停止销售并召回受影响批次。正常食用不会造成健康风险，但违规可能会导致罚款或监禁。
香港食物安全中心于2026年11月6日公布，一个进口冷冻鸡腿样本中兽药强力霉素超标。受影响的产品为“鸡带骨全腿240-260克”，品牌为“城字”，产自中国，由维利加发展有限公司进口。每箱重15公斤，生产日期为2026年7月22日，保质期为2028年1月21日。
据中心发言人称，样本是根据进口层面的常规食品监测计划采集的。检测显示，该样本每公斤含有180微克多西环素，超过了每公斤100微克的法定上限。发言人表示，中心已将违规情况通报进口商，责令其停止销售并将受影响批次下架。进口商已按照指示展开回收，消费者可于办公时间致电进口商热线2944 8139查询回收事宜。
发言人补充说，鉴于检出兽药残留含量，正常食用该产品不会对健康构成风险。根据《食物中有害物质规例》（第132AF章），在香港出售供人食用的禽肉中强力霉素的含量不得超过每公斤100微克。违法者一经定罪，可处最高 50,000 港元罚款及最高六个月监禁。
中心将继续跟进事件并采取适当行动。调查正在进行中。

Imported frozen chicken leg samples exceed veterinary drug residue limit | China Labour Bulletin Board
Saturday, 7 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Imported frozen chicken leg samples exceed veterinary drug residue limit
Hong Kong’s Centre for Food Safety found excessive doxycycline in imported frozen chicken legs from China. The importer has been ordered to stop sales and recall affected batches. Normal consumption poses no health risk, but the violation may lead to a fine or imprisonment.
The Centre for Food Safety of Hong Kong announced on 6 November 2026 that a sample of imported frozen chicken legs exceeded the legal limit for the veterinary drug doxycycline. The affected product is “Chicken Bone-in Whole Leg 240-260 grams”, under the brand “城字” (City), sourced from China and imported by维利加发展有限公司 (Viliga Development Company Limited). Each case weighs 15 kilograms, with a production date of 22 July 2026 and a best-before date of 21 January 2028.
According to a centre spokesman, the sample was collected under the routine food monitoring programme at the import level. Testing showed the sample contained 180 micrograms of doxycycline per kilogram, exceeding the legal maximum of 100 micrograms per kilogram. The spokesman said the centre has informed the importer of the violation and ordered it to stop sales and remove the affected batch from shelves. The importer has initiated a recall as instructed, and consumers may call the importer’s hotline at 2944 8139 during office hours for recall inquiries.
The spokesman added that, given the detected level of the veterinary drug residue, normal consumption of the product would not pose a risk to health. Under the Harmful Substances in Food Regulations (Cap. 132AF), poultry meat sold for human consumption in Hong Kong must not contain more than 100 micrograms of doxycycline per kilogram. Offenders, upon conviction, face a fine of up to HK$50,000 and imprisonment for up to six months.
The centre will continue to follow up on the incident and take appropriate action. The investigation is ongoing.

title: Security chief Chris Tang says gov’t will facilitate Wang Fuk Court fire anniversary events if ‘lawful’
zh_title: 保安局长邓永康表示，如果“合法”，政府将协助宏福苑火灾周年纪念活动
summary: 香港保安局局长邓克里斯表示，当局将在本月晚些时候的悲剧周年纪念日向那些希望纪念宏福苑火灾遇难者的人们提供帮助，前提是此类活动“合法”。保安局局长邓克里斯。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。唐在周四的一次活动中向记者发表讲话时发表了上述讲话，距离致命火灾一周年纪念日还有大约三周。去年11月26日，该小区大规模翻修工程中发生火灾，吞噬了7栋楼房，造成168人死亡。
content:
香港保安局局长邓克里斯表示，当局将在本月晚些时候的悲剧周年纪念日向那些希望纪念宏福苑火灾遇难者的人们提供帮助，前提是此类活动“合法”。保安局局长邓克里斯。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。唐在周四的一次活动中向记者发表讲话时发表了上述讲话，距离致命火灾一周年纪念日还有大约三周。去年11月26日，该村大规模翻修工程中发生大火，吞噬了7栋大楼，造成168人死亡、4600多名居民流离失所。 “很多家人和朋友都想纪念这一天，我们完全理解这一点。只要是合法的行动，我们都会尽力提供便利，”唐说。去年火灾发生后，香港人在广福休憩处设立了一个临时守夜地点，该休憩处是遭受火灾破坏的宏福苑附近的一个公园。火灾发生几天后，在警方的协调下，该处被清理干净。同样在悲剧发生后，政府发布的一份新闻稿猛烈抨击“反华势力和不稳定势力”“发表毫无根据的诽谤性言论”，并试图借火“煽动社会混乱”。 2025 年 12 月 8 日，志愿者在宏福村附近的休息区为大埔火灾受害者移走鲜花、留言和其他悼念品。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
警察国家安全局总警司李志强在火灾发生后表示，他曾到过大埔现场，他认为“情况越来越像‘黑衣暴力’”，指的是2019年民主示威者所穿的衣服。另见：大埔火灾：警方监督连夜清除鲜花、志愿者和政府工作人员向纪念碑致敬的活动。他指出，“基本上是‘黑衣暴力’的小册子和标语”与灾难无关，只是为了煽动仇恨。”中国政府以及北京负责香港事务的最高办公室继续引用一种说法，指责某些行为者利用这场悲剧作为借口，在火灾发生后的几个月里制造混乱。唐周四表示：“我相信，如果依法处理，我们一定会提供帮助。”唐还重申了政府的部分改革建议，并表示当局将采取多管齐下的方法，包括提出立法修正案和协调执法机构，以防止未来串通投标。

【原文 English Original】
Authorities will assist people wishing to commemorate the victims of the Wang Fuk Court blaze on the tragedy’s anniversary later this month, on the condition that such activities are “lawful,” Hong Kong security chief Chris Tang has said. Secretary for Security Chris Tang. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Tang made the remarks when addressing reporters at an event on Thursday, some three weeks ahead of the first anniversary of the deadly fire. The blaze broke out on November 26 last year, engulfing seven buildings in the subsidised housing estate during large-scale renovation works, killing 168 people and displacing over 4,600 residents. “Many family members and friends want to commemorate this day and we fully understand this. We will do our best to facilitate any actions as long as they are handled lawfully,” Tang said. In the wake of the blaze last year, Hongkongers set up a makeshift vigil site at the Kwong Fuk Sitting-out Area, a park near the fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court. It was cleared out days after the fire following coordination with the police. ‘In accordance with the law’ Also in the wake of the tragedy, a government press release blasted “anti-China and destabilising forces” for “making unfounded and slanderous remarks,” and trying to use the fire to “stir up chaos in society.” Volunteers remove flowers, messages and other tributes for Tai Po fire victims at a rest area near Wang Fuk Estate on December 8, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Chief Superintendent of the police’s National Security Department Steve Li said after the fire that he had visited the Tai Po site and that he believed “the situation was becoming more and more like that of ‘black-clad violence,'” in reference to clothing worn by 2019 pro-democracy demonstrators. See also: Tai Po fire: Police oversee overnight removal of flowers, tributes from memorial by volunteers, gov’t staff He pointed to pamphlets and slogans that were “basically unrelated to the disaster and only aimed to incite hatred.” The government — and Beijing’s top office on Hong Kong affairs — has continued to reference a narrative accusing certain actors of using the tragedy as a pretence for sowing chaos in the months since the fire. Tang said on Thursday: “I believe that if they are handled in accordance with the law, we will certainly assist.” Tang also reiterated part of the government’s reform proposals, saying that the authorities would adopt a multi-pronged approach including introducing legislative amendments and coordinating law enforcement agencies to prevent bid-rigging in the future.

title: Buy, Don’t Steal: The Economics of Cognitive Warfare
zh_title: 购买，不要偷窃：认知战的经济学
source: Small Wars Journal by Arizona State Univ
summary: 摘要 认知战以个人数据为基础，而美国以低廉的价格出售大部分数据。这篇文章做了三件事：（1）中国为美国选民档案支付的价格； (2) 将其与秘密收集的记录成本进行比较； (3) 提出五项提高对手购买弹药成本的行动。中国购买美国选民数据并不是为了阅读它。它购买了用于瞄准引擎的原材料。商业广告花了二十年的时间来证明，足够大的个人数据池，通过预测模型运行，可以向人们传递不同的、量身定制的信息。
content:
摘要 认知战以个人数据为基础，而美国以低廉的价格出售大部分数据。这篇文章做了三件事：（1）中国为美国选民档案支付的价格； (2) 将其与秘密收集的记录成本进行比较； (3) 提出五项提高对手购买弹药成本的行动。中国购买美国选民数据并不是为了阅读它。它购买了用于瞄准引擎的原材料。商业广告花了二十年的时间来证明，足够大的个人数据池通过预测模型运行，可以向每个人传递不同的、量身定制的信息。将机器指向人们的恐惧和忠诚度而不是购物习惯，其结果就是认知战：通过数据精确地塑造人们的信念和决策方式的竞赛。该杂志的一篇配套文章认为，认知战是基于数据的，因此认知防御是从数据层开始的。这篇文章对那个战场进行了定价。白宫于 2026 年 7 月发布的一份解密记录显示，这些原材料几乎不需要花费任何成本，因为其中大部分都是合法出售的。获取的算术 在早期关于复合战争经济学的著作中，我提出了成本不对称比率，即对手的进攻单位成本除以防御者的反应成本，作为现代冲突中财政消耗的衡量标准。
一架“沙赫德”单向攻击无人机的成本约为 35,000 美元，根据谁的估计，其价格浮动为 15,000 美元，而国会研究服务处定价约为 400 万美元的爱国者拦截机。战略与国际研究中心 (CSIS) 在分析俄罗斯无人机袭击时，采用了同样的 35,000 美元中间值作为故意保守的数字。这种交换比对抗防守者的 100 比 1 更好。在该研究中，14 个典型威胁配对中的 12 个对攻击者有利。解密的材料允许在不同的领域进行相同的分析：情报获取。结果更糟：交易所对攻击者的支持更大。从购买数据的成本开始。美国每个州和哥伦比亚特区都会出售或发布其选民档案。加州将整个文件的费用上限为 100 美元，对于大约 2200 万条记录来说，相当于每个选民的千分之二美分。阿拉巴马州的收费最高，每个名字收费 1 美分，即全州范围内的名单收费约为 38,000 美元。 11 个州根本不收取任何费用，根据选举援助委员会 2020 年编制的数据，24 个州对全州范围内的文件收取 1 至 1,000 美元之间的费用。直接从各州收集的完整国家档案最多可达六位数。中国支付的费用比这个少。
解密文件中最清晰的文件是一份网络防御通知，记录了一名中国行为者于2022年1月从美国商业网站下载了六个州的选民档案，并声明该信息“可从商业网站公开下载”。没有国家费用，没有入侵，没有利用。边际获取成本是带宽和分析师时间。偷窃的成本是多少 这种隐蔽的替代方案有一个价格表，而且这一次是公开的。当司法部于 2025 年 3 月起诉 10 名中国公民代表中国政府进行黑客攻击时，指控文件中描述了承包商 i-Soon 向中国情报机构收取的每个电子邮件费用为 10,000 至 75,000 美元

【原文 English Original】
Abstract Cognitive warfare runs on personal data, and the United States sells much of that data for pennies. This essay does three things: (1) prices what China paid for American voter files; (2) compares that to the documented cost of covert collection; and (3) proposes five actions that raise an adversary’s cost to buy the ammunition. China did not buy American voter data to read it. It bought raw material for a targeting engine. Commercial advertising spent two decades proving that a large enough pool of personal data, run through predictive models, delivers a different, tailored message to each individual. Point that machinery at a population’s fears and loyalties instead of its shopping habits, and the result is cognitive warfare: the contest to shape what a people believes and how it decides, made precise by data. A companion essay in this journal argued that cognitive warfare runs on data, and that cognitive defense therefore begins at the data layer. This essay prices that battlefield. A declassified record that the White House released in July 2026 shows that the raw material cost almost nothing, because most of it was legally for sale. The Arithmetic of Acquisition In earlier work on compound warfare economics, I proposed the Cost Asymmetry Ratio, the adversary’s offensive unit cost divided by the defender’s response cost, as a measure of fiscal attrition in modern conflict. A Shahed one-way attack drone costs roughly $35,000, give or take $15,000 depending on whose estimate one credits, and forces a Patriot interceptor that the Congressional Research Service prices at roughly $4 million. The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) adopted that same $35,000 midpoint as a deliberately conservative figure when analyzing Russian drone strikes. The exchange runs better than 100-to-1 against the defender. In that study, 12 of 14 canonical threat pairings favor the attacker. The declassified materials permit the same analysis in a different domain: intelligence acquisition. The results are worse: the exchange favors the attacker by an even wider margin. Start with what the data costs to buy. Every US state and the District of Columbia sells or releases its voter file. California caps the fee for its entire file at $100, which for roughly 22 million records works out to about a two-thousandth of a cent per voter. Alabama, at the expensive end, charges one cent per name, or roughly $38,000 for its statewide list. Eleven states charge nothing at all, and according to Election Assistance Commission data compiled in 2020, 24 states charged between $1 and $1,000 for a statewide file. A complete national file assembled directly from the states runs to the low six figures at most. China paid less than that. The clearest document in the declassified release, a network-defense notice , records a Chinese actor downloading the voter files of six states from US commercial websites in January 2022 and states that the information “is publicly available for download from the commercial websites.” No state fee, no intrusion, no exploit. The marginal acquisition cost was bandwidth and analyst hours. What Stealing Costs The covert alternative has a price list, and for once it is public. When the Justice Department indicted 10 Chinese nationals in March 2025 for hacking on behalf of the Chinese government, the charging documents described the contractor i-Soon billing Chinese intelligence services between $10,000 and $75,000 for each email inbox it successfully compromised, with further payments for analyzing the contents. Leaked internal files from the same company, analyzed by SentinelOne in 2024, show data from a foreign ministry fetching roughly $55,000. i-Soon employed over 100 people and projected revenues near $75 million. Those are the discount rates for soft targets, accounts and networks protected by ordinary commercial security. Hard targets are devices and systems that can only be breached with novel unpublished exploits. The exploit brokers that supply state programs publish their bids: up to $7 million for a full-chain iPhone compromise, $5 million for Android. RAND’s study of zero-day vulnerabilities found a median useful life near seven years, which is the asset an intelligence service burns when an operation is discovered. Above all of it sits a national intelligence budget the Director of National Intelligence discloses only as a top line, $73.4 billion requested for fiscal 2025, with everything below that classified. Set the routes side by side. Ten thousand dollars per inbox is the cheapest documented rate for stealing personal data one target at a time. One hundred dollars buys the registration record of every voter in California. The asymmetry is three to four orders of magnitude in direct cost, and that is before risk is priced at all. Covert collection carries indictment, attribution, sanctions, and the loss of tools that took years to build. A commercial download carries none. The defender’s side of the ratio is worse still. Equifax agreed to a settlement of at least $575 million and potentially $700 million for a breach affecting 147 million people. UnitedHealth Group reported that the Change Healthcare attack would cost roughly $2.87 billion in 2024. A breach of the Office of Personnel Management compromised background investigation files on 21.5 million people, including 5.6 million sets of fingerprints, at a national security cost no settlement figure captures. On the kinetic battlefield, an attacker spends a dollar to force thousands. In the data domain, the attacker spends nothing to force billions, or, when the data is legally public, to force no response at all, because there is nothing to remediate and no one to indict. The Portfolio Is the Tell The declassified catalog of data held by a People’s Republic of China computer network exploitation actor around 2019 reads as my cost-asymmetry framework predicts. Most of its American entries are cheap or free: voter files, breached credentials circulating in criminal dumps, social media account data, the commodity substrate of identity resolution. A small number of entries fall into a different category: F-15 maintenance and technical manuals, and documents from four cleared defense contractors. Technical data tied to items on the United States Munitions List cannot be bought at any price, which is precisely why it was stolen. That split is what a rational collector produces. Commodity data is purchased or scraped because covert action against it would be economically irrational. Export-controlled technical data is stolen because no legal market exists. Expensive, risky tradecraft is reserved for the material money cannot buy. An intelligence service that behaves this way is optimizing, and the results of that optimization are reflected in the price column. This reframes how the July release should be read. The alarming interpretation, that a 2022 download of public records constitutes an election compromise, misprices the event. The economic interpretation is more troubling: the United States has structured its data environment so that the cheapest route to a national targeting file on the American population runs through lawful commerce. The vulnerability is not a firewall. It is a fee schedule. Why the Cheapest Input Buys the Most Influence Cognitive warfare is the effort to shape a population’s perceptions, judgments, and decisions. Congress ordered the Department of War to define it in the 2026 National Defense Authorization Act , a task still unfinished months past its deadline, and this journal has carried a sustained debate over whether the term describes anything new. Set the doctrinal argument aside, and the mechanism is one the advertising industry already built. Gather enough data on a person, model what moves them, and serve a message calibrated to that individual. Advertising technology runs this logic billions of times a day to sell products. A state with the same pool of data does it to sell doubt and division, one citizen at a time, and adversaries are already contesting that space with AI-generated content at scale. The declassified materials indicate that China reasons this way. Beside the voter files sits a plan to exploit American fault lines over race, immigration, and the pandemic response, and to push tailored narratives through social and traditional media. Traditional propaganda involves broadcasting one message to everyone and hoping it lands. A data-driven campaign delivers a different message to each person, measures who responds, and adjusts. The difference is the objective. A retailer wants a purchase. An adversary wants a belief. Here the implications for scale turn the economics from severe to alarming. A broadcast’s reach is capped by its cost. A data-driven influence campaign’s is not, because once the pool of data exists, the marginal cost of one more tailored message approaches zero. China assembled that pool for pennies. The input to one of the most consequential forms of modern influence, the shaping of a democratic population’s decisions, is the cheapest item on the battlefield. Inverting the Curve In the kinetic domain, the fix for a bad exchange ratio is a cheaper defense: a laser shot costing a few dollars against a drone costing tens of thousands. The data domain has an analog, and it is regulatory, not technical. Executive Order 14117 and the Justice Department’s Data Security Program , in force since April 2025, function as an export control on Americans’ bulk sensitive data, restricting transfers to six countries of concern. The economic effect is the point. The rule raises the adversary’s acquisition cost at the cheapest point on the curve, the legal purchase, and pushes collection back toward the covert route, where cost, risk, and attribution all favor the defender. A dollar of acquisition cost imposed at the point of sale buys more security than a dollar of breach response after the loss. From Arithmetic to Action: Five Recommendations Five actions raise the adversary’s cost to acquire the ammunition of cognitive warfare. First, extend and enforce the bulk-data transfer restrictions. Close the reseller and aggregation seams through which restricted categories leak, and fund the enforcement capacity to detect violations, since an unenforced export control prices at zero. Second, reprice public records for bulk machine access. This does not require closing them. Transparency for citizens, journalists, campaigns, and researchers can coexist with fees, identity verification, and rate limits calibrated to make wholesale foreign harvesting expensive and visible. A journalist checking a voter roll and a foreign actor downloading 51 jurisdictions are different acts, and the fee schedule should treat them differently. Third, harden the holders whose data cannot be bought. As the legal route closes, adversary covert spending will concentrate on cleared defense contractors, health systems, and genomic repositories. Security investment should follow that predicted shift rather than trail it. Fourth, extend acquisition-cost logic to minors’ data. Behavioral and biometric profiles built on children age into profiles of cleared analysts and field-grade officers, which makes children’s data the longest-dated asset in an adversary’s portfolio and the least defended. Fifth, measure defense by the adversary’s cost to acquire. Program evaluation across data security, foreign investment review, and privacy enforcement should report the acquisition cost imposed on a hostile collector, because that figure, rather than defender spending, predicts adversary behavior. The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States ( CFIUS ) and Federal Trade Commission children’s-privacy enforcement already generate the underlying data. Deterrence here comes from arithmetic, as it does against drones: make the cost to acquire this data exceed the influence it buys. Raising that cost is not only privacy protection, or even counterintelligence. It denies easy access to the ammunition needed for the fight over what Americans believe. Today the price runs in the opposite direction by orders of magnitude, and the adversary reads the price list as easily as we do. The cheapest weapon in the arsenal is the one aimed between our ears. A Note on Estimates and Sources Voter file figures are drawn from published state fee schedules; the national-assembly range is an inference, not an audited total. Covert collection prices are drawn from the March 2025 Justice Department indictment and from analysis of leaked contractor files. Remediation figures come from Federal Trade Commission settlement documents and Securities and Exchange Commission filings. The Cost Asymmetry Ratio framework is developed in The Cost Curve as Deterrent, with the simulator and data sources on GitHub. Disclaimer: The views expressed are the author’s own. The post Buy, Don’t Steal: The Economics of Cognitive Warfare appeared first on Small Wars Journal by Arizona State University .

content:
中国全国人大常委会第二十五次会议星期五（11月6日）在北京人民大会堂闭幕，全国人大常委会委员长赵乐际主持闭幕会。 （新华社）
中国全国人大常委会会议星期五（11月6日）在北京闭幕，决定终止九名全国人大代表资格，其中四人来自解放军和武警部队，分别是少将张弓、郭建军、吴育红和孟庆斌。
但与往常不同的是，根据全国人大常委会公告，四人均是“辞去”全国人大代表职务，而不是被罢免。
台湾开南大学人文社会学院教授张执中向《联合早报》分析，这与2024年原外长秦刚辞去全国人大代表职务的情况相似。他推测，四名军方少将可能涉及违规，但尚未查到不法，因此通过辞去人大代表职务的方式处理，并可能已被降职、降衔。
按公开资料逐项统计，解放军和武警部队全国人大代表人数已从2023年届初的281人减至229人，减少52人，其中50人代表资格终止，另有两人从军队代表团转入地方代表团。
根据公开信息，张弓曾任北海舰队航空兵参谋长、东海舰队副参谋长，2019年晋升海军少将，后任江西省军区司令员、广东省军区司令员，并于2023年出任广东省委常委。
郭建军曾任甘肃省军区战勤处处长、青海省军区政治部主任及副政委、火箭军工程大学政委，2015年晋升少将，2022年出任宁夏军区政委及自治区党委常委。
吴育红曾以海军少将身份担任2019年国庆阅兵岸舰导弹方队领队之一。
孟庆斌曾任武警内蒙古总队副政委、贵州总队政委、四川总队政委，后转任甘肃省军区政委。2025年6月的公开报道仍显示他担任这一职务。
另有五名代表的资格也被终止，其中四人被罢免，一人辞职。被罢免的四人包括已在任上被查的江西省原省长叶建春、河南省政府原副秘书长兼办公厅主任何雄、湖南中烟工业有限责任公司党组书记兼总经理籍涛，以及四川天府银行董事长黄毅。浙江省原舟山市市长徐仁标则辞去全国人大代表职务。
另外，12人获任全国人大六个专门委员会副主任委员，其中包括多名近期卸任地方领导职务的省部级干部。
他们是上海市原市长龚正、湖南省委原书记沈晓明、西藏自治区党委原书记王君正、安徽省委原书记梁言顺、河南省委原书记刘宁、云南省委原书记王宁、河南省原省长王凯、湖南省原省长毛伟明、安徽省原省长王清宪、云南省原省长王予波、甘肃省原省长任振鹤、河北省原省长王正谱。
会议经表决，任命王君正、王宁为全国人大民族委员会副主任委员，王凯为全国人大监察和司法委员会副主任委员，龚正、毛伟明为全国人大财政经济委员会副主任委员，梁言顺、王予波为全国人大教育科学文化卫生委员会副主任委员，刘宁、任振鹤、王正谱为全国人大农业与农村委员会副主任委员，沈晓明、王清宪为全国人大社会建设委员会副主任委员。
另外，在9月底出任安徽省委书记的李乐成，被免去工业和信息化部部长职务；河北省委书记罗文则经河北省人大常委会补选为全国人大代表，代表资格获全国人大常委会确认。

title: What the US midterms mean for ties with China
zh_title: 美国中期选举对中美关系意味着什么
summary: 分析人士表示，民主党在本周的美国中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，控制了国会，这对最大竞争对手中国来说既是机遇也是挑战。 2026 年 11 月 3 日，在佐治亚州亚特兰大举行的美国中期选举之夜派对上，民主党人、亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 预计将赢得佐治亚州州长竞选，支持者欢呼雀跃。照片：Erik S. Lesser/法新社。投票结果让民主党有能力阻止唐纳德·特朗普总统特立独行的外交政策，投票结果可能会对特朗普产生以下影响：
content:
分析人士表示，民主党在本周的美国中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，控制了国会，这对最大竞争对手中国来说既是机遇也是挑战。 2026 年 11 月 3 日，在佐治亚州亚特兰大举行的美国中期选举之夜派对上，民主党人、亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 预计将赢得佐治亚州州长竞选，支持者欢呼雀跃。照片：Erik S. Lesser/法新社。这次投票的结果让民主党有能力阻止唐纳德·特朗普总统特立独行的外交政策，它可能会如何影响华盛顿和北京之间的棘手关系：关税会受到限制吗？分析人士表示，赢得美国国会参众两院的控制权使民主党能够限制特朗普在其任期结束后的两年内对中国产品随意征收关税。这可能对特朗普来说是一个潜在的打击，在双方达成休战协议（定于一月到期）之前，特朗普在激烈的美中贸易战中一直履行职责。上海复旦大学国际问题研究院院长吴心伯表示，如果民主党限制特朗普，这意味着他“在与中国的谈判中将更难利用关税卡”。 2026 年 5 月 14 日，中国国家主席习近平（右）和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在北京人民大会堂会面。照片：中国外交部发言人毛宁，来自 Facebook。
然而，民主党人还必须权衡他们的行动与特朗普关税在美国企业中的受欢迎程度。新加坡南洋理工大学拉惹勒南国际研究学院高级研究员德鲁·汤普森表示，国会将“在未来两年内利用一切机会阻挠（特朗普的政策）”。但汤普森表示，民主党仍需谨慎对待进一步限制关税，这些关税“受到工会、蓝领工人和小企业的欢迎……他们历来是民主党的基础选民”。华盛顿布鲁金斯学会外交政策研究员帕特里夏·金(Patricia Kim)表示，国会将“不太愿意支持那些会急剧升级对华压力的措施，如果这样做可能会增加美国消费者和企业的成本或增加冲突的可能性”。台湾是“游戏规则改变者”？凯投宏观(Capital Economics)首席经济学家尼尔·希林(Neil Shearing)表示，台湾问题可能会“改变游戏规则”。台湾是美国支持的民主岛屿，北京声称拥有主权。华盛顿是台北最重要的安全支持者，已向台湾出售了价值数十亿美元的武器，台湾将用这些武器抵御中国潜在的攻击。但特朗普今年五月宣称美国对台军售可能成为与中国谈判的筹码，这让美国的立场受到质疑。此后，他的政府将一批价值 140 亿美元的武器推迟了数月。
台湾总统赖清德于 2026 年 2 月 11 日在台北举行的国防预算新闻发布会上发表讲话。照片：台湾总统府。希林在一份报告中写道，中国可以利用特朗普总统任期的剩余两年加大对台湾的压力，特别是如果北京“判断华盛顿心烦意乱，或者特朗普愿意同意不干预的条款”。特朗普最近赞扬了他与中国国家主席习近平的“伟大友谊”，迄今为止，他顶住了民主党人和一些共和党议员的政治压力，

【原文 English Original】
A sweeping victory for Democrats in US midterm elections this week, giving them control of Congress, presents both an opportunity and challenge for top rival China, analysts say. Supporters cheer after the announcement that Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, former mayor of Atlanta, is projected to win the Georgia gubernatorial race during a US midterm election night party in Atlanta, Georgia, on November 3, 2026. Photo: Erik S. Lesser/AFP. Here is how the outcome of the vote, which offers the Democratic Party the power to stymie President Donald Trump’s maverick foreign policy, could impact the thorny relationship between Washington and Beijing: Will tariffs be limited? Winning control of both houses in the US Congress puts Democrats in a position to limit Trump’s liberal use of tariffs on Chinese products in the two years he has left in office, analysts say. That could be a potential blow to Trump, who has wielded duties throughout a frenzied US-China trade war before the two sides reached a truce, set to expire in January. If Democrats limit Trump, that means he “will be less able to leverage a tariff card in negotiations with China”, said Wu Xinbo, dean at the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai. China’s President Xi Jinping (right) and US President Donald Trump at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 14, 2026. Photo: Mao Ning Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson, via Facebook. However, Democrats will also have to weigh their actions against the popularity of Trump’s tariffs among US businesses. Congress will “take every opportunity to thwart (Trump’s policies) over the next two years”, said Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies at Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University. But Democrats will still have to tread carefully on further restricting tariffs that “are popular with unions, blue-collar workers and small businesses… who have historically been a base constituency for the Democrats”, Thompson said. Congress will be “less inclined to support measures that would sharply escalate pressure on China if doing so risks raising costs for American consumers and businesses or increasing the likelihood of conflict”, said Patricia Kim, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington. Taiwan a ‘game changer’? The issue of Taiwan, the US-backed democratic island claimed by Beijing, could be a “game changer”, said Neil Shearing, group chief economist at Capital Economics. Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer and has sold billions of dollars’ worth of arms to Taiwan that the island would use to fend off a potential Chinese attack. But Trump threw the US stance into question in May when he declared that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip in talks with China. His administration has since delayed for months a $14-billion batch of weapons . Taiwan President Lai Ching-te speaks during a press conference on the defence budget in Taipei on February 11, 2026. Photo: Taiwan’s Office of the President. China could use the remaining two years of Trump’s presidency to increase pressure on Taiwan, particularly if Beijing “judges that Washington is distracted or that Trump would be willing to agree terms to not intervene”, Shearing wrote in a note. Trump, who recently hailed his “great friendship” with China’s President Xi Jinping, has so far resisted political pressure from Democrats — and some Republican lawmakers — to greenlight the arms package. But a Democrat-controlled Congress “may force Trump to resume arms sales to Taiwan next year”, Wu said. “If that happens, that will also undermine the stability of US-China relationship.” Alternatively, for China, renewed support of Taipei from the US Congress may be “a stronger incentive for (Beijing) to play it safer with Taiwan”, said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute. Nevertheless, Thompson pointed out, while Congress can pass bills requiring Trump to approve an arms sale, the president retains the power to veto it “or simply ignore it”. Will Beijing treat Trump as a lame duck? From China’s perspective, even though Trump has been politically weakened by the midterms, Beijing is unlikely to change its strategy towards working with him, analysts say. “Beijing is likely to continue cultivating him through high-profile, leader-to-leader engagement with Xi Jinping, viewing this as the least costly way to manage relations with Washington,” said Kim. “Neither Beijing nor Washington appears to expect or seek a fundamental improvement in bilateral relations,” she added. Tsang of the SOAS China Institute said “Trump being relegated to lame-duck status will be used by the Chinese to put more pressure on him”. But, he added, Beijing is “calculating” and “would not want to push too hard and trigger Trump behaving totally irresponsibly”.

title: Selling F-35s to Saudi Arabia and Turkey is a Historic Opportunity
zh_title: 向沙特阿拉伯和土耳其出售F-35是一个历史性机遇
source: Small Wars Journal by Arizona State Univ
summary: 摘要：国务院刚刚批准向沙特阿拉伯出售 F-35，国会有 30 天的时间提出反对。我的文章认为，现在是达成有条件协议的最佳时机：政府应该推动沙特和土耳其加入《亚伯拉罕协议》、支持乌克兰以及保护国际航运。由于F-35的竞争对手即将出现，这是美国获得优惠条件的最佳机会。这篇文章讨论了之前推迟这些销售的主要反对意见，即与俄罗斯/中国的关系以及对以色列的威胁。特朗普政府
content:
摘要：国务院刚刚批准向沙特阿拉伯出售 F-35，国会有 30 天的时间提出反对。我的文章认为，现在是达成有条件协议的最佳时机：政府应该推动沙特和土耳其加入《亚伯拉罕协议》、支持乌克兰以及保护国际航运。由于F-35的竞争对手即将出现，这是美国获得优惠条件的最佳机会。这篇文章讨论了之前推迟这些销售的主要反对意见，即与俄罗斯/中国的关系以及对以色列的威胁。特朗普政府已批准沙特阿拉伯购买F-35隐形战斗机，土耳其希望效仿。三个因素强调了这些协议的紧迫性，而国会尚未最终确定这些协议。首先，利雅得和安卡拉处于独特的地位，可以帮助总统应对一些持续的外交政策挑战。其次，延误可能会让这些国家考虑其他国家即将推出的飞机。第三，之前阻碍这些交易的问题已经有了解决方案，包括对与中国和俄罗斯关系的担忧，以及维护以色列的军事态势。潜在的让步 与前几届政府相比，沙特和土耳其可以向华盛顿提供的东西要多得多。可以说，F-35 最重要的补偿将是加入《亚伯拉罕协议》，这将巩固以色列与最有影响力的逊尼派穆斯林领导人的正常化。
除了加强以色列的安全之外，这还将标志着特朗普希望留下的“和平缔造者”遗产中的一个里程碑。 同样，政府一再试图达成结束乌克兰战争的协议。尽管特朗普对普京和泽伦斯基的赞扬前后不一致，但他对基辅面临俄罗斯弹道导弹袭击表示特别同情，这促使他允许乌克兰制造的爱国者拦截弹。土耳其有机会解决总统尽管仍感到沮丧但很可能无法自行解决的问题。乌克兰迫切需要反弹道导弹防御系统，但美国却严重短缺，而特朗普似乎认为与莫斯科对抗会干扰谈判。如果安卡拉向乌克兰提供俄罗斯制造的拦截机（乌克兰在出售 F-35 时已经需要移除这些拦截机），这将提供华盛顿希望看到但不会提供的救济。土耳其可以通过接受特朗普的美国能源报价而不是从俄罗斯购买能源来赢得更多善意。这可能包括建设核反应堆，总统也在与利雅得共同推动这一项目。最后，政府欢迎更多地利用土耳其和沙特军队来保护商业航运。索马里海盗的回归和也门胡塞武装都威胁着通过苏伊士运河的船只。与此同时，伊朗针对正在进行的战争发动的袭击导致霍尔木兹海峡的交通量大幅减少。
采取行动的动力 到目前为止，政治后果使沙特和土耳其无法合作。两国都希望避免与以色列以及其次是阿联酋结盟。他们还缺乏政治资本来开展代价高昂且结局不明的军事行动。此外，这些国家不愿意完全断绝与中国和俄罗斯的关系，因为中国和俄罗斯提供了灵活性作为美国的替代方案。要促使利雅得和安卡拉忽视这些担忧，需要华盛顿做出让步。

【原文 English Original】
Abstract: The State Department just approved an F-35 sale to Saudi Arabia, leaving Congress 30 days to object. My piece argues that this is the right moment to secure conditional deals: the administration should push for Saudi and Turkish accession to the Abraham Accords, support for Ukraine, and protection of international shipping. With competitors to the F-35 on the horizon, this is the best opportunity for the US to receive favorable terms. The article addresses the major objections that have delayed these sales before, namely ties to Russia/China and threats to Israel. The Trump Administration has approved Saudi Arabia’s purchase of F-35 stealth fighters, and Turkey hopes to follow. Three factors stress the urgency of these deals, which Congress is yet to finalize. First, Riyadh and Ankara are uniquely positioned to help the president with several ongoing foreign policy challenges. Second, delays could allow these countries to consider upcoming aircraft from other nations. Third, there are solutions for issues that prevented these deals before, including concerns over ties to China and Russia, and preserving Israel’s military posture. Potential Concessions The Saudis and Turks have considerably more to offer Washington than they could under previous administrations. Arguably the most significant compensation for F-35s would be joining the Abraham Accords , which would solidify Israel’s normalization with the most influential Sunni Muslim leaders. Beyond strengthening Israeli security, this would mark a monumental milestone in the “peacemaker” legacy that Trump hopes to leave behind. In a similar vein, the administration has repeatedly attempted to reach a deal to end the Ukraine War. While his praise for both Putin and Zelenskyy is inconsistent, Trump notably voiced sympathy for Kyiv facing an onslaught of Russian ballistic missiles, which tempted him to allow Ukrainian-built Patriot interceptors . Turkey has a chance to address an issue that the president, despite remaining frustrated, likely won’t solve himself. Ukraine urgently needs anti-ballistic missile defense , but the US has a critical shortage , and Trump seemingly believes that antagonizing Moscow interferes with negotiations. If Ankara gives Ukraine its Russian-made interceptors, which it already needs to remove for an F-35 sale, it will provide relief that Washington hopes to see but won’t deliver. Turkey could earn more goodwill by accepting Trump’s offers for American energy instead of buying from Russia. This could include the construction of nuclear reactors, which the president is also pursuing with Riyadh . Lastly, the administration would welcome greater use of the Turkish and Saudi militaries to protect commercial shipping. The return of pirates in Somalia and the Houthis in Yemen both threaten ships passing through the Suez Canal. Simultaneously, Iranian attacks in response to the ongoing war have heavily reduced traffic from the Strait of Hormuz. Incentives to Act So far, political consequences have kept the Saudis and Turks from cooperating. Both countries want to avoid perceived alignment with Israel and, secondarily, the UAE. They also lack the political capital for costly military operations with no discernable end . Additionally, these nations would prefer not to fully sever their ties with China and Russia, who offer flexibility as alternatives to the US. Motivating Riyadh and Ankara to overlook these concerns will require a concession from Washington. For decades, trading weapons has largely defined the US’ relationships with these countries. Beyond their direct role in war, international arms deals are political tools. Here, equipment matters more as a bargaining chip. This gives two options for negotiating: selling equipment as a carrot, or withholding it as a stick. The Biden administration tried the stick by freezing Saudi Arabia’s weapons in 2021, seeking to improve humanitarian conditions in Yemen. Outraged, Riyadh responded by cutting oil production to raise gas prices, signing a multi-billion dollar arms deal with Russia , and continuing to bomb and blockade Yemen at the same intensity for another full year . This leaves the carrot, which has also been tested: the Saudis made it legal for women to drive in the year following an arms sale that was, at the time, the largest in history. Turkey has followed the same trend. After the US refused to sell Patriot air defense , Turkey paid billions for Russian alternatives . Selling Ankara $23 billion worth of F-16s compelled Turkey to stop blocking Sweden from entering NATO. This pattern demonstrates that when Washington sells, the Saudis and Turks cooperate; when it withholds, they shop elsewhere to the West’s detriment. Because no one sells true substitutes for F-35s, the US has more leverage, but this won’t last forever. Competitors to the F-35 are underway from South Korea and Turkey , two of the fastest rising arms exporters . With Saudi Arabia’s stated interest in both of these aircraft , the Saudi and Turkish need for F-35s is temporary. Riyadh and Ankara will eventually get stealth fighters, either on the US’ terms or someone else’s. Trump can make a deal that achieves his goals, or wait until someone else takes advantage of the Saudi and Turkish demand. In doing so, Trump must account for why these deals have garnered controversy in the first place: Data Security F-35 sales are most often blocked by the risk of technical information reaching the wrong hands. This is why many viewed Saudi Arabia’s ties with China as a nonstarter. However, the Saudis have been careful to keep their engagement with Beijing from burning bridges. For example, Riyadh allowed the CIA to oversee a purchase of Chinese missiles, and Saudi Arabia’s trade with China typically follows the US turning down preferred deals. Also, cutting off Riyadh has not prevented Beijing from stealing information about the F-35 , including physical samples of secret materials . Any outstanding data security risks make the arms sale a stronger bargaining chip by signaling greater trust in the Saudis. Turkey’s situation is similar. Erdoğan has undermined Moscow in Ukraine, Syria, Libya, and Sudan , but infamously turned to Putin after failed attempts to buy Western missiles. The Kremlin might extract data about nearby aircraft from Turkey’s Russian-made S-400 air defenses. This risk drove Congress to legally block F-35 deliveries until Ankara removed the missiles. With difficulty, Turkey is looking for a buyer . If it sells S-400s to a country Russia opposes, Ankara loses the natural gas and partially-built nuclear reactor that Moscow provides. If it sells to a country the US opposes, Ankara alienates the partner it’s aiming to please. Few Western-friendly countries are eager to purchase Russian equipment. So far, proposed deals in the Gulf have stalled, as have efforts to return the missiles to Russia, and Turkey’s new alliance with Pakistan rules out selling to India. Ankara might destroy its S-400s if a deal isn’t salvaged, but the most reliable signal of trustworthiness would be giving them to Ukraine against Putin’s demands. Russia would make this sting for Turkey, but Western compensation can mitigate this: Trump wants to sell American energy , and the pronounced vulnerability of Ukrainian skies would attract European funding for the missiles. Israeli Security The other objection is Israel’s security, which skeptics argue these deals would threaten. These concerns overlook how the US is approaching the end of its monopoly on trusted, exportable stealth fighters. While these deals seemingly violate the policy to maintain Israel’s Qualitative Military Edge (QME) , the US can prolong Jerusalem’s advantage by also selling the upcoming F-47 . Barring F-35 sales will only briefly preserve the Israeli QME, so the chance for concessions should be seized. If those concessions include the Abraham Accords, selling F-35s would improve Israel’s security. Further, the Turkish-Saudi alliance will likely restrain Turkish-Israeli escalation: if Ankara abandons diplomacy, it either drags Riyadh toward an unwanted war or fractures the alliance. Act Quickly The US has considerable misalignment with Saudi Arabia and Turkey on human rights and strategic interests, which explains years of reluctance to sell F-35s. However, both countries have already shown that holding back weapons can push them toward alternative sellers, and continued delays carry other risks. These stealth fighters will soon have serious competition, which will curb what the US can demand in exchange. The US must secure these deals quickly. Beyond the nonnegotiable removal of Turkey’s S-400s, the President should push for more than cash: both buyers should accept strategically preferred policies, such as joining the Abraham Accords, supporting Ukraine, buying American energy, and protecting international shipping. A true dealmaker-in-chief would not let this opportunity go to waste. The post Selling F-35s to Saudi Arabia and Turkey is a Historic Opportunity appeared first on Small Wars Journal by Arizona State University .

content:
发言人办公室对古巴政权的对外军事支持和非法收入网络的进一步制裁 - 情况说明书 情况说明书 2026 年 11 月 5 日 今天，美国国务院指定了 8 个实体和 2 名个人，并将 5 艘船只确定为封锁财产，以进一步推动特朗普政府全面推动结束古巴政权在古巴和整个半球的恶意活动。这一行动包括与古巴政权的石油运输网络、古巴精英、国有进口和技术支持实体以及该政权军队的中国供应商相关的目标。今天制裁的所有国务院目标都是根据第 14404 号行政命令 (E.O.) 指定的，该命令授权对符合与古巴镇压以及对美国国家安全和外交政策的其他威胁有关的特定标准的外国人实施制裁。此外，今天，财政部外国资产控制办公室 (OFAC) 主任根据 E.O. 发布了一项决定。第 14404 号法令授权对任何在古巴经济的制造、技术、电子和海洋部门经营或曾经经营的外国人实施制裁。这些新部门的确定针对的是该政权及其支持者，而不是古巴人民。
美国继续授权人道主义贸易，包括食品、药品和医疗设备，并支持信息向古巴人民自由流动。 古巴政权的非法收入网络 古巴的统治精英囤积岛上的能源和航运资源以图谋取私利，使古巴人民面临停电、燃料短缺和经济停滞的困境。为了维持该系统的运行，该政权依赖离岸中介机构网络。今天，美国国务院正在指定为古巴政权运送原油和石油产品的广泛航运网络的一部分。 GUILLERMO FAUSTINO RODRIGUEZ LOPEZ CALLEJA (GUILLERMO) 是往返古巴运输石油产品的广泛海运公司网络的一部分。 GUILLERMO 是根据第 2 节指定的。 E.O. 2(a)(i)(A) 14404 从事或曾经从事古巴经济能源部门的工作。 CAROIL TRANSPORT MARINE LTD (CAROIL) 是一家总部位于塞浦路斯的公司，管理着悬挂古巴国旗的原油油轮，这些油轮在古巴运输能源产品。财政部此前根据 E.O. 于 2019 年 9 月 24 日指定 CAROIL。 13850. CAROIL 根据第 13850 条被指定。 E.O. 2(a)(i)(A) 14404 从事或曾经从事古巴经济能源部门的工作。以下船舶被确定为 CAROIL 拥有权益的财产： ESPERANZA (IMO: 9289166)：CAROIL 是商业管理者。
财政部此前于 2019 年 12 月 3 日将 ESPERANZA 确定为 CAROIL 的冻结财产。 GLORIA C（IMO：9540273）：CAROIL 是商业经理。 TENTACOOL COMMERCIAL INC 是注册所有者。 MARIA CRISTINA（IMO：9502453）：CAROIL 是商业经理和注册所有者。财政部此前于 2019 年 9 月 24 日将 MARIA CRISTINA 确定为 CAROIL 的封锁财产。TENTACOOL COMMERCIAL INC (TENTACOOL) 是一家总部位于巴拿马的公司，也是 GLORIA C 的注册所有者。 E.O. 2(a)(i)(A) 14404 从事或曾经从事古巴经济能源部门的工作。国际会议

【原文 English Original】
Office of the Spokesman Further Sanctions on the Cuban Regime’s Foreign Military Support and Illicit Revenue Networks – Fact Sheet Fact Sheet November 5, 2026 Today, the Department of State is designating eight entities and two individuals, and identifying five vessels as blocked property, to further the Trump Administration’s comprehensive push to end the Cuban regime’s malign activities, both in Cuba and across our hemisphere.  This action includes targets associated with the Cuban regime’s oil shipping networks, Cuban elites, state-owned import and technical-support entities, and China-based suppliers of the regime’s military forces.    All Department of State targets sanctioned today have been designated pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14404, which authorizes sanctions on foreign persons determined to meet specified criteria related to repression in Cuba and other threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy.  Additionally, today the Director of the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a determination pursuant to E.O. 14404 that authorizes sanctions against any foreign person operating or having operated in the manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine sectors of the Cuban economy.  The identification of these new sectors targets the regime and those who enable it, not the Cuban people.  The United States continues to authorize humanitarian trade, including food, medicine, and medical devices, and supports the free flow of information to the Cuban people. Cuban Regime’s Illicit Revenue Networks Cuba’s ruling elite hoards the island’s energy and shipping resources for its own enrichment, leaving the Cuban people to contend with blackouts, fuel shortages, and a stagnant economy. To keep this system running, the regime relies on a web of offshore intermediaries. Today, the Department of State is designating part of an extensive shipping network moving crude oil and petroleum products for the Cuban regime. GUILLERMO FAUSTINO RODRIGUEZ LOPEZ CALLEJA (GUILLERMO) is part of an extensive network of maritime shipping companies moving petroleum products to and from Cuba. GUILLERMO is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy. CAROIL TRANSPORT MARINE LTD (CAROIL) , a Cyprus-based company that manages Cuban-flagged crude oil tankers that have transported energy products in Cuba. Treasury previously designated CAROIL on September 24, 2019, pursuant to E.O. 13850. CAROIL is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy. The following vessels are being identified as property in which CAROIL has an interest: ESPERANZA (IMO: 9289166): CAROIL is the commercial manager. Treasury previously identified ESPERANZA as blocked property of CAROIL on December 3, 2019. GLORIA C (IMO: 9540273): CAROIL is the commercial manager. TENTACOOL COMMERCIAL INC, is the registered owner. MARIA CRISTINA (IMO: 9502453): CAROIL is the commercial manager and registered owner. Treasury previously identified MARIA CRISTINA as blocked property of CAROIL on September 24, 2019. TENTACOOL COMMERCIAL INC (TENTACOOL) , a Panama-based company and the registered owner of the GLORIA C. TENTACOOL is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy. INTERNACIONAL MARITIMA SA , a Cuba-based company and the registered owner of the ESPERANZA. INTERNACIONAL MARITIMA SA is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy. PETROLEOS MARITIMOS DEL CARIBE S.A. (PETROMARCA) , a Cuba-based company and the ship manager and operator of two Cuban-flagged petroleum product tankers. PETROMARCA is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy. The following vessels are being identified as property in which PETROMARCA has an interest: EMILIA (IMO: 9242209): PETROMARCA is the commercial manager and registered owner. LOURDES (IMO: 9259692): PETROMARCA is the commercial manager. Cuban Elites Regime insiders and their family members continue to profit from the Cuban regime’s control of the island’s economy, including through opaque networks tied to Grupo De Administracion Empresarial S.A. (GAESA), the Cuban military’s business conglomerate. Today, the Department of State is designating the daughter of the previously designated GAESA President. ANY RODRIGUEZ LASTRES (LASTRES) , the daughter of the sanctioned GAESA President Ania Guillermina Lastres Morera. LASTRES is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(I) of E.O. 14404 for being an adult family member of ANIA GUILLERMINA LASTRES MORERA, a person whose property and interests in property are blocked pursuant to this order. LASTRES also previously served as the Commercial Director of U.S.-designated Terminal De Contenedores De Mariel S.A. State-Owned Entities of the Cuban Regime The Cuban regime relies on a web of state-owned enterprises that control the island’s technology resources and direct revenue to the state rather than to the Cuban people. Today, the Department of State is designating the following two Cuban state-owned entities pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(B) of E.O. 14404 for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, the Government of Cuba. EMPRESA IMPORTADORA Y EXPORTADORA DE PRODUCTOS DE LA ELECTRONICA Y LAS COMUNICACIONES (CUBAELECTRONICA) , a Cuban state-owned importer of supplies and equipment for Cuba’s electronics industry. EMPRESA COMERCIALIZADORA DE SERVICIOS TECNICOS Y TECNOLOGICOS (TECNOSIME) , a Cuban state-owned entity that conducts commercial, labor, and promotional activities that generate revenue for the Cuban state. Chinese Companies’ Support to the Cuban Military As the Department’s July 20 report Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism noted, the Cuban regime’s continuing partnerships with China and Russia have supplied Cuba with military hardware, surveillance technologies, and other security capabilities. Today, the Department of State is taking aim at Cuba’s foreign backers by designating two China-based corporations that have supplied the Cuban regime with components and equipment to sustain the Cuban military. The transfer of this equipment involved the Cuban company Sociedad Mercantil Duna S.A., which was designated by the Department of State on August 6, 2026 , and has been involved in the import of military-related equipment from China and Russia to Cuba. The following entities are being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(D) of E.O. 14404 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, the Government of Cuba. CHINA NATIONAL ELECTRONIC IMPORT AND EXPORT COMPANY (CEIEC) , a China-based state-owned enterprise that exports defense electronics, security systems, and construction engineering services. Additionally, CEIEC contracted with the Cuban arms procurement entity Sociedad Mercantil Duna S.A. to export components intended for military equipment used by the Cuban Ministry of Revolutionary Armed Forces (MINFAR) in 2026. CEIEC was previously designated by the Department of the Treasury pursuant to E.O. 13692 on November 30, 2020 , in relation to its support for the Maduro regime’s efforts to restrict internet service and conduct digital surveillance and cyber operations against political opponents. BEIJING H&C TECHNOLOGIES CO., LTD , a China-based subsidiary of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation (CETC) International Co., Ltd. (CETCI) that sells surveillance and security equipment. Additionally, BEIJING H&C TECHNOLOGIES CO., LTD worked with the Cuban arms procurement entity Sociedad Mercantil Duna S.A. to export military equipment to Cuba in 2026. Sanctions Implications As a result of today’s sanctions actions, and in accordance with E.O. 14404 of May 1, 2026, “Imposing Sanctions on Those Responsible for Repression in Cuba and for Threats to U.S. National Security and Foreign Policy,” all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC. Additionally, all entities that are owned individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. All transactions and dealings by U.S. persons or persons within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC or exempt. These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. Foreign persons that engage in transactions with persons designated pursuant to E.O. 14404—or that operate or have operated in the electronics, energy, defense and related materiel, manufacturing, marine, metals and mining, financial services, security, or technology sector of the Cuban economy, as identified in and determined pursuant to E.O. 14404—are themselves at risk of sanctions.  Non-U.S. persons, including foreign financial institutions, should proceed with caution in any dealings with a party sanctioned under this authority. Actions to return assets to a sanctioned party or transfer them to another jurisdiction for potential use by the target expose non-U.S. persons to significant sanctions risk. All property and interests in property of persons that are blocked pursuant to the Cuban Assets Control Regulations (CACR) continue to be blocked.  The CACR prohibits persons subject to U.S. jurisdiction from dealing in property in which Cuba or a Cuban national has an interest, unless authorized or exempt.  The power and integrity of U.S. government sanctions derive not only from the U.S. government’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.    Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be routed through OFAC’s Reconsiderations Portal . Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page.

content:
被监禁的香港民主活动人士黄之锋周四在承认串通外国势力罪后被判处 10 年监禁，这是他根据北京实施的国家安全法第二次被定罪。黄之锋.资料图片：HKFP。另请参阅：黄之锋在 30 多岁时寻求宽大处理，以获释，缓刑信显示 HKFP 收集了本地和国际反应。
当地反应：行政长官黄李家是“破坏香港繁荣稳定的罪魁祸首之一……黄志峰屡次触犯法律，包括组织、参与、煽动他人参加未经批准的集会、非法集会、藐视法庭等，表现出对法律的彻底漠视。”中国外交部发言人郭家琨表示，中国中央政府坚定支持香港特别行政区维护国家安全，依法惩治危害国家安全的行为。香港立法会发言人表示：“这个判刑充分体现了法治和正义，体现了根据香港国安法，任何企图危害国家安全的人都必然会依法受到严惩……针对黄志峰的证据确凿，他选择认罪……”对于国家和香港特区来说，他一定要抓住机会，学会如何尊重法律，正确认识自己的国家。”保安局局长邓克里斯表示：“那些对我们发动袭击的人，与黄、罗勾结的外部势力一模一样……他们必须受到强烈谴责，香港也应该受到谴责。”
推动社会变革的年轻人是任何充满活力的社会的财富，但香港政府却将他们关进监狱。”国际特赦组织副区域主任萨拉·布鲁克斯（Sarah Brooks）表示：“今天的判决再次严峻地提醒我们，香港的国家安全法如何成为惩罚异议的工具，而不是惩罚异见人士的工具。”

【原文 English Original】
Jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment on Thursday after pleading guilty to conspiring to collude with foreign forces, his second conviction under a Beijing-imposed national security law. Joshua Wong. File photo: HKFP. See also: Joshua Wong sought leniency to be freed in his 30s, mitigation letter reveals HKFP rounds up local and international reactions. Local reactions: Chief Executive John Lee Wong was “among the primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong’s prosperity and stability… Wong Chi-fung has repeatedly broken the law, including organising, taking part in, and inciting others to take part in unauthorised assemblies, unlawful assemblies, and contempt of court, demonstrating his utter disregard for the law.” Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun “The central government of China firmly supports the Hong Kong SAR in safeguarding national security and punishing in accordance with the law acts that endanger national security.” Spokesperson for the Hong Kong Legislative Council “The sentence fully demonstrates the rule of law and justice, reflecting that under the Hong Kong National Security Law, anyone attempting to endanger national security will inevitably be severely punished in accordance with the law… [T]he evidence against Wong Chi-fung was conclusive and he chose to plead guilty…” Chief Superintendent of Police National Security Department Steve Li “I sincerely hope that for the rest of his time in prison, apart from reflecting on the wrongdoings he has done to the country and to the Hong Kong SAR, he must seize the opportunity to learn how to respect the law and properly understand his own country.” Secretary for Security Chris Tang “Those launching attacks against us are exactly the same external forces that Wong and Law attempted to collude… They must be strongly condemned, and Hong Kong citizens must recognise and acknowledge that clearly.” International reactions: European Union External Action Press Team: “The EU urges Chinese and the Hong Kong authorities to respect international legal commitments under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration and maintain space for political pluralism in line with the ‘one country, two systems’ principle.” Spokesperson for the UK Foreign Office “We call for an immediate end to all unjust prosecutions of individuals charged under the National Security Law and urge the authorities in China and Hong Kong to honour the rights and freedoms guaranteed to the people of Hong Kong under the Sino-British joint declaration (1984).” Spokesperson for the US Consulate “Wong has been unjustly imprisoned since December 2020, demonstrating that Beijing will go to extraordinary lengths to silence those who advocate for fundamental freedoms in Hong Kong.” Taiwan Presidential Office Spokesperson Karen Kuo “Seeking democracy should not be a crime, and young people should not have to sacrifice their freedom for their ideals.” NGOs Asia Director at Human Rights Watch Elaine Pearson “The harsh sentence on baseless charges against Joshua Wong is cruel and unjust. Young people promoting social change are an asset for any vibrant society, but the Hong Kong government puts them behind bars.” Deputy Regional Director for Amnesty International Sarah Brooks “Today’s sentence is another grim reminder of how Hong Kong’s National Security Law has become a tool to punish dissent rather than to genuinely protect national security… [it] cruelly – and perhaps deliberately – comes mere months before he would have been eligible for release under his previous conviction.”
